#1937. 20 Most Beautiful Wives and Girlfriends (WAGs) in World Soccer Ranked

Correspondent AUTHORITY Football journalist with experience at Reach PLC and PA Media; University of Central Lancashire graduate. FOCUS Fan-engagement content and match analysis across the Premier League and Championship. THE INSIGHT Oliver utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified reporting and fan-first content. He provides the human stories behind the results to ensure fans get the full picture as it happens.

From red-carpet galas to World Cup stands, the wives and girlfriends of soccer’s biggest icons command nearly as much global attention as the superstars on the pitch.

Originally coined by the British press during the 2006 World Cup, the term "WAG" has evolved into a worldwide pop-culture phenomenon—defined by power couples, luxury fashion, and massive social media empires.

Today, the partners of the game's biggest stars are household names in their own right, blending chart-topping careers, modeling contracts, and business ventures with life alongside football royalty.

Football Insider has ranked the 20 most beautiful and iconic wives and girlfriends in world soccer—spanning both current stars and retired legends—based on global star power, glamour, and cultural impact.

Scroll down to see who claims the number one spot, and let us know in the comments who we ranked too low.

Brazilian supermodel Goulart began dating German goalkeeper Trapp in 2015, with the pair getting engaged in July 2018. She is best known for her work as a Victoria's Secret Angel from 2005 to 2008, and for walking in the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show from 2005 through 2016. She has also modelled for leading designers and luxury brands, including Armani, Chanel and Valentino, while appearing on numerous covers of major fashion magazines.

Renowned for her athletic physique and natural elegance, 42-year-old Goulart is widely regarded as one of the most beautiful women in the modelling industry. She boasts over four million followers on Instagram.

Ivanovic is a star in her own right, after spending over a decade as one of the leading women's tennis players from 2003 to her retirement in 2016. She reached the number one spot for 12 weeks in 2008 and won an impressive 15 singles career titles, including the 2008 French Open.

The Serbian began a relationship with former Bayern Munich and Man United star Schweinsteiger in 2014, and they married in Venice in 2016. The pair had three children in the next seven years but decided to end their marriage in 2025.

Johansen is one of the biggest names of the latest era of WAGs, owing to the meteoric rise to stardom of her partner, Haaland, over the last decade. She was a soccer player who came through the youth ranks of his boyhood club, Bryne FK, and the pair knew each other from childhood before beginning a relationship in 2021.

The couple have kept details of their relationship remarkably private, considering his fame, but 22-year-old Johansen has amassed a huge Instagram following of over two million followers and is now considered a celebrity in their home country of Norway. She has adorned the cover of numerous high-profile national magazines, and the couple have one son together.

Hertfordshire native Benson is another relatively new face of WAG culture, becoming one of the standout figures of this era thanks to her striking looks and impeccable style. She drew national attention in 2024 after being photographed in the stands watching England star partner Saka at that summer's Euros.

She has built a career of her own, working in media planning and communications after studying Public Relations and Media at Birmingham City University. She reportedly met the Arsenal winger in 2020, and the couple announced their engagement in November 2025 to huge fanfare online. Adoring followers are waiting with bated breath for details and photos of whenever they do tie the knot soon.

Rubio has enjoyed a substantial career in Spanish entertainment independent of her relationship with Real Madrid legend Ramos. She appeared on numerous comedy programmes in their home country in the 1990s and 2000s, then started to present game shows and appear in movies as her profile grew outside of Spain.

Rubio was named Spain's sexiest woman by FHM magazine in both 2008 and 2009, and began dating Ramos in 2012. They are now known as one of the most iconic couples in soccer history, as they have since married and share four sons. Rubio is still active as a TV presenter and boasts a whopping 10.6m followers on Instagram.

Nara and Icardi's story is one that has dominated news headlines far and wide for many years. It is perhaps the most publicised soccer romance of the last decade. The Argentine television personality is widely known for her glamorous appearance and confident personality, but the relationship has made her a globally known star.

She was initially married to Icardi's Sampdoria teammate and friend, Maxi Lopez, but they separated in late 2013 and by May 2014 Nara was controversially married to the Argentine international. The players' games against each other were subsequently known as the 'Wanda Derby'. They were then involved in a major scandal in 2021, as Nara accused Icardi of being unfaithful, and despite several reconciliation attempts and children involved, they were officially divorced in October 2026.

Carbonero is one of Spain's most recognisable media personalities, admired for her effortless elegance and long-standing body of journalistic work. She rose to prominence covering football for La Sexta and Telecinco in the noughties and first met legendary goalkeeper Casillas while they were both working at the 2009 Confederations Cup.

Their relationship became known across the globe due to a surprise embrace live on air at the 2010 World Cup after Spain's victory in the final while she interviewed her partner. The couple wed in 2016 and built a family, but separated in 2021.

Vinicius' status as a global superstar in soccer has been flanked by his on-off relationship with Fonseca over the last 18 months, which has unsurprisingly kept them both in the headlines for both good and bad reasons. The USA-born influencer moved to Brazil as a child and became immensely famous for her YouTube channel and previous relationships with notable media and music personalities before meeting the Madrid forward in 2025.

She attended his 25th birthday in July as they grew closer, and the pair confirmed a relationship later that year. They split in May 2026 as Fonseca alluded to their differences online, but reconciled two months later before separating again in October. She remains one of Brazil’s most influential internet personalities, keeping her huge 57m Instagram following updated with snapshots into the glamorous life she is currently leading without Vinicius by her side.

Bellingham is one of the biggest stars in soccer right now, and his enormous commercial appeal has inevitably led to intrigue around his personal life. He has been romantically linked to American model Castro since 2024 after they reportedly matched on celebrity dating app Raya.

The California-born personality is actually six years older than her English superstar boyfriend, and became known before their relationship for her budding modelling career and appearances in music videos for globally known artists like Drake and DJ Khaled. She is regularly spotted at his games for club and country and has developed a sizeable social media following as a result of their romance.

Sabatini is another who can count herself as a celebrity in her own right without Argentine international husband Dybala to boost her profile. She hails from a family of actors and sportspeople, and was a child actor who won awards for her work on nationally acclaimed TV show Aliados.

She opened live shows for the likes of Ariana Grande and Coldplay after turning her attention to music in 2017, and met Dybala at a concert of the former. The pair married in 2024 and have since started a family. Sabatini boasts over 68m streams as a music artist on Spotify.

Stunning blonde Ward always seemed destined for fame in some measure, after her mother, Dawn, became a multi-millionaire through interior design and her father, Ashley, had his own soccer career in the Premier League. Dawn shot to fame on The Real Housewives of Cheshire in 2015 and Taylor appeared on the show while building her own profile as a model and fashion influencer online.

She met Algerian star Mahrez through a mutual friend in 2020, and they quickly became a real power couple as English media lapped up the idea of two very different worlds colliding through fame. They appeared together on Amazon Prime’s 2024 documentary series Married to the Game, and are now married and have children.

Pinnock is a very clear example of a modern-day WAG who is actually much more famous than her soccer-playing partner. The striking chart-topping pop star is one of Britain’s most recognisable celebrities after forming one quarter of the hugely successful girl group Little Mix between 2010 and 2021. The X Factor-formed collective sold more than 50m records worldwide and boasted five UK number one singles.

She met former Burnley and Watford striker Gray while holidaying in Marbella in 2016, as they soon got together and were eventually married in Jamaica in 2023. Pinnock is currently pursuing a solo music career and is branching out into the world of TV and fashion.

Pinnock’s former bandmate and close friend Edwards has also found herself in the WAG world for a similar length of time. The cheeky Geordie shared the highs of Little Mix’s extraordinary success after initially applying to The X Factor as a solo contestant.

Edwards met Celtic midfielder Oxlade-Chamberlain on Raya in 2016, and they made their first public appearance at the 2017 BRIT Awards to massive excitement and media attention. They were engaged in 2022 and welcomed two children before tying the knot after almost 10 years together in June 2026. With Little Mix on an indefinite hiatus, her debut solo album ‘Perrie’ reached number three in the UK charts in September 2025.

The idea of a soccer WAG first became a prominent part of British culture and the wider celebrity world during the 2006 World Cup in Germany. English international star Rooney had been with his future wife, Coleen, for a decade, and she was arguably the most important figure in the early era of the WAG in soccer, becoming one of the most recognisable faces among Three Lions’ players’ partners at the tournament.

She was launched to stardom alongside him as a teenager in the early noughties, with tabloids watching their every move and the Liverpool native developing her own career through high-profile endorsements and TV appearances. She is still as big a name as ever, despite his retirement, and has retained a down-to-earth image that many can relate to, especially after the huge 2019 ‘Wagatha Christie’ scandal.

Clancy is widely known for her slender figure and glamorous looks which have seen her dominate the WAG world for decades on end. She finished as runner-up on Britain’s Next Top Model in 2006 and was instantly propelled into an international career in the industry that saw her adorn the covers of numerous iconic fashion magazines and amass huge wealth in her own right.

The former Strictly Come Dancing winner met England hero Crouch in 2006 shortly after he had signed for Liverpool, as they began dating, were engaged in 2009 and wed in 2011. She has continued to keep up national celebrity status with appearances on red carpets galore, high-profile modelling contracts and increased TV appearances. She is also renowned for her down-to-earth persona and sense of humour, a popular match for the man who popularised the 'Robot' dance during his cult-hero playing days.

Neymar is a modern-day Brazilian icon who has dominated social media and the wider sporting zeitgeist of the last 15 years, and so his romance with Biancardi has also attracted major interest across the globe. She was a known Instagram and YouTube influencer before their relationship, but was catapulted to worldwide fame when they went public online in 2022.

Their turbulent partnership has been closely scrutinised since then, with allegations of infidelity and subsequent reunions in abundance, which have all been played out in front of a widespread online audience. Biancardi now has more than 15m followers on Instagram and shares three children with the Selecao soccer star.

Shakira needs little introduction as a global superstar and a phenomenon of Latin pop music who is among the world’s best-selling artists of all time. She is credited with popularising Spanish-language music across the globe and has carved out her own path as a soccer icon with her 2010 World Cup anthem ‘Waka Waka’ and 2026 official song ‘Dai Dai.’

Her romance with ex-Barcelona and Spain defender Pique was one of the most high-profile in sports history, and actually began at the 2010 tournament. They became a prominent celebrity couple who were followed everywhere by paparazzi, and even shared two children, but made particular headlines after a bitter 2022 split that later saw the Colombian star aim a diss track at her ex-partner.

Another global superstar music artist makes the top three of our list, with ‘Posh Spice’ Beckham still known as the benchmark against which WAG style is measured. They were the original soccer celebrity couple who transcended the sport after building hugely successful and high profile respective careers in their own domains.

Victoria has evolved from cultural pop icon to one of the biggest fashion designers on the planet in the 21st century, with the pair still by each other’s side to this day after first dating in 1997 (albeit while surviving a dose or two of scandal along the way). She is also a mother of four who remains heavily involved with several of the biggest fashion labels in the world, and boasts a massive online presence to boot. The original but, on our list, not quite the best.

Roccuzzo and Messi share a love story that has stood the test of time. Being the childhood sweetheart of the greatest soccer player ever can’t have always been easy, but the sweet Rosario native has stuck by his side and tried to remain as out of the public eye as possible throughout his decorated career. She moved to Barcelona to be with him in 2010, and they wed in 2017.

Her public profile is low-key but active, as she cares for their three children and keeps her 42m Instagram followers regularly updated with a glimpse into the lifestyle of one of the most famous sporting families ever. Roccuzzo also utilises her following to front commercial campaigns for global companies like Adidas, DoorDash and Anastasia Beverley Hills.

The world’s biggest sports star needs a strong partner by his side, and Ronaldo has had Spanish glamour model Rodriguez on his arm for over 10 years now. She has embraced global stardom and built a successful career on top of her relationship to become an icon of modern celebrity culture as an individual.

Rodriguez boasts the most Instagram followers of any WAG on this list by some margin, at over 77m, regularly works with top fashion brands and is often seen at the biggest events in fashion, film and television. She was the subject of Netflix docuseries ‘I Am Georgina’ between 2022 and 2024, and remains a figure of constant fascination, with swathes of adoring fans hanging on her every move.

#1936. CM: Three names on the list as Milan begin difficult hunt for Modric’s heir

AC Milan must start thinking about the midfield of the future, and there are reportedly a few names on the list of ideas.

At 41 years of age Luka Modric, still remains simply irreplaceable for Ruben Amorim and for Milan. However, given that his deal expires at the end of the season, the Rossoneri management have a duty to also look to the future and prepare for the post-Modric era.

The scouting team are very active in England, Spain, Belgium, and France, looking for the right players for Amorim’s footballing philosophy. Among the priorities for next season is identifying the right player to potentially take the reins as a deeper-lying playmaker.

Calciomercato.com report that three players have attracted considerable interest from Milan. One of them is Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, but he remains a dream at the moment because Arsenal and Chelsea have already swooped in on him.

The 23-year-old was called up to the England squad for the last break because manager Thomas Tuchel is very keen on him, but there’s a significant obstacle: the price tag. In England, there is even talk of a €100m+ asking price, given the clubs interested.

The spotlight has recently turned on Brighton’s Yasin Ayari too. He’s a highly versatile midfielder, performing at a high level both as a defensive midfielder and behind the striker. The Swede’s deal runs out in 2027 making him a big opportunity, but Brighton have a one-year option to.

Finally, we arrive at the new name on the list: Adem Zorgane of Union-Saint Gilloise. Scouts like what they have seen from the Algerian, who combines physicality with good technical ability. He would likely be the cheapest of the three, but his potential is high in the eyes of Milan.

#1935. ‘Looking back…’ – Alexander Isak speaks out over penalty controversy in defeat to Arsenal

Alexander Isak has spoken out about the controversial penalty incident in which he was involved during Liverpool’s defeat to Arsenal a fortnight ago.

Five minutes after Kai Havertz netted the only goal of the match, the Reds’ number 9 had his shirt pulled by Jurrien Timber inside the box, but neither on-field referee Andy Madley nor Stuart Attwell on VAR deemed it to have been a foul.

The transgression was unmistakably clear on replays, and the Premier League’s Key Match Incidents panel has since acknowledged that a spot kick should’ve been awarded.

Speaking to reporters whilst on international duty with Sweden, Isak was asked if he felt that he should’ve had a penalty.

He replied (Aftonbladet, via Liverpool Echo): “Yeah, looking back I suppose it does look that way, but when you’re in the moment, you don’t always perceive exactly what’s happening.

“I could feel myself being pulled a bit, but not to the extent that it appears later on. I was focused on scoring. It’s hard to try to score and then fall down at the same time. I was so locked in on the goal that I didn’t really register it.”

On whether he should’ve gone to ground to try and sway the referee, Isak said: “I don’t think there’s any need to embellish or go down on purpose. Sure, if I’d had a better read on the situation, I might have made sure the referee noticed it, that’s about all you can do, but I don’t believe you need to dive or exaggerate in situations like this.

“Perhaps it shouldn’t even matter that much, given that we have VAR and systems in place to make the decisive calls in these kinds of moments.”

Isak is absolutely right in saying that a penalty should’ve been awarded, and that he shouldn’t have to act unnaturally to convince the referee to give the decision in his team’s favour.

Andoni Iraola remarked after the game that a spot kick probably would’ve been given if the Liverpool striker had gone to ground, but the onus isn’t on players to sway the officials – it’s on the latter to get these big calls right, especially with recourse to VAR.

It feels as though the debate about officiating in the Premier League will continue indefinitely, with no discernible sign of an improvement in standards from Pro Ref figurehead Howard Webb.

It’s to Isak’s great credit that he’s given such a calm and measured verdict on the penalty incident when he and his team were so blatantly wronged. He’d have had every right to complain profusely about what happened; we’d suspect that many other players would’ve done so if they were in that situation.

He certainly hasn’t let it bother him in terms of his contributions on the pitch, with the 27-year-old scoring in Liverpool’s subsequent games against Fenerbahce and Crystal Palace to take his tally for the season to eight goals in 14 matches across all competitions.

That is, in fact, the best response to the injustice which was done against him Anfield two weeks ago.

#1934. 20 Richest Soccer Players of All Time Ranked by Net Worth

Correspondent AUTHORITY Football journalist with experience at Reach PLC and PA Media; University of Central Lancashire graduate. FOCUS Fan-engagement content and match analysis across the Premier League and Championship. THE INSIGHT Oliver utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified reporting and fan-first content. He provides the human stories behind the results to ensure fans get the full picture as it happens.

Massive salaries, lifetime shoe deals, and global business empires have turned soccer’s biggest icons into some of the wealthiest athletes on earth.

Today, iconic figures like David Beckham earn hundreds of millions off the pitch through club ownership, fashion ventures, and brand partnerships that even dwarf their mega on-pitch earnings.

From record-breaking contracts in Saudi Arabia and Major League Soccer to royal family fortunes like Faiq Bolkiah’s, the financial scale of modern soccer is staggering.

Football Insider has ranked the 20 richest soccer players of all time by estimated net worth, combining career wages, endorsement deals, and post-playing investments.

Scroll down to see who tops the rich list, and let us know in the comments which fortune surprises you most. There are some huge shocks that nobody would have expected.

Pep Guardiola has reshaped modern soccer more profoundly than any other figure of his generation, turning his tactical blueprint into global celebrity and a £100m ($132.3m) fortune. While the Spaniard enjoyed a decorated playing career with Barcelona and Spain, the vast majority of his wealth has been built from the touchline through record-breaking managerial contracts at Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Manchester City.

The Spaniard was believed to be earning around £35m ($46.3m) annually, with bonuses included, during his final years in charge of Man City. He owns high-value property in England and his home country, and has partnered with the likes of Puma, Nissan and Visa to bolster his whopping fortune over the years.

Ultra-passionate Atletico Madrid manager Simeone is widely regarded as the highest-paid in his profession right now, owing to how desperate the La Liga club are to hold onto his services for as long as humanly possible. Some reports estimate that he takes home around £26m ($34.4m) each year as they aim to break the dominance of Barcelona and Real Madrid.

He also earned a decent wage in a successful 19-year playing career, but has accumulated such a high net worth through management and an extensive property portfolio of over 180 apartments in Madrid that he oversees with his wife. Simeone became an ambassador for both Betinia and CampoBet in 2026 too.

Salah has utilised his amazing soccer career to amass huge wealth through lucrative contracts and a whole host of sponsorship deals. The Egyptian superstar became Liverpool’s highest-paid player ever in 2022, with a reported annual salary of £20m ($26.5m) in basic wages.

He has worked closely with major brands like Adidas, Pepsi, Vodafone and Uber, with estimates putting his endorsement income alone at around £15m per year ($19.8m) at its peak. Trabzonspor are paying the Premier League great around £15m ($19.8m) annually after he joined on a free transfer in the summer of 2026. His wider business interests are focused on real estate investment and commercial holding companies.

The first unusual name on this list comes in the form of ex-Chelsea and AC Milan striker Pato. He had a good career but failed to reach the lofty heights many expected of him, yet has turned that pain into power to become a hugely successful investor after his retirement. He did earn huge contracts at Milan and in a two-year stint in China, but his wealth mainly comes from off-field endeavours.

He has ventured into the world of gastronomy, with a chain of burger restaurants in Brasilia, while also putting his money into CoverGirl cosmetics, his own vodka brand and numerous properties in his home country. Pato is clearly looking to further his wealth in the future, after joining a consortium who completed a takeover of English club Northampton Town in 2026.

2026 Ballon d’Or winner Kane is not only loving life on the pitch with Bayern Munich and England, but he is also a supremely wealthy man off it, with a bank balance that stands head and shoulders above the rest of his international teammates. The Three Lions captain reportedly earns around £25m ($33.1m) each year before tax at Bayern Munich.

He boasts a high-profile commercial partnership with footwear brand Skechers, after signing a lifetime global deal in 2023 that earns him up to an estimated £7.5m ($9.9m) annually. Kane also regularly works with major brands like Allianz, Oura and Reflo.

The exceptional soccer career of Welsh superstar Bale translated into immense wealth, as he raked in over £500,000 per week ($661,625-a-week) in basic wages during the peak of his powers at Real Madrid. Commercial deals followed in abundance as he shone at the top of the game, with huge partnerships signed with Adidas, BMW, Lucozade and EA Sports.

Bale has dipped his toes into several different investment pathways since retiring, with a stake in a TGL golf franchise, co-ownership of a Cardiff-based bar and ties to Penderyn Whisky. His biggest step has undoubtedly been helping launch a sports investment fund worth over £500m ($661.6m), and Bale has also publicly admitted that he would like to co-own a soccer club in the near future.

Even soccer players on the level of Ronaldo were not paid close to the astronomical figures that relatively average players earn nowadays back in his time with some of the world’s biggest sides. He was one of the sport’s first truly global marketing superstars, though, signing a lifetime deal with Nike in 1994 and being one of the faces of their brand to this day.

Ronaldo boasts an endless list of partnerships with top brands that have all contributed to his huge fortune, with notable links to Santander, Betfair and Snickers. He actually had a bigger net worth in previous years, but failed investments at Spanish club Real Vallodolid and Brazilian side Cruzeiro have seen him fall down this list.

Mercurial genius Ibrahimovic has been able to transform his enigmatic persona as a player into a successful post-retirement career that has swelled his bank balance to new heights. He is one of the most recognisable soccer players of all time, and that is reflected in how unashamedly centred his commercial campaigns are on him.

After earning big money across his career with the likes of AC Milan, PSG, Barcelona and Man United, as well as being exceptionally well-paid by MLS standards at LA Galaxy, he has only continued to further his celebrity status through partnerships with Nike, Oakley Meta and XTB.

If you were waiting for the first mention of Saudi Arabian money impacting this list, then here it is. The oil-rich kingdom has enticed many of the world’s top names to the Middle East in the last five years with the promise of massive riches, and Benzema was no different. He joined Al Ittihad in 2023 and Al Hilal in 2026, with his latter contract reportedly worth over £1.6m each week ($2.1m) in basic wages.

Such incredible mega-deals came after a 14-year stay at Real Madrid that had already made him wealthy beyond comprehension. The 2022 Ballon d’Or winner maintained a long-standing relationship with Adidas until the contract expired when he was without a club in September 2026, while his effortless aura has also seen him link up with luxury brands like Fendi, Jean Paul Gaultier and Assaf.

Now a name that may only be familiar to British soccer fans, with Whelan being best known for his ownership of EFL side Wigan Athletic between 1995 and 2015. The Bradford native had a modest playing career but built his fortune after retirement by developing Whelan’s Discount Stores from the ground up and selling it on, then moving into sports retail with JJB Sports.

JJB grew exponentially in the UK as one of the market leaders for sportswear and equipment, and was valued at over £1bn ($1.32bn) at its peak in 2009. He then sold shares for a combined £240m ($317m) and effectively repeated the trick with DW Sports Fitness, all while pumping his money into Wigan to help them become 2013 FA Cup champions.

Rooney was consistently one of the highest-paid players in the world during his playing career. The Man United and England legend earned £300,000 per week ($396,975 per week) with his biggest contract extension in 2014, while he was one of the faces of Nike and synonymous with EA Sports’ FIFA franchise, appearing on seven consecutive covers between 2006 and 2012.

His status as one of the Premier League’s greatest ever players has seen the endless list of commercial opportunities continue post-retirement, with managerial deals, punditry contracts with the BBC and Sky, and his lucrative image-rights company keeping him afloat near the top of this list.

Mbappe has reached incredible heights over the last 10 years and is a global phenomenon who consistently ranks among the best scorers and players every season. Real Madrid pay him a reported £12.5m ($16.5m) in basic salary each year, while a £125m ($165.4m) signing-on bonus has been spread across his five-year deal. The French forward is not even in the prime of his career and has amassed a huge financial portfolio that rivals legends of the sport.

His commercial powerhouse has been accentuated by a massive Nike contract that ran for 20 years until its 2026 expiration, while major brands like Dior, Hublot and Oakley have all looked for a slice of the Mbappe pie with commercial endorsements in recent years.

You can be forgiven for potentially forgetting about the intricacies of Braithwaite’s soccer career, even though he has featured for the likes of Barcelona and Denmark. The Gremio forward’s huge fortune comes from a 2017 investment into American property developers NYCE Companies.

NYCE’s huge portfolio has expanded across the States in the last decade, with reports stating that they own and let out over 1,500 properties in several major cities. It was believed to have more than £270m ($357.3m) in assets in a 2026 report. Braithwaite has expanded his empire by investing into restaurants in Barcelona and Brazil, as well as establishing his own French fashion label.

Neymar still holds the world-record transfer fee from his eye-watering £200m ($263m) switch from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain in 2017. Paris is where the Brazilian superstar transformed from a generational prodigy into a commercial juggernaut, pocketing roughly £30m ($39m) a year in base wages before injury-hit spells and an eventual homecoming to boyhood club Santos.

His 2023 switch to Al Hilal saw utterly insane reported annual figures of £129m paid to the Selecao star as Saudi clubs looked to dislodge the European heavyweight leagues. He also reportedly signed a £23m yearly deal with Puma in 2020 after leaving Nike, while remaining in a lucrative partnership with Red Bull to this day.

David Beckham turned a lethal right foot and matinee-idol looks into the original athlete-as-a-global-brand blueprint. After winning everything on the pitch with Manchester United and Real Madrid, the Londoner became the ultimate pitchman—selling everything from underwear and fragrances to watches and whiskey for decades after hanging up his boots.

His shrewdest financial move came in 2007 when he signed for LA Galaxy, negotiating an expansion franchise option that allowed him to co-found Inter Miami for a fraction of its modern valuation. Combined with his Authentic Brands Group partnership and his Studio 99 production house, Brand Beckham has proven far more lucrative than his playing days ever were.

Being widely regarded as the greatest soccer player of all time still isn’t enough to crack the top four on this list—though Lionel Messi is hardly checking behind the sofa for spare change. Across legendary spells at Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain, and Inter Miami, the Argentine icon has cleared over £900m ($1.19bn) in career pre-tax playing earnings while securing a lucrative MLS equity pathway modeled on David Beckham’s playbook.

Off the pitch, Messi brings in a reported £56m ($74.1m) a year in 2026 through blockbuster partnerships with Adidas, Apple, Pepsi, and Konami. Eight Ballon d’Or trophies may not outrank royal oil money or biochemical startups here, but his commercial pull across the Americas remains unmatched.

In a fair world, spending 23 years at the summit of world soccer, becoming the sport’s first active billionaire, and collecting roughly $300m a year at Al Nassr would guarantee first place. Instead, Cristiano Ronaldo has to settle for fourth—making him easily the wealthiest player on this list who actually earned his fortune purely by kicking a ball.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner became the first athlete to clear $2bn in career pre-tax earnings, boosted by a reported 15 percent equity stake in Al Nassr, a $1bn lifetime Nike contract signed in 2016, and his sprawling CR7 hotel and lifestyle empire. With more than 660 million Instagram followers, even a single sponsored post earns him more than most European pros make in a season.

During his playing days at Manchester United and Everton, Louis Saha was best known for clinical finishing and a frustratingly fragile hamstring. Since hanging up his boots, however, the former France striker has pulled off one of the greatest post-retirement glow-ups in sports history, building a tech fortune reportedly stretching into the multi-billions.

In 2014, Saha co-founded AxisStars, a private digital network that connects professional athletes and entertainers directly with vetted commercial partners and business ventures. Alongside savvy investments in AI and blockchain, Saha still pops up on television punditry panels—though at this point, he is clearly doing it for the love of the game rather than the appearance fee.

Arsenal fans remember Mathieu Flamini as a combative midfield enforcer famous for flying into two-footed tackles and cutting the sleeves off his matchday shirt. Few at the Emirates realized he was quietly building a green-energy empire between training sessions.

While studying law and still playing for the Gunners in 2013, Flamini co-founded GF Biochemicals, the first company to mass-produce levulinic acid as a sustainable alternative to petroleum. With estimates valuing his stake at up to £10bn ($13bn), the Frenchman is a regular fixture at global climate summits—and has refused to rule out buying a major soccer club of his own.

Faiq Bolkiah tops this list by £5bn ($6.6bn), proving once and for all that having the right uncle beats winning the Ballon d’Or. Born in Los Angeles, the winger spent time in the youth academies of Southampton, Chelsea, and Leicester City before playing senior club football in Portugal and Thailand—a modest resume that contrasts wildly with his status as soccer’s richest man.

Bolkiah is a member of the Brunei royal family and the nephew of Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, whose oil-and-gas fortune underpins an estimated £15bn ($19.85bn) family net worth. To his credit, Faiq has repeatedly played down his royal background so managers judge him on his football rather than his family vault.

Kevin De Bruyne is likelier to move to the MLS or the Saudi Pro League than return to the Premier League, sources have told Football Insider.

The 35-year-old has been linked with a move to Everton in recent days, with his contract at Napoli set to expire at the end of the season.

The Italian side have an option to extend it by an additional year but are yet to exercise the option, with the Belgian's future still uncertain.

As I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, De Bruyne is unlikely to make the move to Everton if he does decide to leave.

The legendary midfielder left Manchester City in 2025, having won the Premier League six times and recorded nearly 300 direct goal involvements in an extremely successful 10 years.

De Bruyne struggled with injuries in his debut campaign with Napoli but looks to have returned to his best this season, scoring four goals and providing two assists in his first 15 appearances.

For the likes of Everton and the queue of other clubs who would dream of signing him, it is De Bruyne's wages which would be a sticking point in contract negotiations.

The midfielder reportedly took a pay cut to join Napoli, but he is still on a highly lucrative contract in Italy.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "If De Bruyne was to leave Napoli any time soon, it's maybe more likely that he would go to a different league.

"Maybe the MLS could be something that would be of interest to him, and I would imagine there would be a lot of Saudi Pro League clubs who would love the opportunity to sign the Belgium international as well.

"So as things stand right now, I would say any move back to the Premier League is probably unlikely for De Bruyne."

While De Bruyne's move to Napoli appears to have been fuelled by his competitive spirit, he has previously admitted to being open to a move to the Saudi Pro League.

Speaking in 2024, he said: "At my age you have to be open to everything. You're talking about incredible amounts of money in what may be the end of my career.

"Sometimes you have to think about that. If I play there for two years, I will be able to earn an incredible amount of money. Before that I had to play football for 15 years. I may not even reach that amount yet.

"Then you have to think about what that could mean next. But at the moment I haven't had to think about that yet."

Luca Netz will be eyeing a Nottingham Forest revival, with a possible chance emerging following injury fears over Neco Williams.

The Forest defender was withdrawn early against Norway, with the Welshman seen limping heavily.

Williams has been a consistent and key performer for Forest, featuring in all 10 Premier League games, and only failing to play 90 minutes once across those.

Oliver Glasner will be sweating on the defender's fitness ahead of the return of domestic football.

Elsewhere in the squad, Netz has been rarely used by Glasner, and truthfully, since he arrived in the 2026 winter window.

But Netz may have to come into the side, as Williams' impressive display against Norway came to an end early.

Nottingham Forest will be hoping Williams is OK, but his heavy limping was not a great sign against Norway.

Williams, despite being 2-0 down to Norway, was having quite a good game against the Scandinavians.

The Nottingham Forest ace completed 91 per cent of his passing, and defensively had seven contributions as per FotMob.

These were made up of four tackles, two interceptions and one clearance, while he also managed to routinely come out on top in his duels.

He won 71 per cent of his ground duels (five out of seven) across his 72-minute performance.

Netz ended the season in the 73rd percentile for expected assists per 90, and with more game time, perhaps he could have more influence.

Additionally, Netz' 0.11 xA per 90 is not too dissimilar to Williams' 0.12 from this season.

#1931. 20 Best Soccer Players of the 2010s Ranked

Correspondent AUTHORITY Football journalist with experience at Reach PLC and PA Media; University of Central Lancashire graduate. FOCUS Fan-engagement content and match analysis across the Premier League and Championship. THE INSIGHT Oliver utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified reporting and fan-first content. He provides the human stories behind the results to ensure fans get the full picture as it happens.

The 2010s delivered one of the greatest golden eras in soccer history, defined by unforgettable Champions League nights and World Cup drama.

At the center of it all stood Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, pushing each other to historic Ballon d’Or totals while dominating El Clásico for Barcelona and Real Madrid.

Alongside them, endless stars produced peak performances that captivated fans from Europe to the United States.

Football Insider has ranked the 20 best soccer players of the 2010s strictly on their output, trophies, and individual brilliance between 2010 and 2019.

Scroll down to see who makes our top five, and let us know in the comments who we left off the list.

Benzema sneaks into the top 20 but cannot go any higher because he actually reached the peak of his powers in this current decade, when he won the 2022 Ballon d'Or. The French striker was the ultimate foil in one of the most iconic forward lines in soccer history throughout the 2010s, and had huge pedigree to boot.

He was key to Madrid winning an unprecedented four Champions League titles between 2014 and 2018, was named in the La Liga Team of the Season twice and scored over 200 goals for the club in the alloted timeframe. He did lack international pedigree, though, after spending five years away from Le Bleus from 2015 onwards.

Ibrahimovic's career started in 1999, but he arguably dominated the 2010s more than any other decade while playing for four different clubs in as many countries. The charismatic ponytailed forward recovered from a tough period at Barcelona to further his reputation as one of the great players of his generation.

He scored over 20 goals in every full season during the decade and won five league titles across spells at AC Milan and PSG. The Swede dominated everywhere he went, even with Man United, and also had time to become one of the most individually decorated MLS players ever in a successful stint at LA Galaxy, but international glory always eluded him.

Marcelo may not be that highly ranked, but he can take pride in being the only left-back to make this list. That is simply because he consistently outperformed his peers every year, and did it while playing for one of the most successful club teams of all time. The eccentric Brazilian was a cornerstone in Madrid's aforementioned superteam.

He truly established himself as one of the best in his position of all time in this decade, winning heaps of club and personal honours and eventually making both the IFFHS and France Football Team of the Decades.

Ribery may not be revered worldwide as one of the all-time greatest, but he was certainly a force to be reckoned with in the 2010s as he maintained a consistently high level rarely matched by other wingers of the era. He utilised every bit of his pace and trickery to help Bayern dominate.

The French forward enjoyed a superb peak, as he made the final three-man shortlist for the 2013 Ballon d'Or following a season in which he helped fire them to Champions League glory and was the top assister in the Bundesliga. He wound down towards the end of the decade but was a true great in his prime for the German giants and a key man at international level.

Right-back Alves, much like his compatriot and rival Marcelo, became a standout in his own position as Barcelona ran riot in Spain and the rest of Europe for much of the 2010s.

He was the first choice in the position for Barca between 2010 and 2016, and with Brazil until 2019, becoming one of the most decorated players in soccer history with over 30 trophies won throughout the decade. He also tasted success as a mainstay for Juventus and PSG, proving that he could also dominate in other countries.

Kroos also formed part of a dominant Madrid side and became known as one of the greatest soccer midfielders ever in this era. He was calmness personified and had an unbelievable eye for a pass which made him a mainstay at the Santiago Bernabeu.

He helped Germany win the World Cup in 2014 as the tournament's top assister, while also lifting countless league and continental trophies at Bayern Munich and then Madrid, making a switch to Spain after winning on the world stage. Kroos will always be remembered as a midfielder who helped define the decade after others had moved past their peak.

The first player to primarily feature in the Premier League to make this list, Aguero was one of the faces of English football for so many years as Man City began to dominate and overtake the traditional top four sides. His 2011 signing truly kickstarted their glory era, particularly as he went on to score the most iconic goal in the league's history to win their first title since 1968.

Aguero won countless trophies in his time at the Etihad, both team and personal, scoring over 220 goals for the club before 2020 came around. The only thing stopping him coming any higher on this list was injuries, as his impact was somewhat restricted by recurring absences at City.

Hazard was an unplayable genius of a winger who could win matches all by himself when on song. He became a Premier League great at Chelsea and scored countless key goals in their pursuit of success throughout the decade.

He started the 2010s firing Lille to an unprecedented Ligue 1 title, then lifted plenty of silverware in a seven-year Stamford Bridge stint that saw him rip defences apart and also shine internationally in Belgium's Golden Generation. Hazard made the Premier League Team of the Year in four different seasons and was later named in the Blues' All-Time XI.

Robben was another who shone at Bayern throughout the 2010s, offering different qualities to left-wing teammate Ribery and arguably outshining him through key moments and better consistency. He was absolutely deadly when cutting onto his strong foot from the right flank and even made the bald head an iconic part of his look.

The Dutch star registered over 120 goals and over 90 assists for Bayern in the decade, scoring the winning goal in their 2013 Champions League success. He was a main player for the Netherlands as they just fell short in the 2010 and 2014 World Cups.

Neuer was not only the best goalkeeper of his generation, but he will also go down as one of the greatest to play between the sticks in soccer history. He redefined what it meant to be a keeper in the decade, pioneering the sweeper role and maintaining outstanding consistency for club and country.

The 2014 World Cup winner also lifted two Champions Leagues in the 2010s as captain of Bayern, becoming the only goalkeeper ever to achieve two European trebles. He made the IFFHS World Team of the Decade and firmly established himself as an all-time great.

Bale was an international superstar at his peak, figuring regularly at the highest level for the biggest and most dominant club in the world during the previous decade. He had a knack of scoring in the biggest moments and his overhead kick in the 2018 Champions League final may be the most iconic strike in the history of the competition.

He powered Wales to an unprecedented semi-final berth at the 2016 European Championships and was key to Los Blancos' huge successes alongside a plethora of greats. Those achievements came after he was arguably the best player in the Premier League between 2010 and 2013 at Tottenham.

Lewandowski became one of the greatest pure goalscorers in the history of soccer in this decade. His elite finishing, exceptional anticipation and underrated physicality combined to make him a serious force and certainly one of the finest strikers in this century so far.

Only three players scored more than him in Europe’s top five leagues in the 2010s, and the Polish superstar also matured into his country’s greatest ever player by some distance in the same timeframe. He helped Borussia Dortmund rise again and then dominated alongside others on this list at Bayern, winning countless honours and making IFFHS’ World Team of the Decade.

Neymar’s amazing natural ability saw him become one of the world’s greatest and most famous athletes in the previous decade. He was maybe the closest of anyone to becoming a consistent top-two player in the world at the time, and also remains the most expensive player ever after joining PSG for £200m in 2017.

Selecao soccer royalty in his own right, even though the World Cup eluded him despite his outstanding career, he formed part of what many believe is the best front three of all time at Barcelona and came third in the Ballon d’or voting twice. He arguably peaked too soon in the middle of the 2010s, and has failed to reach such heights in this decade.

Xavi oozed class and elegance throughout his playing days, building on an already excellent career in the 2010s as Barca went from strength to strength with their star-studded side. He was the constant in that team, undeterred by the competition and part of one of the best midfield threes ever known.

He may not rank as high as expected because his career at the top level effectively ended in 2015, but the Spaniard was key to 2010 World Cup success and barely put a foot wrong in those five years to help the Catalan machine keep going full steam ahead. Xavi finished third in Ballon d’Or voting in 2010 and 2011.

Ramos was another star of that iconic Real Madrid side, and he established himself as one of the greatest centre-backs in soccer history during this era. The Sevilla academy product matured into an absolute warrior at the back who led his team into battle with undying passion and determination, as well as fantastic quality in every facet of his game.

He was named in the UEFA Team of the Season in all four of their Champions League-winning campaigns, while also popping up with huge goals and displaying impressive offensive abilities on a regular basis. Ramos not only impressed for his club, he was also a regular in Spain’s 2010 World Cup and 2012 Euro-winning tournaments too.

Now comes the man who scored that memorable winner in the 2010 World Cup final. Iniesta’s effortless class made him the perfect partner for Xavi, as he mostly took on a more attacking role for club and country, creating chances at will with a deft touch and unbelievable close control.

He was named as the Euro 2012 Player of the Tournament, and La Liga’s Best Midfielder for four years in a row between 2011 and 2014. Iniesta ranks above his former midfield teammate on moments alone, and because he remained a regular for the Camp Nou side until 2018. Sir Alex Ferguson famously confessed that he felt Iniesta was the main “danger” of the iconic Barcelona side of the early 2010s, rather than Lionel Messi.

Few forwards in modern soccer have terrorized defenders quite like Luis Suarez at the height of his powers. After joining Liverpool in 2011, "El Pistolero" capped his Anfield spell with one of the greatest individual seasons in Premier League history in 2013/14—scoring an astonishing 31 goals in just 33 league appearances without taking a single penalty. That breathtaking campaign nearly carried Liverpool to a long-awaited title, sweeping England’s Player of the Year awards and earning him a share of the European Golden Shoe. Controversy was never too far away as his will to win too often crossed the line, but his technical skill and ability to wriggle away from defences in tight spaces was thrilling to watch.

Suarez reached another stratosphere after moving to Barcelona in 2014, forming the iconic "MSN" trident alongside Lionel Messi and Neymar. He fired Barca to a historic treble in his debut season before exploding for 40 La Liga goals in 2015/16 to outscore both Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo for a second European Golden Shoe, cementing his spot as the deadliest pure striker of the decade.

Modric’s peak was higher than any player below him on this list during the 2010s, and this is why he slots surefootedly into the top three. The silky Croatian could change a game within seconds and had everything a midfielder needed to dominate opponents at the highest level throughout his prime. He became the best player ever from his country during this decade.

That is because he was the one to upset the established order, being crowned the first Ballon d’Or winner not called Messi or Ronaldo since 2007 after an outstanding 2018 that saw Croatia reach the World Cup final, as he picked up the Golden Ball, and Madrid lift a third successive Champions League crown. His victory was hugely significant as it ended an era of dominance - and cemented the unassuming midfield kingpin as an all-time great.

Ronaldo shaped the 2010s as a global superstar both on and off the pitch, as the decade transformed him from a newly-established great of his time to one of the most revered sportspeople to ever walk the earth. His unmistakable charm and aura, coupled with extraordinary athleticism and consistency in front of goal, all combined to see him challenge for the biggest prizes every season and year without fail.

He won four Ballon d’Or awards, four Champions League titles and helped fire Portugal to Euro success in 2016. CR7 also adapted to his strengths and went from being a tricky winger to a devastatingly prolific centre-forward by 2019. He broke club and competition records galore in a decade of relentless brilliance as one half of an iconic rivalry that will never be seen again.

No player has ever dominated a single decade of soccer quite like Lionel Messi did during the 2010s. Operating at his absolute peak for Barcelona, the Argentine magician turned the impossible into a weekly routine—shattering Gerd Müller’s single-year scoring record with an astonishing 91 goals in 2012 and finishing the decade with 522 club goals in just 521 appearances.

His numbers between 2010 and 2019 border on video-game fiction, leading Europe’s top five leagues in both goals and assists while powering Barcelona to seven La Liga titles, two Champions League crowns, and the 2015 continental treble. Messi claimed five Ballon d’Or trophies across the decade (2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, and 2019) to reach six overall, cementing his place at the top of the era—and sparking the fiercest GOAT debate in sports.

#1929. 30 Greatest Soccer Forwards of All Time Ranked

Correspondent AUTHORITY Football journalist with experience at Reach PLC and PA Media; University of Central Lancashire graduate. FOCUS Fan-engagement content and match analysis across the Premier League and Championship. THE INSIGHT Oliver utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified reporting and fan-first content. He provides the human stories behind the results to ensure fans get the full picture as it happens.

Goals win trophies, and the greatest forwards in soccer history have defined every era of the sport.

From Pele’s three World Cup triumphs and Diego Maradona’s brilliance to Ronaldo Nazario’s explosive prime, attacking icons have consistently captured global imagination.

In the modern era, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo shattered every scoring record imaginable, taking their rivalry from European nights to Inter Miami and Saudi Arabia.

Football Insider has ranked the 30 greatest soccer forwards of all time—covering center-forwards, wide forwards, and second strikers—judged on peak dominance, silverware, goalscoring output, and lasting legacy.

Scroll down to see who claims the number one spot, and let us know in the comments who we ranked too low.

Kicking this list off is an enigmatic genius of a striker who had it all. Ibrahimovic was consistently dominant in the air, had outstanding technique and could score from anywhere on the pitch. He is one of the most recognisable soccer players ever, with his long ponytailed locks providing an iconic silhouette to a decorated career.

He cannot be any higher on this list because of a lack of success at international level and in the Champions League, but the Swedish superstar featured for several of the world’s biggest clubs and scored over 570 career goals across four consecutive decades. He even took his talents to LA in 2018 and became one of the best MLS players of all time.

One of the few active players in this list, and the youngest by a margin, Haaland has rewritten the rules of goalscoring in the Premier League and is well on track to being an all-time great of the sport. He utilises immense power and pace and otherworldly movement in the penalty area to score at an unbelievable rate every season, and is one of the biggest names in sport in this century. His recent World Cup exploits propelled him to being the fifth-most followed player ever on Instagram as it stands.

Haaland boasts a number of the biggest honours in the game and has already earned endless achievements despite likely only being halfway through his playing career. His record-breaking career is showing no signs of slowing down, and he may well end his playing days in the top 10 of this list.

The reigning Ballon d’Or winner has set the benchmark for being a complete striker over the last decade of soccer. He is England’s greatest ever player, when impact and statistics are considered, and the best part is that he was never even meant to be this good. Kane deserves his plaudits for putting in the work to dominate across numerous competitions, with clinical finishing and pinpoint passing being key parts of his repertoire.

He may be nearing the end of his career, but is arguably better than ever before and could see his stock rise even further with more trophies added to his cabinet. He is the only Englishman to score over 500 official senior career goals and the fastest player in Bundesliga history to reach 100 strikes.

Moving away from traditional number nines, Figo is the first winger to be included on the list. He had incredible speed and vision and remains one of the most controversial figures in the sport for his world-record move from Barcelona to Real Madrid in 2000. That switch is still remembered as one of the craziest events in soccer, and he was also a leading figure in Portugal’s Golden Generation.

Figo won the Ballon d’Or in 2000 and FIFA World Player of the Year in 2001, while also picking up several big domestic and European honours in his time in Spain and at Inter Milan. He was not particularly a prolific scorer, but did utilise amazing creativity to record 276 assists in 919 career appearances.

Salah has been one of the defining players of his generation following an unprecedentedly amazing career at Liverpool. He has broken the mould for African players in the sport, becoming a trailblazer for those from his continent in the 21st century by combining electric speed and trickery with outstanding finishing ability and movement.

The Egyptian star is the greatest African player to ever grace the sport, with countless trophies and exceptional longevity at the top level firing him to the top above other strong candidates. He remains a world-renowned name in soccer and boasts incredible records and achievements in the Premier League and Champions League.

No, this list is not only full of players who have featured in the 21st century. Kopa was one of the first household names in soccer as he scored prolifically across Europe in the 1950s and 1960s. His influence on the game as we know it is still prevalent today, with the ‘Kopa Trophy’ awarded to the best-performing under-21 player each year being named after him because he was such a fantastic player and because he won the 1958 Ballon d’Or.

The versatile French forward was also known for his outstanding dribbling and playmaking abilities, as he became the focal point of a Real Madrid side that won three successive European Cups between 1956 and 1959.

Regarded by many as the best Premier League player ever, and potentially the greatest in English soccer of all time, Henry comes in ahead of Salah due to the sheer rate at which he contributed to goals and the outstanding aesthetics that he carried throughout a decorated career. The Frenchman had style, grace and an unmatched aura that could only be summed up by his own “va-va-voom” catchphrase, coined in a 2002 Renault commercial.

His complete centre-forward abilities made him one of the most feared players of all time across his career, and he also had the trophy haul to match. World Cup and European Championship glory came alongside Champions League silverware, and he even ended his soccer days with a memorable MLS swansong at the New York Red Bulls.

Lewandowski is one of the greatest pure goalscorers in the history of soccer. His elite finishing, exceptional anticipation and underrated physicality have all combined to make him a serious force across several decades of playing. He will go down as one of the best players to ever play in Germany and certainly one of the finest strikers in this century.

He was robbed of a Ballon d’Or in 2020 after cancellation due to COVID-19, and arguably again in 2021 as Messi trumped him on reputation alone. The Polish superstar is his country’s greatest ever player and has scored over 750 goals across a 20-year career, while he is now winding down his playing days with Chicago Fire.

Neymar is perhaps one of the most divisive soccer players ever, given that he would have placed even higher on this list had he applied himself fully, but his amazing natural ability has still seen him become one of the world’s greatest. He is a modern-day Brazilian icon who has dominated social media and the wider sporting zeitgeist of the last 15 years, and holds the distinction of being the closest of any player to breaking up the Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo Ballon d’Or duopoly of the 2010s.

The ex-Barcelona winger is Selecao soccer royalty, even though the World Cup has eluded him despite his outstanding career. He is the all-time top scorer and assist provider for his national team and is one of five players ever to have scored over 100 professional goals with three different clubs. Neymar also remains the most expensive player ever after joining PSG for £200m in 2017.

Rummenigge was capable of playing across the forward line and dominated defences in Germany during his 10 years at Bayern Munich between 1974 and 1984. He was equally strong with both feet and a fine dribbler who boasted impressive finishing ability, while also becoming a global ambassador for his country as he established himself as a star for Inter after Bayern.

He won the Ballon d’Or in 1980 and 1981, and helped shape the German giants into a European superpower with two European Cup wins in the 70s. Rummenigge also won the European Championships with his country and finished as a runner-up twice in the World Cup.

Kocsis was an integral part of Hungary’s ‘Golden Team’ of the 1950s, which remains one of the most iconic national team sides in soccer history. The Budapest-born star became a sporting icon for his country throughout his playing days, as he scored at an exceptional rate for several sides and also became one of Barcelona’s greatest-ever players. His nickname was ‘Golden Head’ because of his exceptional heading ability.

He is second in the list of top single-tournament World Cup scorers, with 11 in the 1954 edition, and his 1.103 goals per game average is ranked number one for those with caps in FIFA class-A competitions, meaning he is effectively the most prolific international scorer ever.

An icon who is perhaps mostly defined by his off-field troubles and antics, Best is lauded as one of the best of his time and someone who consistently pushed fans to the edge of their seats whenever he had the ball at his feet. He was soccer’s original celebrity superstar in the West, and his mop-top hairstyle remains synonymous with those silky feet to this day.

Best changed the image of soccer players as a real household name in the UK, and had the undoubted ability to match his fame. Man United were already a huge club before his arrival on the scene in 1963, but he fired them to a maiden European Cup triumph and was a key player as they continued to rise. The Northern Irishman’s career tailed off but he still had time to become one of the first big-name stars to play in the USA with LA Aztecs, as he enjoyed numerous strong spells in the NASL.

Back to the modern day with a player who is currently starring in MLS, ‘El Pistolero’ has been one of the best soccer stars in the world since joining Liverpool in 2011 and is one of Uruguay’s greatest of all time. His outstanding technical ability has been flanked by an unstoppable determination to win and pure aggression over the last 15 years, with numerous high-profile incidents making him one of the most controversial players ever too.

Suarez was part of the best attacking trio of all time at Barcelona alongside Neymar and Messi, and has scored over 600 professional goals in his career so far. He holds numerous major records and is another who would have dominated even more if not for two standouts also playing in his generation.

Some may feel like Mbappe is too high on this list, but it is only right to celebrate him as one of the greatest forwards ever, even if he is nowhere near finished in the sport of soccer. The French superstar has reached incredible heights over the last 10 years and is a global phenomenon who consistently ranks among the best scorers and players every season. Mbappe is yet to lift a Ballon d’Or but, incredibly, has finished in the top 10 in all nine editions in which he has been nominated.

His remarkable collection of records includes: most World Cup goals in history (22), most World Cup final goals (4), France’s all-time leading scorer and the only player to win two World Cup Golden Boots. He is only likely to move further up this list as time goes on.

Matthews was one of soccer’s first genuine global superstars. Nicknamed ‘The Wizard of the Dribble’, he helped to define the traditional winger’s role and attracted hundreds of thousands of supporters to stadiums all by himself during his time with Stoke, Blackpool and England. Pele reportedly said that he had taught people how soccer should be played.

He became a landmark figure in the history of the sport after winning the first Ballon d’Or in 1956 at the age of 41. Matthews also remains the oldest professional to play in England, at 50, and he raised the profile of wide players as a whole for the way he decimated defences before retiring in 1965.

The San Siro’s official name is the ‘Stadio Giuseppe Meazza’; such is the significance of the Italian forward to soccer in the region and his country. It was named thus in 1980 following his passing, after Meazza represented both clubs between 1927 and 1942 and built his name as one of the sport’s first prolific scorers at the top level known across the world. He was regarded as an elegant player and a great leader who could feature across the forward line.

Meazza won numerous individual accolades during and after his playing career. His crowning moment was a World Cup Golden Ball award in Italy’s winning campaign of 1934, while he also featured as they won a successive crown four years later.

Puskas is another star of the past who has been able to transcend generations in soccer folklore. He was the crown jewel of Hungary’s Golden Team and a leading star in the sport across the world in the 1950s and 60s. His outstanding range of scoring ability and prolificness means his legacy still lives on through FIFA’s Puskas Award, awarded to the best goal each year.

He holds one of the best international scoring rates, with 84 in 85 Hungary games, the most goals scored in a single European Cup final (four for Real Madrid in 1960), and bagged a whopping 802 official career goals in 792 matches between 1943 and 1966.

Muller was such a good striker that France Football’s award for the most prolific player in that position for each season has been named after him since 2021. The six-yard box was home for the German star, who needed little space or time to find the net and was a defining figure for his country as well as a global star of the 1970s and 80s.

He is one of just eleven players ever to have won the Ballon d’Or, World Cup and Champions League. Muller also plundered home 68 goals in 62 international appearances, while he remains the all-time leading scorer in the Bundesliga (356 goals).

Romario was one of the most clinical forwards in soccer history during his playing days. He personified Brazilian skill and flair alongside a natural ruthless streak in the area to become one of the leading strikers of his generation in the 1980s, 1990s and 2000s. Romario only featured for eight seasons in Europe, and so his outstanding legacy is testament to a career that was not held back by a preference to play in his home country.

His explosive ability in the final third fired Brazil to 1994 World Cup glory in the USA, as he lifted the Golden Ball and was named the FIFA World Player of the Year. He scored over 700 professional goals in his decorated career.

Van Basten retired at just 30 years old in 1995, and so it speaks to just how much of an impact he had on soccer that he is so high on this list despite injury ending his career prematurely. The Dutch forward combined exceptional physical presence with amazing technique to create iconic moments aplenty. His volleyed goal in the Euro 1988 final against the USSR is widely regarded as one of the greatest ever.

He was a central figure in AC Milan’s run as one of the most successful European sides in that same period, winning two European Cups and the Ballon d’Or three times between 1988 and 1992. Van Basten’s career was an incredible one as he peaked higher than many in this list, but he can only rank here because it was cruelly cut short.

Ronaldinho brought Brazilian street spirit to the world’s biggest stages in his time playing soccer. He was the ultimate entertainer and became one of the most recognisable and most marketable sporting figures on the planet in the 2000s for his iconic swagger on and off the pitch. The extraordinary playmaker became an icon for his nation, as well as the likes of Barcelona, PSG and AC Milan.

His mercurial performances helped Brazil win the 2002 World Cup, and he also won the 2005 Ballon d’Or while spearheading Barca’s resurgence throughout the decade. Real Madrid fans were even drawn to applauding his performance in a particular El Clasico, while he was the world’s highest-paid soccer player ahead of David Beckham in 2006 too, owing to his wealth of commercial endorsements.

‘The Blond Arrow’ was an outstanding striker for his time and is held up as one of the greatest players to grace the sport. Di Stefano was a complete player who could drop deep and dictate play as well as hang around the box to score at will. He is attributed with pioneering such a role, as well as an early version of the Dutch ‘Total Football’.

His 1953 arrival at Real Madrid transformed the club into the global superpower we know today, with five consecutive European Cup wins, as he scored in each final, and eight La Liga titles in his next 11 seasons at the club. He ranks fourth in their all-time scorers list (308) after also winning two Ballon d’Ors and the unique Super Ballon d’Or award in 1989.

Garrincha pioneered and symbolised the Brazilian idea of ‘joga bonito’, as he wowed audiences throughout his career with incredible dribbling skills, balance and acceleration. He provided the blueprint for the winger role as we know it now and was a global superstar as Brazilians took the sport by storm in the mid-20th century.

He carried his country to the 1962 World Cup and won the Golden Ball, while Brazil also remarkably avoided defeat across all 40 international games that he played with Pele. The right winger is one of the greatest players to feature in the top flight of his home country, with 245 recorded goals in 612 appearances for Botafogo.

Eusebio put Portuguese soccer on the map during a similar era to Garrincha, and was the first African-born player to become a worldwide star in the sport. He was dangerous both inside and outside the penalty area while possessing excellent close control and underrated physicality. Eusebio was the biggest soccer export from Portugal before the 21st century and helped to break down barriers as a leading black figure in a time full of racial discrimination and inequality.

The 1965 Ballon d’Or winner’s achievements speak for themselves. He was central to Benfica becoming a powerhouse of a club as they won numerous league and continental titles with him in attack, while also winning the European Golden Shoe twice and the 1966 World Cup Golden Boot.

O Fenomeno is among the most technically gifted strikers on this list and was a generational talent during his soccer career. He was a completely unstoppable force on the pitch and became a global celebrity off it in the rising digital age of the early 2000s. No one can forget Ronaldo’s 2002 World Cup haircut, which may well be the most iconic style of any player ever.

An absolute nightmare for defenders, the Brazilian’s silky skills and devastating speed made goals almost easy for him to come by, even at the top level. He is a club legend for Barcelona, Inter and Real Madrid, a two-time World Cup winner and two-time Ballon d’Or winner, and still one of soccer’s biggest ‘what ifs’ as serious knee injuries disrupted his later career.

Cruyff remains a true pioneer and trailblazer for attackers throughout soccer history. The enigmatic Dutch star was able to destroy defences with exceptional intelligence and creativity while being the face of ‘Total Football.’ His long, swept-back hair and innocent look became iconic as it went hand-in-hand with the effortless class he showed on the pitch.

The number 14 is synonymous with Ajax icon Cruyff, who helped the Dutch side dominate European soccer in the 1970s and won three Ballon D’Ors in four years during that period. Cruyff is the greatest Ajax and Netherlands player ever, while he also holds legendary status at Barcelona.

Five-time Ballon d’Or winner Ronaldo has a seriously strong claim to being the most recognisable and well-known sportsperson of all time. That is no mean feat, but his incredible wealth, longevity and social reach all combine to make him a machine of marketing to this very day. He has built such an empire by becoming one of the most dominant and prolific soccer forwards ever over the last 20 years.

The Portuguese icon holds records galore for numerous competitions and clubs, with the most international appearances (234) and goals (146) of any player in the sport. He is approaching the incredible 1,000-goal mark and is the statistically greatest player in Champions League history too. Ronaldo misses out on the top three through no real fault of his own, but those above him were more naturally talented players.

Maradona is not only one of the greatest soccer stars ever; he defined the sport for numerous years and became a global phenomenon for his crazy antics on and off the pitch, while also building an almost cult-like following that spread across clubs he represented and the wider soccer world. He became a symbol of national pride in Argentina and even inspired the creation of a religion, such is the way he captivated those by how he played the sport.

The eccentric second striker enjoyed the single best World Cup campaign of all time as he dragged his country to glory in 1986, with his ‘Hand of God’ goal against England arguably the most iconic and well-known strike in soccer to this day. His best club achievement was undoubtedly transforming Napoli into Italian champions, as he became a hero in Italy, with his influence there still prominent to this day as their stadium is named after him.

Pele was long regarded as the number one on this list, but will have to settle for second place despite being a game-defining superstar who remains lauded as a soccer immortal nearly 50 years on from his retirement. The greatest player from the most decorated country in the sport, superlatives can barely describe his legacy after he was key to making soccer a global spectacle in the mid-20th century.

The Brazilian was the best player of his generation and would have been the greatest in those directly before and after him before Maradona came along. Pele remains the only player to win three World Cups, scoring in two finals, while the debate around his official career goals total rages on. He boasted over 1,000 strikes with friendly and exhibition games included, and was also a trailblazer overseas as he grew the game exponentially in the USA during his stint at the New York Cosmos.

Messi is simply the best soccer player ever. Forget forwards. The Argentine hero has defined a generation over the last 20 years and reached heights that no one thought could be found after Pele and Maradona. He also has a strong claim to be the most recognisable sportsperson of all time, with immense wealth and global reach making him a celebrity across the planet aside from his genius on-field achievements.

The iconic number 10 shirt worn by those before him is now Messi’s above anyone else. He has defied description in so many ways on countless occasions, yet has seemed to reach even greater levels in recent years towards the end of his career. The most Ballon d’Ors (8), most goals in a calendar year (91), the most official goals scored for one club (672 at Barcelona) and the most official team trophies (47) are just some of the seemingly limitless list of records he holds in the sport. It will be one of the most monumental days in sporting history when he decides to hang up his boots.
