Crystal Palace are closing in on an agreement for Thomas Frank to become their next manager, sources have told Football Insider.

Pierre Sage's dismissal was not in the plans for the South London club, who had been keen to stick with the Frenchman, but they have now been forced into a change.

The former Tottenham and Brentford boss has quickly emerged as the front-runner for the position at Selhurst Park, with talks having taken place throughout this week.

As I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, Frank's Premier League experience and remarkable work with Brentford have made him the top choice.

The boss is also viewed as a good motivator, which is something Palace are searching for to improve their morale having dropped to the bottom of the Premier League table.

Crystal Palace hope Frank's reign will reflect the work he did with Brentford rather than with Tottenham, where he struggled, and believe he is the right man for the job.

Football Insider revealed on 13 November that Crystal Palace are locked in talks with Frank to become their next manager and are making progress in their discussions.

A number of other candidates have been considered, including the likes of Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira, but the former Brentford boss has always been the first choice.

Palace had initially hoped to have his appointment wrapped up quickly, but despite the drawn-out timeframe, they still believe he will be the man to deliver positive results.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "Discussions are happening between Crystal Palace and Thomas Frank, they have made him their number one target to replace Pierre Sage.

"Obviously the key thing for Thomas Frank is that he's got the Premier League experience that Palace probably need right now to get them out of their current predicament.

"They want to make sure they're not involved in a relegation battle as the season goes on, and think Frank is the man to get them out of that.

"His CV is quite good. He's a good motivator as well. He did a great job at Brentford and I'm sure Palace will be hoping that he could repeat his success that he had at Brentford at Crystal Palace.

"The squad is good at Palace as well, I think it's just about getting the best out of them, and I'm sure that Palace feel that Thomas Frank is the right man to turn things around at Selhurst Park."

As previously mentioned, Crystal Palace had hoped to have the appointment of their next manager wrapped up closely after Sage's exit earlier this week.

However, one week after the 3-1 defeat against Liverpool which put the writing on the wall for Sage, they have still not reached an agreement with their top target.

Football Insider revealed on 13 November that Frank's appointment has hit a new stumbling block regarding the backroom team who would join him at Selhurst Park.

The Eagles are currently working to negotiate deals with Frank's rather sizable team, as they aim to back him with his trusted allies after doing the same for Sage previously.

While the deal is not expected to face any major issues as a result, the ongoing negotiations explain the reason for the delays surrounding Frank's official appointment.

The likes of Bayern Munich and Arsenal are interested in the talented forward, who would have his pick of the European giants if he decided to leave.

#1915. Lewis Hall faultless, 2/10 nearly ruins game: England player ratings in win vs Spain

Senior Correspondent AUTHORITY Senior football journalist specialising in refereeing and officiating; former contributor to The Football League Paper, Late Tackle, and the Premier League; University of Derby graduate. FOCUS Refereeing controversies, football finance and governance, PGMOL decisions, and officiating analysis across the Premier League, EFL, and SPFL. THE INSIGHT Harri utilises a network of officiating and industry contacts to deliver verified, expert analysis of refereeing decisions and PGMOL policy. He provides the regulatory clarity behind the controversy to ensure fans get the full picture.

England avoided a second-half scare to secure an important three points against Spain in a heavyweight Nations League clash.

Thomas Tuchel's side started the brighter on Sunday, 15 November, as Jude Bellingham was thwarted by Unai Simon in the opening minutes.

The Three Lions finally made their pressure pay, with Harry Kane converting from the penalty spot after being fouled by Pau Cubarsi.

Ezri Konsa then doubled the lead in the 53rd minute, powering home a cross from Declan Rice, with Ben White also getting in on the action.

Bellingham slid in the on-rushing right-back, who slotted brilliantly under Simon, all but bringing an end to Spain's incredible unbeaten run.

Elliot Anderson's red card changed the game completely, though. Only James Trafford could save the 3-2 win after goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams.

It's rarely a good sign when the best player on the pitch is a full-back, but Lewis Hall was absolutely everywhere against Spain.

An early test against Lamine Yamal actually ended in Declan Rice being cautioned. After that, it was smooth sailing for the Newcastle United man.

It's simple to see why Manchester United want him so badly. It wasn't just his defending, but also his impact in the final third.

Hall will be disappointed that he didn't get an assist in the first half, but he continued fighting right until the final whistle.

England were absolutely cruising at 3-0 up, but just one bad decision later, and Spain were right back in the game at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano.

He clearly pushed Yamal in the back insisde the penalty area, and given that it was a last-man challenge, the referee was given no other choice.

Anderson's sending-off changed the game completely, and for that reason alone, the Manchester City man falls right to the bottom of the rankings.

Up until that point, the midfielder was just one point behind Hall. His red card didn't just change his score, but also the game in its entirety.

- Jude Bellingham (Off for Spence 83') - 7

- Anthony Gordon (Off for Calvert-Lewin 83') - 7

- Harry Kane (Off for Lewis-Skelly 78') - 5

- Myles Lewis-Skelly (On for Kane 78') - 5

- Dominic Calvert-Lewin (On for Gordon 83') - 6

- Djed Spence (On for Bellingham 83') - 5

#1909. Mauricio Pochettino identifies seven Man Utd stars he is desperate to work with

Mauricio Pochettino is relishing the opportunity to work with a number of Manchester United stars when he arrives at Old Trafford.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has agreed a two-and-a-half year deal to replace Michael Carrick in Manchester with his first game in charge set to be away to Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

Marcus Rashford could be one of the big winners of the club’s latest appointment with The Daily Telegraph reporting Pochettino has ‘always loved’ the England international.

#1904. Zinedine Zidane defends Chelsea star after ‘nightmare’ performance in France defeat

Zinedine Zidane has defended Malo Gusto following the Chelsea defender’s poor performance during France’s 3-1 defeat to Italy on Thursday night.

Michael Olise gave France an early lead in Milan but a double from Pio Esposito, plus a goal from Davide Frattesi, handed Zidane his first loss since taking over from Didier Deschamps in July.

Gusto, who has started just three Premier League games for Chelsea this season, was selected at right-back but struggled against Nicolo Cambiaghi and gave away the foul which led to Italy’s penalty in the second half.

French media described Gusto’s performance as a ‘nightmare’, while RMC Sport host Daniel Riolo tore into the Chelsea defender after France’s defeat.

‘Malo Gusto, who never plays for his club, I don’t even know what he’s doing there,’ Riolo said. ‘He was toyed with by Bologna’s winger… I don’t understand why Zaire-Emery isn’t playing. We don’t have any full-backs, so you play with the wingers tucked in.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

But despite the scoreline against Italy, Zidane has urged his players not to panic.

‘We lost the match, so naturally there were some more complicated situations, particularly in duels and one-on-one situations, we weren’t quite as good. It’s all part of the learning process.

‘When we were in difficulty, we didn’t know how to react and stay within the game plan we had put in place. We did it in the first half, but when they took the lead, we became a little scattered, especially defensively.

‘Tonight wasn’t a bad game. There’s room for improvement. I told the players we shouldn’t panic. We became more fragile as the match went on. What I told them is that it was a defeat, but not entirely deserved.

‘We did some good things and some not-so-good things. We’ll analyse it when we’re in Bordeaux to prepare for our match. We just need to rest and focus on the game we have left.’

#1899. What Sebastien Pocognoli said to Billy Gilmour after Scotland miss left him ‘alone on the pitch’

Sebastien Pocognoli has hailed the way Billy Gilmour responded to the horror of missing an open goal just moments after half-time against North Macedonia.

The midfielder experienced a moment to forget when he blazed over from the edge of the six-yard box with the goal gaping in front of him during Friday’s 2-1 Nations League win.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

All’s well that ended well as Scotland kept their Nations League hopes alive thanks to John McGinn’s double. However, there was concern when North Macedonia equalised almost immediately after the midfielder’s opener on 54 minutes.

Gilmour played his part in the recovery before being replaced by Ryan Christie two minutes after McGinn’s winner from the penalty spot. He was given a tremendous ovation by the home crowd, who recognised his bravery in playing through the difficult moments directly after the miss.

Gilmour had to literally pick himself back up from the turf after slumping to the ground following his moment to forget. Pocognoli noted “the noise” as fans sought to process what had happened. He described Gilmour as “alone on the pitch” in this period. But the midfielder did not hide and contributed to Scotland’s win.

McGinn’s second of the night from the spot, after Ben Gannon-Doak was tripped by goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski, drew the midfielder level with Hughie Gallacher in third place in the all-time Scotland goalscorer standings with 24 goals.

Gilmour, who has scored twice in 51 international appearances, won’t ever feature at the top end of this list but he should now be sitting on three goals for Scotland.

Some have compared his miss to the infamous one suffered by striker Chris Iwelumo in a World Cup qualifier against Norway in 2008.

Peter van Vossen, whose name is forever associated with a horrendous open goal gaffe for Rangers against Celtic in a league fixture 30 years ago this weekend, was also referenced.

“For me, it is part of football to miss big chances,” said Pocognoli. “With his quality, he absolutely has to put it away. It was more difficult to put out!

“But I always say to the players that I am watching the reaction more. I was straight on at him after he missed. I say: ‘Go on!’ He reacted really well and I was really happy.

“That was what I said to him when he came off. I said: ‘Good reaction.’ Because there was a lot of noise after that and he was alone on the pitch. I think he did really well.”

#1898. Michael Carrick issues first statement after Manchester United sacking

Michael Carrick has thanked Manchester United’s players and supporters following his sacking and insists he wants ‘nothing but success’ for the club.

Carrick was sacked by United on Thursday, while Mauricio Pochettino was officially announced as his replacement on Friday afternoon.

The 45-year-old returned to United in January following Ruben Amorim’s departure and joined on an interim deal until the end of last season.

Carrick was then rewarded with a two-year contract in May following United’s impressive end to the Premier League campaign, with no club in the top flight securing more points than the 36 United collected following Carrick’s arrival.

In his statement which was released on Friday, Carrick wrote: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful.

‘With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It’s different to anywhere else.

‘I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

‘I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

#1897. Saturday's Nations League predictions including Norway vs. Wales, Portugal vs. Denmark

By Ben Knapton | 14 Nov 2026 00:00

Today's Nations League predictions include Wales' trip to Norway, while a Cristiano Ronaldo-less Portugal battle Denmark.

Kosovo and Israel will clash at Stadiumi Fadil Vokrri on Saturday afternoon in UEFA Nations League B Group 3.

The hosts are second in the standings with five points from four games, while the visitors are at the bottom of the table with two points after four matches.

Kosovo have had the stronger campaign and have never lost to Israel in any of their previous meetings, and with the home advantage also in their favour, we are predicting a victory for the hosts.

Georgia and Hungary both still have plenty to play for as they prepare to lock horns in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League on Saturday night.

The hosts are currently bottom of the section but can still finish second, while Hungary are currently second in the standings behind Northern Ireland.

Georgia have struggled in this group and will be without their star player on Saturday, so it is difficult to back them to pick up a positive result against a solid Hungarian outfit.

Two teams still in with a chance of making the quarter-finals of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League will lock horns on Saturday, with Norway hosting Wales.

Norway have actually lost each of their last three matches in Group A4 to give themselves a mountain to climb, while Wales have been beaten in three of their four games in the competition, but qualification for the final four is still possible at this stage.

Norway have struggled in the section so far, but we are expecting Haaland to help the hosts secure a vital three points on Saturday.

Fighting to maintain their lead at the top UEFA Nations League B's Group B2, Northern Ireland will host Ukraine at Windsor Park on Saturday.

The Norn Iron are unbeaten in the competition so far, while the Blue and Yellow arrive on the back of a three-game winless run.

Northern Ireland have been far from free flowing in the Nations League, but their defensive resilience has been impressive, especially with the likes of Ballard sidelined.

Ukraine have struggled even more than their hosts up front, and could find the Norn Iron's backline particularly tough to break down.

The Republic of Ireland will look to close the gap to the top of their Nations League B group by beating hosts Austria on Saturday at Raiffeisen Arena.

Sitting in third place with five points, Ireland trail their first-placed opponents by three points with six left to play for, and a victory would set up a tense final matchday.

Ireland have been poor away from home, though they boast a positive record against their opponents.

Austria's performances at home have been excellent, but while they are unlikely to lose, they may have to settle for just a point.

> Austria vs. Republic of Ireland preview

Romania and Poland will lock horns at the Arena Nationala in Bucharest on Saturday night, with both nations desperate to get their UEFA Nations League campaigns back on track.

Pressure is mounting on both managers, while the threat of relegation from League B adds further intrigue to an already tasty contest.

Romania are in the midst of a turbulent time, but Poland’s run of three successive away defeats does not exude much confidence either.

This does not have the makings of a classic under the lights, and our prediction is a 1-1 draw.

The top two in Group B4 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League will lock horns on Saturday evening, as Sweden welcome Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Both teams are bidding to secure first position in the section, which would mean automatic qualification to League A for the next Nations League.

This is a really difficult match to call, and we are finding it difficult to separate them given Bosnia-Herzegovina's unbeaten campaign to date. The two teams could be forced to accept a share of the spoils on Saturday.

Portugal will officially begin life after the legendary Cristiano Ronaldo with a clash against Denmark in the UEFA Nations League on Saturday night.

Jorge Jesus' side have already booked their spot in the quarter-finals of the competition, while Denmark are battling to claim the second qualification spot in the section.

Denmark are more than capable of making this a tricky match for Portugal, and we are backing the visitors to score, but Jesus' side should be able to extend their 100% record in this season's competition.

From watching the World Cup from the comfort of his local pub to making his first international start at the heart of Scotland’s defence, it’s been a remarkable couple of months for Luke Graham.

Nominated for the SWFA Young Player of the Year award following a series of colossal displays for Dundee last season, many tipped him to make a late claim for a place in Steve Clarke’s squad for the tournament in the summer. Courted by both Celtic and Rangers in the weeks that followed, Portsmouth had launched a seven-figure bid during the January window. However, when the summer transfer window re-opened, it was Stoke City who won the race for his signature. Currently third in the EFL Championship, Graham has been a star performer for them this season.

Awarded his first international start in Friday’s 2-1 win over North Macedonia, Graham admits things are beginning to fall into place. “Not much is going wrong for me at the moment,” he smiled. “I wouldn’t say I merited a start, we have a lot of good players in the camp. A good turn out.

“We’re going through a bit of a transitional spell just at the minute, so it’s not going to be all smooth sailing from the get-go. It’s about adjusting to that and try to build on performances in every game.”

It was all so different for the youngster a mere 142 days ago. Asked how he digested Scotland’s World Cup adventure - the first in his lifetime - during the summer, Graham’s financial situation stopped him from attending the tournament in North America. However, on the evidence of his composed performance against North Macedonia, he’s got every reason to believe he won’t need to watch from afar when Scotland next travel to a major tournament.

“I didn’t go [to the World Cup] - it was too expensive for me!” laughed Graham. “I was just like everyone else, watching in the pub with their mates. It was pretty amazing and hopefully I can be part of something like that one day. I wasn’t too far away, Steve Clarke told me. It’s just about trusting myself now and hopefully get there one day.”

By Lewis Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 01:13

Arsenal could be joined in the race for Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi by Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City, the newest report has revealed.

The Gunners may have entered the international break as leaders in the Premier League, but there are still some concerns in the fanbase.

Mikel Arteta's side have only scored 15 goals in 10 top-flight matches, and that has naturally led to calls for the club to strengthen in attack in the January transfer window.

The Londoners have been linked to Tresoldi, with the Club Brugge striker currently valued at just over £29m by Transfermarkt.

However, a new report from Het Laatste Nieuws claims that the striker is also wanted by Premier League sides such as Liverpool, Chelsea and Man City.

Tresoldi has enjoyed a strong start to 2026-27, scoring 13 goals in 15 games for Club Brugge, including five times in four Champions League games.

Arteta will be pleased that the 22-year-old scored against Aston Villa and Inter Milan this season as it would suggest that the striker could adapt to a team in a more competitive league.

The biggest reason for the Gunners' interest in the forward is undoubtedly the underperformance of Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres, both of whom have disappointed for some time.

Gyokeres has only been trusted to start once in the Premier League this season, and he has routinely struggled against teams in the top half of the table.

Havertz has found it difficult to stay consistently fit, and his performances have been frustratingly mixed since signing for the Gunners in 2023.

The Gunners will almost certainly not face any serious competition from Liverpool, who already have Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitike as options up front.

Manchester City could have interest in Tresoldi as a backup to Erling Haaland, though it remains to be seen how keen any player would be about moving to the Etihad due to the threat of sanctions following news of the club being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

Chelsea are known to be active in the transfer market irrespective of the depth they have, and there is a clear spot for the Club Brugge striker at Stamford Bridge as the backup to Joao Pedro.

Whether Tresoldi would accept a role as a backup is unclear, but the Blues are in a serious battle for a Champions League spot, whereas Arsenal will almost certainly secure a return to the top level of European football.

#1892. John McGinn tells Scotland fans where to place Kool-Aid frustrations amid ‘March or September’ warning

Scotland may have got the win they needed against North Macedonia on Friday night; however, the grumble of discontent which greeted the final whistle proved that supporters are not yet ready to drink the Sebastien Pocognoli Kool-Aid.

Rescued by two second-half goals from John McGinn, the Aston Villa skipper spared his side’s blushes as they ran out 2-1 winners to keep alive their slim hopes of qualifying for the Nations League playoffs. Their overall performance was perhaps best described as patchy, though.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Booed off the park by sections of the home crowd at the break, McGinn admits he takes no issue with the Tartan Army voicing their displeasure at the team’s on-pitch displays, but has pleaded with them to vent their ire at himself and the more experienced names in Scotland’s dressing room than the fresh faces as they look to adjust to Pocognoli’s methods.

Get our daily football newsletter by clicking here.

“The manager's got a great reputation and a good record at both places he's went,” said McGinn following his two goal haul. “The most important thing now in football is individuals don't win you games. It's unity, teamwork and everyone on the same page. And you see how successful clubs do it, successful countries and we want to be one of them. It's not going to happen overnight.

“There's a lot to learn but we did create big chances in the game where we could have scored three, four or five and it could be a different story. This isn't something that gets fixed in March or even next September. it will start to build over the next 18 months. I think the young players are starting to show now more. Luke Graham tonight, I thought he was brilliant, it's not easy playing in the middle of a back three.

“He's been waiting for his chance and the manager's shown that if you deserve your chance you're going to get put in there. So we need players like Luke, Porto [Ryan Porteous] coming back, Doaky [Ben Gannon-Doak] showed glimpses tonight. So we've got so many players that can step up and they will. We just need to show that belief and take it to pitch.”

Asked if he felt the fans need to show patience, McGinn said: “Maybe a bit. I understand it's frustrating; it's freezing, you want to see four, five, six goals, but the balance has got to be there. They're entitled to their opinion, but there's got to be a mixture of patience. But at the same time, the supporters are entitled to say whatever they like. But just as long as they hurl anything they want to shout at the experienced boys. Just let the young ones flourish and try to settle into the team.”

Awarded player of the match against North Macedonia, the 31-year-old’s brace shot himself into joint-third in Scotland’s record goalscorers list. McGinn’s international goal tally is now 24, drawing level with Hughie Gallacher, six short of Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law. Asked if it had sunk in yet, the former Hibs man kept his focus on the team, insisting Monday’s clash against Switzerland holds more importance as they look to give themselves a chance of qualifying for the Nations League playoffs.

“A bit strange obviously but at the minute that's gone to the back burner,” said McGinn. “We need to play slightly better. We know that but we're going through a period which I've been used to at club level, a lot of changes, a lot of detail that we need to try and remember and get used to. It's about sticking at it. We're keen to play a style of football that's not easy but it's going to get bums off seats.

“It takes time, over a few years now at club level it's been the exact same for us but the supporters stuck with us, the players stuck at it and it's important that everyone believes in it because if one person drops off or doesn't believe in it that's when it all starts to fall apart. We've got an important win but there's definitely a lot of room for improvement.

“It’s difficult, I know they [Switzerland] drew [vs Slovenia] but they've got a couple of players back that they were missing last time. We want to be competing against these teams away from home, playing the same way. We're going to stick at it, it's not going to be perfect for a while but on Monday night we're no different.”

#1889. Sebastien Pocognoli believes Scotland ‘click’ is coming for player who served up a curate’s egg at Hampden

After 12 games so far, from Liverpool to Ljubljana, from Miami to North Macedonia, the ‘No Scotland, no party’ world tour of 2026 grinds into St Gallen on Monday for one final performance.

What a 12 months it’s been. Scotland at least managed to avoid going a whole calendar year without winning a competitive game at Hampden by narrowly overcoming North Macedonia in the Nations League on Friday night.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It’s a small triumph considering Scotland were hoping to make history a few months ago by qualifying for the second stage of a major tournament for the first time. So this is where we are, which is where exactly? Wrestling with a system that looks increasingly unsuited to Scotland. Rather than freeing them up, which was Sebastien Pocognoli’s manifesto when he took over, his preferred 3-4-1-2 formation seems to have put the players in a straitjacket. The idea was to play ten yards further forward. Instead, Scotland appear to be going backwards in every sense.

They nevertheless have the chance to end the international year with a truly eye-popping result if they can beat Switzerland, already confirmed as Group B1 winners. It is the 13th match in a year where Scotland have played teams from five of the six FIFA confederations. Six of the matches, including Monday, have been against teams in the top 20 of the Fifa rankings. This perhaps explains the unexceptional total of just five wins, two of them friendlies.

Scotland need another victory on Monday and must hope Slovenia don’t take three points their trip to North Macedonia to finish in the top two and earn a promotion chance via the play-offs this Spring. It’s been a challenging as well as often very memorable year.

The danger is Scotland are already all played out, no one more so than Andy Robertson. No one except Kenny Dalglish has appeared as many times for Scotland as the skipper. Robertson has survived the risk of suspension and will become Scotland’s most capped ever player when, fitness permitting, he lines up on Monday.

Ryan Christie came on for his 75th cap on Friday, while Kieran Tierney, if selected, will earn cap No. 60 against Switzerland. Scott McTominay, meanwhile, will hit the 75-mark.

No one’s getting any younger. But Pocognoli seems determined to keep faith with a system that demands dynamism.

“I think we need to rest well,” he said. “That is the first thing. If we want to play like this we need energy. I will need to consider the best approach for the game regarding the quality and also the fitness of some players. We have some players in the squad who we have to manage. They cannot play two games in a row.”

Aaron Hickey might be one of those, hence him being named among the substitutes for the supposedly less testing fixture against North Macedonia. If he comes back into the side against Switzerland what does that mean for Ben Gannon-Doak? The winger featured at right wing-back and once again produced a curate’s egg of a performance. Good in parts, including when he won Scotland’s match-winning penalty (although even that was after he had taken a poor touch).

The focus and indeed expectation placed on him seems completely unreasonable, although he possibly hasn’t helped himself. It’s what happens when you are named man of the match for Bournemouth in a 3-0 Europa League win over AC Milan.

But this does not mean there's been an overnight cure for the imperfections that dog the player, understandably so given he’s only just turned 21. Pocognoli believes things will “click” for him in time. The right choice will suddenly become his instinctive reaction. The final ball will become a weapon rather than his Achilles heel. “We know that he needs to improve on the end product,” said Pocognoli. “But he created a penalty and against Slovenia and North Macedonia away he created a number of unbelievable one v ones. He did that (on Friday) as well.

“I believe in one moment he will have a click about decision making. I believe if he is playing every game he can make (better) decisions….. he knows that he only has to play a game every two weeks sometimes he can (over)think, ‘This is my moment.’ It is a process. He will become older and will at some point become relaxed in his decision making.”

Whether Gannon-Doak ever achieves his potential might hinge on playing where he ought to be playing, which is as an out-and-out winger. At present, Pocognoli’s preferred formation won’t accommodate this. It’s unlikely that the Belgian is going to change his ways ahead of Monday, when Scotland might really need three centre halves (even if one of them is really a full back).

Former Dundee defender Luke Graham’s assured performance aged just 22 surely means he will line up once more in the middle of defence.

“I have really scanned the quality of the squad and I believe we have the quality to play like this,” said Pocognoli. “I believe that Luke Graham can be important to the defence. “I believe Kieran Tierney can be good in that position. I believe that Ryan Porteous is helpful for how we want to play because he is on the front foot."

Pocognoli mentioned his adherence to a midfield 'box', where Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson act as pivots. “We need speed if we want to use the box,” he said. “We have that with Ben, but we don’t have that unlimited specific quality.

“It is up to me to find the best way to play,” he added. “But it is not easy to bring players who come from different clubs with a different approach to fit into (the system) in two days. But we have a lot of players who play that way in Italy and other places. It has helped me a lot in the past.”

The past is history. Never mind Gannon-Doak, things need to start clicking sooner rather than later for Pocognoli.

#1888. Linda Noskova vs Elina Svitolina - WTA Finals prediction, form, head-to-head

By Joel Lefevre | 14 Nov 2026 01:44, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 19:28

In a rematch from this year’s Stuttgart Open quarter-finals, Linda Noskova and Elina Svitolina square off in the WTA Finals semis on Saturday.

Both ladies finished the group stage at 2-1, with the Czech losing her last match to Jessica Pegula 6-7 (2-7) 6-4 5-7, and Svitolina ousting Aryna Sabalenka on Friday 6-3 3-6 6-1.

The group phase did not end the way she had envisioned, but Linda Noskova will hope to shake off her surprise defeat from Thursday as she enters the knockout stage of this tournament for the first time.

After losing the opening set to Pegula, it appeared as though the tide was turning in the Czech’s favour, but the reigning Wimbledon champion failed to covert her match point, losing three straight games in the final set, which sent her to defeat.

She is the youngest player to reach the semi-finals of this tournament since Petra Kvitova in 2011, and Noskova will hope to follow in that same path as the former Czech player went on to win that edition of the WTA Finals in what was her debut.

If Noskova wants to advance, she must be cleaner on serve, registering 15 double faults versus Pegula, six more than she committed in her first two matches at this event.

In her three group contests, the 21-year-old converted 14 break-point opportunities overall while conceding eight.

She has hit a total of 20 aces at the tournament so far and won over 60% of her first serves in all three of her matches.

In a roller coaster three-set outing on Friday afternoon, Svitolina came out on top, winning six straight games in the end.

It was her first win against Sabalenka in six years as the Ukrainian earned a berth in the semis-finals of this event for the first time since 2019.

For a while it looked like Svitolina was going to throw it away, failing to convert four match points before finally claiming victory.

As a result, she has a chance to advance to the final of this tournament for a third time in her last three appearances.

Not since the 2017 WTA Finals group stage has she lost a match in this tournament when winning the opening set.

Svitolina has converted 11 break point opportunities in her last two outings after failing to convert six chances in her opener.

Third match: vs. Jessica Pegula 6-7 (7-2) 6-4 5-7

Second match: vs. Karolina Muchova 3-6 6-2 6-2

Third match: vs. Aryna Sabalenka 6-3 3-6 6-1

Australian Open (2024) - Round of 16: Noskova wins 3-0 walkover

Monterrey Open (2024) - Quarter-finals: Noskova wins 6-4 6-4

Stuttgart Open (2026) - Quarter-finals: Svitolina

The first meeting between these two occurred at the Aussie Open two years ago, when Svitolina was forced to retire with a severe back injury.

Later that year in Mexico, Noskova won 91% of her first serves, with two break points to take the win.

Svitolina earned her first win against Noskova in Germany this year, hitting 11 aces without a single double fault.

Svitolina has played a lot of tennis in a short time, and at her age, we do not believe she will have the energy to outlast Noskova this weekend.

#1887. Encouraging signs for Scotland under-21s as Spanish training camp ends in draw against experienced USA side

Scotland Under-21s rounded off their Spanish training camp with a 1-1 friendly draw against the United States Under-23 side at Pinatar Arena, as preparations for the upcoming European Championship qualifiers continued.

The Young Scots faced a stern test against an American outfit featuring six players with senior international experience and led by 87-cap former international Steven Cherundolo. The USA were using the fixture as an important step in their preparations for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Tony Docherty's side went into the contest in confident mood following an impressive 4-0 victory over Ukraine earlier in the week, looking to carry that momentum into their final fixture of the year in Murcia.

Their opponents presented a different challenge, bringing greater physical presence and experience to the encounter. However, Scotland proved more than a match for the Stars and Stripes, with St Mirren's Eseosa Sule scoring an 85th-minute equaliser to secure a share of the spoils.

Hearts striker James Wilson, who bagged a double against Ukraine on Thursday, featured in the starting line-up once again, alongside captain Tyler Fletcher, midfielders Lennon Miller and Kyle Ure, Andrew Tod of Dunfermline and Aberdeen full-back Mitchel Frame.

The fixture provided Docherty with another valuable opportunity to assess his much-changed squad as he builds towards the start of next year's qualification campaign. Following a productive week in Spain, Scotland can take plenty of encouragement from two performances against contrasting opposition.

Reflecting on the benefits of the training camp, Docherty said: “We were delighted with the performance and the result in the game against Ukraine on Thursday. It is a credit to the players that they have been able to take on board so much information in such a short period of time.

“The game against the USA was another step up in quality for the group. They were taking on a more experienced side, but we wanted to challenge the players, and we wanted to see what they can do on and off the ball in different situations.”

#1886. ‘Needs to move on’ – Mauricio Pochettino urged to sell £47m Manchester United star

Mauricio Pochettino has been urged to wield the axe and ‘move on’ club captain Bruno Fernandes in one of his first acts as the new Manchester United manager.

Pochettino will take charge of the United States’ two games against Haiti before beginning life as United boss after signing a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Carrick.

And the Argentine will not have much time to work with the squad before his first Premier League match in charge of the Red Devils away to Liverpool on November 22.

Pochettino might be hopeful that the January transfer window might offer him the chance to reshape his squad after a disappointing summer transfer window left several holes in United’s squad.

And former Red Devils assistant manager Rene Meulensteen has suggested that Pochettino consider cashing in on Fernandes after his sluggish start to the season.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘In terms of Bruno, Bruno has been a fantastic servant for Manchester United over many, many years,’ Meulensteen told talkSPORT.

‘He’s not hit the same levels this year round. I think he’s also been, to some extent, maybe even mentally damaged by all the negativity that has surrounded the club and himself.

‘To be fairly honest, I think he’s been a great servant, but I would not be too sad if he decided to leave the club.

‘I think there’s many more people, more players that I think need to move on, and we need to create a different kind of dynamism in the team.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Fernandes won the PFA Players’ Player of the Year last year after a superb second half of the season under Carrick, but has not hit those same heights so far this campaign.

The 32-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season, with The Athletic reporting that the midfielder recently turned down a second contract offer from the club.

Fernandes can talk to foreign clubs about a potential free transfer from January, but United do have the option to trigger a 12-month extension until the summer of 2028.

The Red Devils are also said to be considering a move for talented Como midfielder Nico Paz if they do decide to part ways with Fernandes in the coming months.

#1885. Who is Mario Frick? The new manager at Aberdeen who scored at Hampden, lost to Hibs and develops players

Mario Frick says he will create an environment at Aberdeen “where his players can thrive” after being appointed the next manager of the Pittodrie outfit.

Former Luzern boss Frick takes over from Stephen Robinson, who was sacked on Monday by Aberdeen with the team languishing in 11th place in the Premiership. The length of his contract has not been disclosed.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Dons hierarchy have moved quickly to land his successor and after a week of interviews have settled on former Liechtenstein striker Frick, 52, who has been out of work since the summer after end a five-year spell in Switzerland with Luzern.

Frick has also managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz in his homeland. He will be assisted by Roman Matter, a 44-year-old Swiss coach who was also at Luzern. The pair are due to arrive in Aberdeen imminently ahead of Saturday’s league match against bottom club Kilmarnock.

“I'm excited to be joining Aberdeen FC,” said Frick. “It's a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and big ambitions.

“Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.”

Chief executive Adrian Bevington revealed Frick was the “unanimous” choice of the Aberdeen board after going through a robust process to identify him.

“We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club,” said Bevington. “This appointment follows a thorough and extensive recruitment process led by [sporting director] Lutz Pfannenstiel and myself on behalf of the board, during which we spoke to a number of highly qualified candidates.

“Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

“Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.

“He was also exceptionally well regarded by the many people across the game we consulted during the process, and the Board was unanimous in its belief that he is the right person to lead Aberdeen Football Club forward.

“I would like to thank the board, in particular Willie Garner, and colleagues across the club for their diligence and support throughout this process.”

Pfannenstiel tipped Frick to have a “real impact at Pittodrie” and said his character will be crucial as the Dons look to climb the league table.

“I’m really pleased that we have been able to bring Mario Frick to Aberdeen,” said Pfannenstiel. “I have enormous respect for his football knowledge, leadership qualities and passion for the game.

“Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

“We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact. I’m looking forward to working closely with him.”

Born in the Swiss town of Chur, Frick carved out a playing career as a physical striker and holds the record number of caps for Liechtenstein, scoring 16 goals in 125 appearances. One of those strikes came at Hampden in a 2-1 defeat by Scotland in 2010.

Also deployed as a centre-half, Frick played for clubs such as FC Basel, FC Zürich, St. Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana before hanging up his boots in 2016 and moving into coaching.

At Vaduz, he secured promotion to the Swiss Super League, which earned him a move to Luzern. He spent five years with them, landing a fourth-placed finish. He faced Hibs in the 2024 Conference League, losing 5-3 on aggregate.

Frick most used formation with Vaduz and Luzern was a 4-4-2 diamond and he has carved out a reputation as a head coach who has developed younger players, most notably AC Milan and Switzerland midfielder Ardon Jashari.

#1884. Ex-Premier League ref calls Mikel Arteta a ‘nightmare’ to deal with

Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has named Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta as the toughest person to deal with on the touchline.

Last month, Arteta received his second yellow card of the season during Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Everton but said after the game that he had a dossier of other managers committing similar offences which have gone unpunished.

The Arsenal manager now faces a one-match touchline ban if he receives a third yellow card.

Scott, who refereed in the Premier League for a decade before retiring in 2025, claims Arteta ‘does push all the limits all of the time’ and described the Spaniard as ‘hard work’.

When asked who was the worst manager to deal with on the touchline, Scott told The Athletic: ‘Well, the trite answer is all of them when they’re losing.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The honest answer, I’m afraid, I know whatever I say at this point just gets me pelters but it is Arteta. He is the hardest work.

‘He really does push all the limits all of the time. I don’t mind that in many ways, he’s trying to get a competitive advantage for his team. That’s fine. That’s part of his job. And of course, he’s entitled to do it, and it’s for us to place them, but he does make your life extremely difficult.

‘He’s out of his box [technical area] all the time. I watched him recently in the game against Everton and every time Everton had the ball anywhere near the touchline on his side, he was like joining in the press, his toes are on the touchline.

‘As fourth official, it’s a nightmare, because if you step forward and do anything about it, you’re being pedantic, being petty. He does get away with rather too much. The officials do need to be a bit tighter. And I was one of them who let him do that. I’m not going to deny that. But he was just hard work. Really, really hard work all the time in a way that others tended to be hard work some of the time.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘And let’s not pretend the others are all, by comparison, angelic. Some were very controlled. Graham Potter would be an example. Didn’t have anything to do with you, just very, very calm, quiet. But then, of course, he got some stick at times for not showing that he cared enough. So I guess managers can’t win either way.’

#1882. Man United transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino's first signing 'completed' as major overhaul of Red Devils targeted

By Lewis Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 02:30

Manchester United have signed teenager Tyler Adjei from Reading and registered the centre-forward this week, the latest report has revealed.

The Red Devils confirmed the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino as the replacement for Michael Carrick this week, and fans are keen for further changes at Old Trafford.

United are 18th in the Premier League, and many of the players in their squad have failed to prove that they are good enough to play for the club.

The January transfer window will be key for Pochettino, and it would not be surprising to see the team target younger stars in the coming months.

Teenager Adjei has become the first signing of the Pochettino era, according to The Athletic, with the 16-year-old having signed from Reading, and he is expected to head straight into Darren Fletcher's Under-18s side.

The signing of Adjei will not benefit Pochettino this season, but his addition will still be important for the future of the club given there are a number of stars that will need to be phased out.

Though captain Bruno Fernandes is the side's best attacker, he is 32 and has started to show signs of decline, and the Red Devils will need a successor to fill his void sooner rather than later.

Ensuring there is a steady stream of younger stars at the club will make replacing important first-team players much easier, especially as prices across Europe have become significantly inflated.

Fernandes is not the only ageing star at Old Trafford, with nine members of the team set to be 29 or older by the time the season ends.

Defenders Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are 33 and 31 respectively, while Lisandro Martinez and Diogo Dalot have frequently been linked with exits.

While the Red Devils need reinforcements in almost every area of the pitch, their most pressing needs are in the backline.

Younger talents would help secure the future of United's defence, though bringing in defenders in their twenties would also be beneficial to Pochettino in 2027.

#1881. Romano and Moretto provide update on Milan’s Endrick pursuit: “Hasn’t said no”

This week, there have been some interesting rumours about AC Milan and their pursuit of Endrick. However, it may have been a bit misleading.

Yesterday, it seemed that Milan were almost out of the race to sign Endrick, with the Brazilian against the club’s Devil logo. Instead, the Corriere dello Sport report would have you believe that he’d prefer a move to Roma.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, his agency have denied this rumour and later reports suggested that the Rossoneri are very much in the race to sign the Brazilian. In fact, he could even leave Real Madrid permanently – with future clauses – so things have certainly developed a bit this week.

Speaking on his YouTube channel today, Romano provided an update on Endrick’s situation alongside Matteo Moretto and their words have been relayed by MilanNews.

“Endrick is currently evaluating his future. On one side, Real Madrid doesn’t want to release him, from the president to Jose Mourinho, who continues to reiterate this publicly; on the other, the boy wants to play,” Romano started.

“I wanted to add a footnote: Endrick’s entourage, ROC Nation, are letting it be known that the player hasn’t said no to Milan; he hasn’t said no to anyone on November 12th. He’s still in the evaluation phase; we’ll see what happens.

“He has two months left with Real Madrid: football changes in five minutes. Endrick’s position is currently completely open, and he’s a player—we were the first to talk about him—that Milan really likes. But it’s true that Roma is also there, there’s a queue of many teams ready to chase him.

“I just wanted to clarify that Endrick hasn’t said no to Milan. He’s keeping everything open while waiting to figure out—if he leaves—the best solution.”

Moretto then added, “A lot will depend on the player. In December, he’ll really understand what kind of path he wants to take. He’s currently noticing this lack of playing time, so the loan option is taking shape. Roma have been maintaining contact for weeks.

“Roma want an additional striker because they believe with one or two signings they can really compete for something important this year. Keep an eye on Roma, but Milan was one of the first to move, and the relationship between Cardinale and ROC Nation is excellent. So far, Roma has maintained contact a little more actively, but Milan is insisting.”

It’s clear that January will be very interesting where Endrick is involved, especially with him being the one to make the decisions on his future.

Martin Odegaard hopes to stay at Arsenal ‘for a long time’ despite interest from Bayern Munich.

#1878. Arsenal star ‘will not turn down Real Madrid’ when transfer offer comes

Arsenal star William Saliba would not turn down a move to Real Madrid, according to his former teammate Morgan Schneiderlin.

Saliba has developed into one of the best centre-halves in world football under Mikel Arteta having arrived from Saint-Etienne for £27million in 2019.

During his time in north London, the centre-half has been persistently linked with a move to Real Madrid. Last year, Mikel Arteta sat down with his defender to discuss the ‘noise’ with Saliba telling the Gunners boss he was happy in north London.

Former Southampton, Manchester United and Everton midfielder Schneiderlin played alongside the France international for one season at Nice back in 2021, convinced then of his world class ability.

But the former Premier League star feels there will come a time where he will be unable to say no to a move to the Bernabeu.

#1876. Sudan vs Senegal - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 14 Nov 2026 06:19, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 16:27

Sudan will be looking to bounce back from a heavy defeat in Dakar when they welcome Senegal to the Juba National Stadium on Monday.

The Lions of Teranga sit top of Group J on seven points from three games after Thursday’s 4-1 win in the reverse fixture, while the hosts are third on three points, having won one and lost two of their opening three qualifiers.

Senegal have made an unbeaten start to life under Patrick Vieira, who replaced Pape Thiaw after the Lions were eliminated by Belgium in the last 32 of the 2026 World Cup.

They opened with a 1-1 draw away to Mozambique, with Nicolas Jackson scoring, then won 1-0 away to Ethiopia thanks to Ibrahim Mbaye’s early goal.

Thursday’s victory in Dakar was Vieira’s home debut and it went smoothly, with the in-form Jackson putting Senegal ahead in the 31st minute, before they scored three times in 25 second-half minutes to take the game away after Mohamed Abuaagla equalised on 45 minutes.

The Lions will hope for the same on Monday and will be quite optimistic, having never lost to Sudan in nine meetings across all competitions.

Sudan, ranked 118th in the world against Senegal’s 18th, began with a 1-0 win over Ethiopia in Juba, where Mohamed Eisa scored a penalty in the 86th minute.

They then lost 4-1 away to Mozambique, with Yasin Hamed’s penalty in the 88th minute their only goal. Abuaagla’s equaliser on Thursday came after both of their previous goals in the campaign had been penalties.

They have now conceded four goals in each of their last two games, a lack of defensive solidity that will be a big issue for coach James Kwesi Appiah, especially given that the two wins they have recorded in their last nine games have had to come with clean sheets.

However, they will hope to withstand the arsenal in Senegal’s attack, though the Falcons of Jediane might find that difficult due to fatigue, having taken a long route to this fixture, as Juba, in South Sudan, is their designated home ground in this campaign.

Sudan Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Senegal Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Sudan named a 24-man squad for the double-header, with several of Kwesi Appiah's players coming from domestic heavyweights Al Hilal and Al Merrikh.

Mohamed Eisa, Yasir Mozamil and Abubakr Eisa are among the attacking options available to Appiah, while defenders Ahmed Tabanja and Mustafa Karshom and goalkeeper Mohamed Mustafa will be important to the visitors' hopes of keeping Senegal at bay.

Senegal are without several regulars, with Sadio Mane and Idrissa Gana Gueye left out of Vieira's squad, while Ismail Jakobs has retired from international football after announcing his decision in October.

Krepin Diatta was initially selected but subsequently became unavailable through injury and replaced by Sevilla defender Arouna Sangante, while Mamadou Sarr is also sidelined with a calf problem.

Habib Diarra, Ismaila Sarr and Abdallah Sima are also unavailable for medical reasons.

Vieira can call upon Aston Villa duo Jackson and Mbaye in attack, with Boulaye Dia, Iliman Ndiaye and the newly called-up Pathe Mboup also providing options in the final third.

Kalidou Koulibaly captains the side, while Dion Lopy has returned after missing the previous international window.

Mustafa; Awad, Tabanja, Karshoum, Kuku; Khidir, Abuaagla; Alhassan, Omer, Nooh; Eisa

Diouf; Sane, Koulibaly, Niakhate; Mbaye, Camara, Lopy, El Hadji Malick Diouf; Ndiaye, Dia, Jackson

Sudan have conceded eight goals in two games and such porosity will be punished severely against a Senegal side that has a clear edge in quality and depth.

The Lions should have enough to win again and move to 10 points, and this should be a straightforward one, though we expect the scoreline to be more respectable compared to the reverse fixture.

#1875. Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono handed ban for tackle that led to Jesus de Miguel death

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games for his tackle that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The 25-year-old was sent off after his collision with De Miguel near the halfway line late in the Spanish second division match on November 2.

De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after Owono’s knee had struck him in the chest. The 30-year-old striker was taken to hospital where he died the following morning.

The Spanish Football Federation’s disciplinary committee has now issued the maximum suspension possible for Owono’s challenge.

A statement said: ‘The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel, is public knowledge. In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.’

In his first statement since De Miguel’s death, Owono insisted he will ‘face whatever comes with the utmost respect’.

‘These are the most difficult days of my life. I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very hard to process what has happened,’ Owono said.

‘I feel immense pain at the loss of Jesus. I’m thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

‘I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

Speaking this week, FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said that Owono is still considering his future in football.

‘He is deeply affected by the situation,’ Manso said.

‘We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return.’

#1874. Steyning’s second-half storm sinks Hastings United

The Barrowmen travelled full of confidence following their 2–1 home win over Horley Town. Hastings, meanwhile, were looking to respond after just one win in their previous four games, although a strong start to the league campaign meant they remained in the top three.

A crowd of 1,034 watched on a cold Saturday afternoon as an evenly contested opening offered few clear-cut chances.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Hastings broke the deadlock in the 20th minute when a corner caused chaos in the Steyning penalty area, with the ball going in off Conrad Honore for an own goal.

Chances remained scarce for the rest of the half as both sides defended well, allowing the hosts to take a slender advantage into the interval.

Steyning came flying out of the blocks after the restart and needed just four minutes to draw level, with Alex Brewer powering home a superb header.

Brewer struck again only a couple of minutes later, finishing off a fine Barrowmen counter-attack to turn the match on its head and put the visitors 2–1 ahead.

Charlie Pitcher extended Steyning’s lead on the hour mark, latching on to a well-judged headed flick-on to make it 3–1 and give the Barrowmen a two-goal cushion.

There was also an away debut from the bench for new signing Tosin Dada, whose arrival from Billingshurst had been announced late on Friday night.

Hastings threatened to pull a goal back, but Steyning goalkeeper Alfie Mansell produced a superb save, diving to his left.

Jesse Sentamu then rounded off an outstanding second-half display in the 90th minute, slotting past Harry Haines to make it 4–1 and ensure the Barrowmen headed home with all three points.

The victory lifts Steyning to 13th in the league table, while Hastings drop to fourth.

Both sides return to league action on Saturday – Steyning host Punjab while Hastings travel to Broadbridge Heath.

#1873. How microbes can secure the critical minerals the world needs

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Gerhard Schenk is a professor and senior research leader at the School of Chemistry and Molecular Biosciences and the Biosustainability Hub, University of Queensland, Brisbane, Australia.

Paul Evans is a research fellow at the School of Chemistry and Molecular Biosciences and the Australian Centre for Ecogenomics, University of Queensland, Brisbane, Australia.

Torben V. Borchert is the scientific director of biomanufacturing at the Novo Nordisk Foundation, Copenhagen, Denmark.

Alan Tordoir is the director of new mining technology at Mining3, Basel, Switzerland.

Susan T. L. Harrison is a professor in bioprocess engineering and deputy vice-chancellor of research and innovation at the University of Queensland, Brisbane, Australia.

Copper compounds (blue) can be extracted from solution using microorganisms — a process known as bioleaching. Credit: Dirk Wiersma/Science Photo Library

The clean-energy transition is creating a paradox. To expand renewable-energy technologies, electrify transport and build infrastructure for artificial intelligence, society must extract unprecedented quantities of minerals. Demand for many of these ‘critical minerals’ is projected to increase several-fold over the coming decades1. Yet, the technologies used to obtain them remain rooted in an old model through which single metals are extracted from virgin ore2.

The consequences are increasingly apparent (see ‘Critical-mineral supply under pressure’). As deposits of high-grade ores decline, larger quantities of rock must be mined and processed to produce the same amount of metal3. That requires more energy and water. Mining accounts for around 1.7% of global energy consumption and this number is projected to rise by up to eight-fold by 20604. Many critical-mineral projects operate in regions facing high water stress, such as arid parts of Africa and Latin America1.

Sources: Top to bottom: Ref. 3; ref. 3; ref. 6 and go.nature.com/4nzbbnx

Mining waste is growing, too. Already, hundreds of billions of tonnes of mine tailings are stored globally. Projections suggest that by 2050, up to two trillion tonnes of extra waste rock and tailings will have accumulated3,5.

Meanwhile, society is producing vast quantities of metal-rich waste that remain a mostly untapped secondary source of metals. In 2022, 62 million tonnes of electronic waste (e-waste) was produced globally — almost 8 kilograms for every person on the planet — and only around 22% of that was formally collected and recycled6.

How to widen access to the critical minerals that the world needs

How to widen access to the critical minerals that the world needs

Many discarded electronics contain valuable metals, including gold, palladium and rare-earth elements — in concentrations that can exceed those found in primary ores. However, recovering these metals remains technically challenging and is often economically unattractive using conventional approaches.

Retrieval of metals and increasing metal circularity should be seen as a strategic capability to offset the growth of metal extraction from virgin ores. Nations that can efficiently recover critical minerals from waste streams, mine residues and low-grade resources will be less exposed to geopolitical disruptions and supply-chain shocks7.

Biology offers a powerful route forwards. Although biomining — which uses microorganisms to extract metals — was once considered a niche approach, it has evolved. Driven by advances in microbial ecology, synthetic biology, structural biology, protein engineering and machine learning, the scientific foundations for a new generation of mineral biotechnologies are emerging at speed8,9. These methods offer potential levels of selectivity for extracting and recovering certain metals that are often difficult to achieve through conventional hydrometallurgical processes.

But, scientific progress alone will not transform mineral supply chains. The main obstacle is no longer a shortage of ideas. It is a lack of pathways from scientific discovery to industrial deployment. Here we outline how to develop those pathways, drawing on discussions at the International Workshop on Biomining of Critical Minerals and Elements, which was sponsored by the Novo Nordisk Foundation and held in Sitges, Spain, in September last year.

Biotechnologies have demonstrated their industrial potential for decades. Bioleaching and biooxidation processes are already established for recovering copper, nickel, gold and cobalt from ores10. They involve irrigating heaps of crushed ore or treating ground mineral powders with specialist microbes that generate chemicals, such as acids or modifiers of reduction–oxidation reactions, that selectively dissolve either target metals or other minerals found with them.

Advances in synthetic biology have expanded the range of potential applications. For example, engineered microbial systems can be designed to dissolve metals more effectively. Biomolecules (such as the protein lanmodulin) can separate rare-earth elements with yields of 99.9% in one step under conditions that are simpler than conventional techniques, using aqueous solutions rather than organic solvents8,11. AI-assisted protein design is further accelerating the discovery of macromolecules designed to selectively recognize, bind to and separate target metals from complex solutions of several elements9.

How the rush for critical minerals is neglecting human needs

How the rush for critical minerals is neglecting human needs

Collectively, these developments suggest that biotechnology could become an important component of future critical-mineral supply chains. However, many promising approaches never progress beyond being validated in the laboratory. They often stall between proof-of-concept studies and commercial demonstration, a challenge familiar throughout industrial biotechnology. Even promising technologies often struggle to attract the capital, infrastructure and industrial partnerships needed to scale them up12,13.

Barriers must be overcome. Although a few bioprocessing pilot projects exist, their capacity is insufficient to evaluate technologies across the diverse types of ore, feedstock and process conditions encountered in practice. Investors are reluctant to finance first-of-a-kind projects when it is uncertain how well they will perform in the real world.

Regulatory frameworks for emerging biomining technologies are also inadequate. They often vary across biotechnology, environmental and mining sectors and between jurisdictions. Developers might need to navigate several regulatory authorities and approval pathways, creating uncertainty and delays as technologies advance.

Electronic waste can contain higher concentrations of key metals than are found in natural ores.Credit: Martin Bernetti/AFP via Getty

In the European Union, for example, the use of genetically modified microorganisms and their environmental applications are subject to distinct regulatory frameworks. Genetically modified microorganisms are allowed to be used in contained systems, whereas those used for field applications generally rely on naturally occurring or adapted microbial strains. The United States uses a coordinated multi-agency approach, involving the Environmental Protection Agency, the Food and Drug Administration and the US Department of Agriculture.

Valuable technical knowledge (on protein engineering, mineral characterization, hydrometallurgy and economic modelling, for instance) remains dispersed across disciplines, institutions and jurisdictions. This makes it difficult to generate the necessary evidence base — including long-term continuous operating data, metrics for tracking chemical cycles and validated economic assessments — to support large-scale adoption of such technologies.

The result is a growing mismatch. Scientific advances in mineral biotechnology are accelerating, yet the mechanisms needed to deploy them are not keeping pace. Although billions of dollars are being invested to secure future supply chains for critical minerals, comparatively little attention has been devoted to building the innovation systems required to commercialize biological solutions.

If biotechnology is to contribute meaningfully to critical-mineral security, environmental sustainability and circularity of resource use, then governments, industry, development banks and philanthropic funders must move beyond supporting research alone. They must invest in the institutions that enable translation of these new technologies as well.

Countries should establish shared pilot and demonstration facilities dedicated to mineral biotechnology. Individual companies often cannot justify the risks associated with developing specialized infrastructure for technologies that remain commercially unproven. Shared facilities can help to overcome this barrier by allowing several organizations to evaluate biological processes using realistic feedstocks under industrially relevant conditions. These facilities can support both pre-commercial and competitive studies. Similar approaches have been implemented successfully in synthetic biology and bio-refining, advanced manufacturing and in the clean-energy and semiconductor sectors.

The dark side of green technology: what do electric vehicles really cost?

The dark side of green technology: what do electric vehicles really cost?

For the mineral sector, such facilities should be located near relevant resource and waste streams, including mining districts, e-waste recycling hubs and sites affected by acid mine drainage or metal-laden urban waste waters. They should have connections to universities, research labs and a skilled workforce.

Access to research and engineering expertise would enable rapid iteration, troubleshooting and integration of mineral biotechnologies with established processes. Such sites would extend beyond technology testing to generate the operational, environmental and economic data needed to inform investment decisions, regulatory approvals and commercial deployment.

Initiatives in other sectors illustrates the value of such infrastructure. In Sweden, for instance, publicly funded pilot and demonstration facilities have been set up to test processes for biochemically converting biomass under realistic conditions14.

#1872. Arsenal news: Max Dowman breaks another record on historic England appearance

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 09:17

Arsenal teenager Max Dowman made another piece of history when he represented England Under-21s on Friday night.

Despite recent criticism from Gunners boss Mikel Arteta, the 16-year-old continues to be fast-tracked for both club and country.

As well as already making 19 appearances for Arsenal's first team, the winger has made an array of appearances for England at youth level.

Dowman had already earned 13 caps for England at Under-19 level before being handed a call-up to Lee Carsley's Under-21 squad for the November international break.

That gave Dowman the chance to make history versus Portugal on Friday night.

Carsley named Dowman on the substitutes' bench for the showdown at Ashton Gate.

A first-half goal from Afonso Moreira made the difference as Portugal earned a 1-0 victory at the home of Championship club Bristol City.

However, Dowman became the youngest ever representative of England Under-21s when he was introduced as a 61st-minute substitute.

Jude Bellingham had previously held the feat for six years, having made his debut aged 17 years, two months and six days when facing Kosovo in 2020.

In comparison, Dowman featured on Friday night aged 16 years, 10 months and 13 days.

Dowman will now hope to be handed his first England Under-21s start when France are the opponents on Monday night.

As he is still serving a domestic ban, Dowman remains suspended for Arsenal's Premier League game at Newcastle United on November 21.

However, he is expected to be part of the squad for the Champions League encounter versus Borussia Dortmund on November 24.

On seven minutes Sheaf put the ball inside to Henry McDonald and he hit a shot on the turn and low. Billy Collings did well though to divert it wide.

Ethan Robb latched on to a ball in midfield and picked out Roberts on the left but after speeding down the wing his cross flew over the bar. In 17 minutes Cal Laycock found Roberts and he sped on before shooting wide from the edge of the box.

Golds’ Harry Heath was a nuisance and forced a save from Tommy Scott at his near post. Then Matthew Storm lost possession to Laycock who ran through into the box but his strike was easily saved on 27 minutes.

Benny Read – a new Rocks signing from Gosport – made a mistake as Dion Jarvis stole the ball before picking out Gaskin but with only Scott to beat, he hit it straight at the keeper.

It didn't take long for Bognor to take the lead in the second half. Read put a pass inside to Laycock and he had beaten the offside trap and turned and coolly slotted the ball into the bottom corner on 47 minutes.

Scott Faber lashed out with a challenge on Robb and went into the book on 57 minutes.

Bognor extended their lead in the 59th minute as Josh Batt lashed a loose ball into the net on the half-volley after a long free-kick by Kaya Tshaka.

On 64 minutes Bognor made a double change as Laycock and McDonald made way for Oliver Lovell and Charlie Gunson.

The Golds got a goal back directly from a corner as Gaskin headed in from a 69th minute delivery. Then Gaskin put in a dangerous ball across from the left but Lewis Olajide flashed it wide.

Jarvis blasted over as Littlehampton swung the momentum to their advantage.

Ben Anderson and Louie Williams replaced Robb and Read for Bognor in the 76th minute.

Tshaka was battling in midfeld and was unlucky to lose possession. A long ball saw Heath run powerfully into the area but Scott was quick out of his goal to bravely stop him.

Williams was booked for simulation on 87 minutes as he seemed to lost his footing in the box.

It was a real battle in the closing moments as Williams was holding up the ball for Bognor where he could. But Littlehampton posed a threat with some quick play and long throws from the dangerous Heath.

Five minutes were added but Bognor held on to move third in the division.

Chi just couldn’t get back into things and injured James Sweet was subbed for Joe Clarke. Dabre had a cut-back cut out and nice play from Will Sweet broke up a move instigated by Alonge and Odokonyero.

Joshua Hedges came on for Salisbury after the break, replacing captain Joshua Sommerton. Sweet got done by Bartolo on 47 minutes but Pashley headed away, and Evans, who had a fantastic second half, pulled off a fine save in the 49th minute.

Sivi fired one high and wide on 52 and then conceded a handball; Evans saved Dabre’s shot; and Hutchings tackled Bartolo in the box.

Bartolo made it 4-0 as we neared the hour and Jeanes came on at right-back for Pattenden with Bello pushed up.

Hedges was flagged offside on 59 minutes and Odokonyero had a good chance before Evans saved low down. The Chi No1 saved again after Chichester were ripped apart in the 64th minute, and at the other end Bello got through on goal before a well-timed tackle denied him.

Odokkonyero was swapped for Robbie Gallagher in the 68th minute and Munt replaced Moore for City. Bridle’s long-ranger didn’t trouble Henry.

The visitors cleared a Bartolo delivery and Ogunleye’s shot wasn’t far off. At the other end, Jeanes won Chichester a corner that Hutchings took and Chebby blazed over.

The hosts then brought on keeper Zak Beard in place of Henry on 85 and Hedges dragged one wide.

Bello could have shot first time and Russe had an attempt blocked in the 88th minute before Jeanes put an end to a Hedges and Gallagher move.

Dabre fluffed his lines as we entered additional time with the goal gaping before Evans made another stunning stop.
