#1866. Christian Imga: Athletic Bilbao's £75m clause after 15 clubs show interest

By Naim Beneddra | 14 Nov 2026 09:32

Athletic Bilbao have moved to protect one of their most promising young talents with a new long-term contract featuring a release clause that could eventually reach £75m, following reported interest from 15 Champions League clubs.

The player in question is Christian Imga, a 17-year-old winger whose rapid emergence from the Basque club's academy has already earned him opportunities under former Borussia Dortmund manager Edin Terzic.

Athletic confirmed on November 8 that Imga had signed a contract until June 2031, with an option for the club to extend the agreement by another season.

According to Spanish radio station Cadena SER, representatives of the youngster have revealed that as many as 15 clubs competing in the Champions League have enquired about his availability and contractual situation in recent months.

The interest reportedly prompted Athletic sporting director Mikel Gonzalez to accelerate negotiations, resulting in a considerably improved agreement designed to discourage potential suitors.

Imga's release clause is understood to increase progressively, potentially reaching €85m (£75m) towards the end of his contract, although the amount required to sign him immediately would be lower.

Imga's representatives have confirmed that the teenager's progress has attracted attention from several of Europe's leading teams, including clubs from Spain.

"There have been many clubs asking about Cristian. Many top European clubs," a representative told Cadena SER's Bilbao sports programme.

"In terms of interest, clubs asking about him and his contractual conditions, we could say 15 Champions League clubs. Almost everyone has made enquiries."

The identities of those clubs have not been disclosed, and there is no indication that Athletic have received 15 formal transfer offers.

Nevertheless, the level of attention surrounding a player who only made his senior debut last month helps explain the club's determination to secure his future.

Spanish newspaper AS reports that the release clause could rise from approximately €70m (£61m) to €85m (£75m) over the course of the agreement. Cadena SER, meanwhile, suggests that the initial figure could be closer to €60m (£52m), with the maximum amount applying if Athletic activate their option to extend the contract.

Athletic's official announcement did not disclose the financial details, but confirmed that the winger had committed his future to the club until at least 2031.

Imga arrived at Lezama from Deportivo Alaves during the 2024-25 season, having experienced a difficult final period with his former club. The youngster was left out of Alaves' youth-team plans after declining a proposed contract extension while negotiations with Athletic were taking place.

His subsequent move to Bilbao initially brought further complications, with competition regulations preventing him from immediately representing his new club's youth side.

Those setbacks have done little to slow his development.

Last season, Imga scored eight goals in 24 appearances for Athletic's Under-18s and added two more in six UEFA Youth League matches.

His performances persuaded the club to promote him directly into Bilbao Athletic, bypassing the usual intermediate step through Basconia.

Standing almost 6ft 3in, Imga is an unusually imposing winger for his age, combining his physical presence with acceleration and the ability to beat defenders in tight spaces.

Although naturally left-footed, he generally operates from the left flank and has shown the versatility to attack both the outside and inside channels.

His progress has particularly impressed Terzic, who has already begun incorporating him into Athletic's senior squad.

The teenager made his first-team debut on October 25, replacing Nico Williams during a 4-0 La Liga victory over Getafe at San Mames.

Four days later, he scored his first senior goal in the Copa del Rey against AE Prat, providing another indication of his readiness to compete above youth level.

Imga's representatives have suggested that his promotion has happened more quickly than originally anticipated because of Terzic's enthusiasm for the youngster.

"The intention was for him to play for Bilbao Athletic this season, but the manager wants to use him whenever he sees him in training," they explained to Cadena SER.

"If things are moving faster, it's because the coach likes him and the player is earning it through his performances."

The teenager has also been selected to represent Spain at the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, giving him an opportunity to continue his development on the international stage.

He is expected to divide his time between Athletic's reserve team and the senior squad during the remainder of the campaign.

With his new contract secured, Athletic can manage that progression without immediately confronting the prospect of losing him to one of the European clubs reportedly monitoring his performances.

For Imga, the next challenge is to turn his promising first appearances under Terzic into a more regular role at San Mames.

#1864. It’s agony for Worthing at Scunthorpe as 93rd minute goal denies them another away win

Jordan Young gave the away side a half-time advantage with a well-taken effort on 17 minutes, but the Rebels backline could not quitewithstand the Iron’s second half resurgence and Eastbourne-raised Norwood came up with the late leveller for new boss Andy Preece.

It was gutting for Adam Hinshelwood and his players and the manager was shown a red card at full-time. But the Rebels remain in the play-off one, in seventh place.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Returning after an 11-day break from action, the side featured two changes to the eleven that began the 3-0 defeat by Sutton United in their last league outing.

Harrison Foulkes regained his place in goal while Charlie Waller returned to the defensive unit. New signing Sam Clucas featured on the bench, with Daniel Isichei also named amongst the substitutes.

A sense of optimism among the home faithful in Preece’s first game at the helm was combatted by a strong start from the away side, spearheaded by the dynamic movement of Young to initiate some promising moves early on.

Having asserted themselves on the ball through the opening quarter of an hour, the Rebels found the breakthrough in the 17th minute. Brilliant link-up between Kendall and Young saw the latter pick up the ball in a central position just outside the box. The former Torquay United man let off a fierce low effort on his left side which clipped off the foot of Maison Campbell’s left post before nestling inside the opposite upright.

The movement of Razzaq Coleman De-Graft and Young to pick up space behind the Iron midfield gave the away side a constant outlet on the break, from which they were able to fashion several dangerous breakaways.

Scunthorpe came close to drawing level with three minutes of normal time remaining at the end of the first half. An in-swinging corner delivery was swept onto the crossbar by Kyle Hurst, before Norwood saw two follow-up attempts blocked from just outside the six-yard box.

The Rebels’ counter-attacking prowess remained their best route towards goal heading into the break, with Kendall having a good chance to double the visitors’ lead 90 seconds before the interval.

After jinking away from one challenge at the edge of the box, the forward drilled a low effort narrowly wide of the mark down to Campbell’s left-hand side.

Having grown into the game towards the end of the first 45 minutes, Preece’s hosts started the second half with renewed intensity, keeping play largely in the Worthing half as Adam Hinshelwood’s side were forced to defend their box.

Alfie Beestin had two attempts on goal, first being denied by Foulkes from a long throw before having a strike blocked from around 20 yards.

The attacking movement and nuisance of Norwood lent itself to Scunthorpe’s direct approach to getting back level, with the former Oldham striker constantly winning first balls.

Just after the hour mark, Pat Jones’ delivery from the right flank was stabbed over the bar by Norwood at the edge of the six-yard box, as tight defending from Joe Cook and Jayden Moore prevented the veteran from getting a more telling touch.

Pressure continued to mount on Worthing with minutes ticking away. With two minutes of the 90 to play, the Attis Arena was plunged into momentary silence as substitute Declan Howe’s header deflected agonisingly wide.

With 30 seconds remaining of three additional minutes, all the resolute defending from the visitors came undone as Scunthorpe found a leveller. After the away side surrendered possession inside their own half, Howe’s clipped ball towards the back post was headed back across goal and eventually poked home by Norwood.

It was a gutting conclusion from a Rebels perspective, especially for Foulkes, who commanded his box astutely through numerous waves of lofted deliveries into the area.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, it’s a meeting between the past and present of the Rossoneri. Not the first time, but it’s not not newsworthy. In fact, it’s a chance for an Italian stadium to be split between two goalkeepers.

#1861. Sharpe by name, sharp by nature: Antoine lifts Lancing to big win over Pagham

Manager Dale Hurley was proud of the Lancers performance, which he described as very efficient.The clean sheet particularly pleased him and it was no understatement for him to point out that, with a bit of luck, the goal tally could have been even higher.

The result demonstrated the progress Lancing have made since a shaky beginning to the season and they now occupy 14th place.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Lancing had a dream start, taking the lead with five minutes gone. Gabe Robinson used his pace to break clear down the right, hitting a fine low cross for Antoine Sharpe to run on to and strike against the upright. Sharpe by name, sharp by nature – he was quickest to react to the loose ball and squeeze it at across the line.

Mo Khedidji and Robinson were a constant threat to the Lions left, using their pace and close control. A tricky run by Khedidji saw him switch the ball to Robinson, who laid the ball across to Rob Deda, whose effort was narrowly high.

Deda then turned provider, winning the ball before a slide-rule pass put Khedidji into the box to finish coolly.

Sharpe was denied a clear run on goal when the referee decided to award Lancing a free-kick for a foul on Robinson, rather than allow adavantage.

The Lions were working hard to reduce the arrears .Alfie Davidson wriggled clear of Khedidji and floated in a cross that was met with a volley which cleared the bar. The Lions’ first shot on target came from Toby Hewitt but Elliot Dailly dealt with it.

The goal of the game came on 38 minutes .The ball reached Sharpe just outside the box. He allowed it to drop before volleying it out of reach of keeper Kelly and into the top corner.

The three-goal lead came close to being reduced shortly before half-time but Elliot Dailly pulled off an excellent save to preserve the three-goal margin.

Lancing inroduced Kaiden Hummerston at the restart for Deda. Lancing began where they left off with Robinson, Sharpe and Khedidji too hot for the Lions to handle and it took barely three minutes for Sharpe to sprint clear through the middle, with only the keeper to beat. A well-placed strike into the bottom corner gave the attacker his hat-trick.

Pagham threatened with a dangerous cross from the right which flew across the Lancing six-yard box but it eluded everyone.

Sharpe came close to a fourth when picked out by a sublime pass from Khedidji.He fired the ball with real venom but it rattled the underside of the bar before being cleared. This was his last meaningful action as he was given a well deserved break with Dylan Hurst coming on.

Some clever interplay between Billy McKay, Robinson and Khedidji culminated in a deep cross which proved just too high for Alek Amissah, on for Kai Birchley, to get his head to.

Robinson broke clear down the left, cut in on his right and forced a good save from Kelly.

With 71 minutes gone Lancing were in dreamland when Oliver Deda got his head to the ball at a corner to put his side five up.

Khedidji ,set up by fine pass from Ryan Plummer, executed a delicate chip which was well saved by keeper Kelly. McKay ,a real dynamo in Lancing’s midfield, made way for Dylan Walter.

The Lions were striving to salvage at least a consolation but were denied by another excellent save by Dailly and Lancing finished the stronger with a good strike from Archie McGonigle which Kelly held. In the closing minutes, a strong run from deep by Ryan Gummer saw him come close with a shot which grazed the bar.

#1860. Chelsea transfer news: Blues 'boost' in pursuit of Malo Gusto replacement

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 09:39

Chelsea have reportedly received a boost ahead of potentially making an approach for Barcelona defender Jules Kounde.

Xabi Alonso is currently focused on trying to improve the Blues' fifth-placed position in the Premier League table after the November international break.

However, with Malo Gusto said to be open-minded to an exit from Stamford Bridge during the winter transfer window, the Spaniard will assess his options in the market.

When everyone is fit, Chelsea are not short of alternatives at right-back, with Josh Acheampong, Marco Palestra and Reece James all capable of playing in that role.

Nevertheless, as per TEAMtalk, the West Londoners remain attentive to any developments at Camp Nou.

The report suggests that Barcelona will give consideration to ways to generate transfer funds at the turn of the year.

Kounde is allegedly someone who they would think about selling for the right price, while the France international is said to be aware of the situation.

Therefore, Chelsea are seemingly conscious of Kounde - a long-term target for Blues chiefs - becoming available.

He has been restricted to four starts and four substitute outings in all competitions this season, not making an appearance since October 17 due to injury.

Xavi Espart, Joao Cancelo and Brian Farinas are further right-back options for Hansi Flick, highlighting that Barcelona would not necessarily have to spend money to replace Kounde.

While most Chelsea fans would take Kounde as a direct replacement for Gusto, they would not want to add him to the squad if he is going to play ahead of Acheampong.

With the England Under-21 international having emerged as one of Chelsea's best players this season, the Blues fanbase will not want to see his development halted by Kounde.

Therefore, it is questionable whether he should be signed by Alonso, even though he provides cover at centre-back.

All things considered at this point in time, Chelsea should stay out of any race to sign Kounde.

#1857. Erling Haaland speaks out on Manchester City future as financial scandal rumbles on

Erling Haaland says he knows little or nothing about the financial scandal Manchester City are involved and is happy at the club, having signed a contract running until 2034.

In September Manchester City were found guilty of over 100 charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City were found to have artificially inflated their financial position by over £900 million from 2009-18.

The club is now appealing those guilty verdict, with a hearing taking place in December and a decision on the appeal expected in early 2027.

If the appeal is unsuccessful than punishment is likely to be severe, with points deductions and fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League a possibility.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Manchester City’s players have not said much about the situation and continue to compete, although three league defeats on the spin to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest may suggest the situation is taking its toll.

Haaland, though, says he has not even looked into the scandal much, pointing out that he was not at the club during the period of time that has been under investigation.

The 26-year-old scored in Norway’s 3-1 win over Wales on Saturday in Oslo and after successfully converting from the penalty spot, he successfully dodged the issue while speaking to TV2.

‘The investigation covered 2009 to 2018,’ he said. ‘In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2012, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don’t need the whole list…2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne’s first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

‘So this is a question I struggle to answer because it’s a legal battle…It’s a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with.

‘Am I supposed to answer that? I’m not really sure.’

The iconic striker then joked that these questions should be put to his compatriots that were at Manchester City during the time period in question.

Haaland dug out some names that only die hard Manchester City fans wil remember, saying: ‘There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think.

‘Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can’t remember.

‘But it’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t really know that much about it. I assume the answers will come… I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it.

‘To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything.’

Haaland stuck to his guns when asked about his thoughts on his future amid the ongoing appeal process.

‘I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,’ he said. ‘I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

‘I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we’re top of our group in Europe.

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 10:08

Real Madrid have reportedly identified Atletico Mineiro teenager Vitao as a potential transfer target.

Having reduced the gap to leaders Barcelona in the La Liga table to three points, Jose Mourinho will be content with his start to life back at the Bernabeu.

Furthermore, Los Blancos have improved defensively of late, now having the joint-best such record in Spain's top flight and having conceded three fewer goals than Barcelona.

However, with Antonio Rudiger now 33 years of age and Eder Militao having suffered a number of significant injuries during his career, Real Madrid may soon wish to sign younger alternatives.

According to Sport, club officials have started to assess the development of Brazilian youngster Vitao.

Despite being just 18 years of age, Vitao has already racked up 18 appearances for the Atletico Mineiro first team.

Nine of those outings have come in this season's Brazilian top flight, Vitao most notably scoring in a 3-1 win over Fluminense in September.

At 6ft 4ins and being a three-cap Brazil Under-20 international, the starlet is naturally attracting attention from Europe.

Brighton & Hove Albion are said to be considering whether to make a formal bid for Vitao during the winter transfer window.

Everton are also being linked with a player who allegedly has a €20m (£16.69m) release clause for foreign clubs in his contract.

Although Real Madrid have strength in depth at centre-back, this may be viewed as a tempting market opportunity.

Vitao has just over two years left on his contract and is seemingly destined to make the move to a European club sooner rather than later.

However, he will want to establish a suitable pathway for his development. Signing for Brighton and spending a season on loan in Belgium with Union SG may make more sense than moving to Real Madrid and being used in their Castilla squad.

#1855. CF: Instalments and repeatable bonuses – the exact figure Milan paid for Goncalo Ramos

Today, more information about the structure and cost of Goncalo Ramos’ move to AC Milan has been revealed.

It’s fair to say that Ramos’ start to life with Milan has been poor. The Portuguese striker has not scored (or assisted) as many as had been hoped from a player worth a substantial amount and it’s fair to suggest that some have been disappointed with his time at San Siro so far.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, the club will not be giving up on him anytime soon, considering he is their record arrival.

This evening, Calcio e Finanza have looked at the fee paid for Ramos – as they did for Diego Moreira recently – and picked apart both the fee, the bonuses and the structure of the payment, as MilanNews relays.

In terms of the fixed fee, the Rossoneri agreed on a deal worth €70 million, with an extra €3.1m in additional costs. This figure will be paid over the course of four years, with yearly payments scheduled on July 15 on each year – ending in July 2029 – and each payment will be worth €17.5m.

Then, there is €16m in bonuses that can be achieved, taking the total fee to almost €90m if all bonuses are achieved.

If Milan win the Scudetto, €2m will be owed; then there are several Champions League bonuses, which could be worth up to €5.2m if the Diavolo win the competition. Finally, if he is the top goalscorer in Serie A, another €2m will be owed to PSG.

These bonuses are capped at €16m and are repeatable, but they’ll only be redeemable if the Portuguese plays 60% of games in that season, unless he is the top scorer, where only the €2m will be owed.

#1854. Declan Rice fires back at Graeme Souness after criticism from Liverpool legend

Declan Rice has fired back at Graeme Souness after stinging criticism, suggesting the Liverpool legend doesn’t understand how football has changed.

Rice is an integral player for England and Premier League champions Arsenal, widely recognised as one of the best midfielders in the world.

However, Souness has his own view and is not entirely sold on the talents of the 27-year-old, who he believes plays too deep to be considered a complete midfielder.

‘How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball? In the build-up, he’s last man,’ Souness said on Piers Morgan’s Football Uncensored. ‘He’s sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He’s last man. A lot of the time, he doesn’t play in midfield.

‘It’s old man’s football. It’s cheating. An old man’s way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

He plays too deep to affect the game. I don’t think he’s got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do. He’s the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he’s back there all the time.

In 323 Premier League outings for West Ham and Arsenal, Rice has scored 25 goals and provided 35 assists.

He is yet to scored in the top flight during the current campaign, but his five assists are more than any other player in the division.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to the criticism from Souness, Rice said: ‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’

‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’

Rice pointed out that there are different requirements placed in players in the modern game, using Harry Kane’s pitch-trotting exploits as an example.

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man’s football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ he said. ‘We played him the other week [Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal] and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball.

‘The game is different now. It’s what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It’s changed a lot, and you’re always trying to look for tactical advantages.

Declan Rice hit TWO worldie free-kicks vs Real Madrid 🤯So nice he did it twice ✌️ pic.twitter.com/zg5CzlQQNh

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I’m constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He’s constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we’re now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There’s no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he’s done.

‘I didn’t get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I’ve never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’

#1853. Daily briefing: Where academic freedom is declining — and where it’s on the rise

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Hello Nature readers, would you like to get this Briefing in your inbox free every day? Sign up here.

Matthew Montgomery, the science officer of a simulated Mars mission organized by NASA, takes part in a ‘Martian’ geology project.Credit: NASA

Engineer Matthew Montgomery was one of a four-person crew who spent more than a year in a 158-square-metre, 3D-printed habitat for a simulated mission on the red planet. The hardware-engineering design consultant (and co-owner of a film production company) took charge of the hydroponic garden and participated in simulated ‘Marswalks’ wearing a protective suit. As well as dealing with a realistic 13–22-minute delay in their connection with mission control, the crew experienced a total communication blackout for two weeks.

A new artificial-intelligence tool can identify an individual bird by its song, and can be used to track that bird’s movements over time. The system provides a less invasive way to monitor birds than using physical tags. Researchers tested the model on recordings of male ovenbirds (Seiurus aurocapilla) — a species that sings individually unique songs — from more than 100 locations, and found that it could match songs to specific birds with up to 96% accuracy. “This is almost a holy grail,” says biologist Scott Sillett.

The amount that preprint platform XSci pays referees for a quick-turnaround peer review. Authors pay up to $399 for a round of review. (Nature | 10 min read)

Protecting key underground fungal networks in Mongolia could help to preserve biodiversity, boost climate resilience and revive iconic grasslands across the country, say researchers. In September, evolutionary biologist Toby Kiers and her team announced that they had found more than 500 types of fungus in networks across Mongolia, 90% of which were new to science. Mycologist Burenjargal Otgonsuren hopes that leveraging these networks could help to restore the swathes of degraded land in Mongolia — and preserve the 3,000-year-old way of life practiced by Mongolia’s 230,000 nomadic herding families.

Sources: Free to Think 2026; V-Dem Dataset (https://go.nature.com/47UZF3P)

Academic freedom is deteriorating globally, according to the Scholars at Risk (SAR) network, a human-rights organization based at New York University. Data show a steep decline in academic freedom in the United States, some of which preceded the 2024 election of President Donald Trump. But there is cautious optimism about the trend in Hungary following the end of Viktor Orbán’s 16-year premiership.

By studying people who show no signs of neurodegeneration well into older age, scientists have identified several gene variants that could help to protect against dementia. These protective variants seem to defend the brain against the toxic clusters of proteins that cause Alzheimer’s — mechanisms that scientists now hope to exploit. “Nature has already done the experiment for us: certain gene variants protect us from Alzheimer’s,” says neuroscientist Guojun Bu. “Learning how they do this could guide us to new therapies.”

The mathematics community’s reaction to OpenAI’s huge drop of AI-generated proofs last month “ranged from exhilaration to despair”, writes mathematician Ursula Martin, one of the authors of the Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics, which put forward several safeguards on the technology. “This is a moment to be clear-eyed about AI’s potential to make discoveries,” she writes. “The challenge … is to sustain the community of mathematicians on whom the discipline depends.”

Reference: Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics

Biomining strategies — those that use microorganisms to extract metals — could provide a more sustainable alternative to conventional technologies, which are struggling to keep up with soaring demand for critical minerals, argue a group of biotechnology and mining researchers. These methods can also extract metals from discarded electronics, reducing the need for virgin ores. For biomining methods to reach their potential, researchers must work with governments and industry to establish a pathway through which these technologies can be deployed at scale, the authors write.

The NASA space probe Voyager 1 is now almost one light-day away from Earth. Nearly 50 years after its launch, finding ways to conserve power on the spacecraft requires innovative thinking, says heliophysicist Jamie Rankin, deputy project scientist of the Voyager mission. (Popular Science | 6 min read)

#1852. Arsenal's Jurrien Timber lauded by Dutch media for attacking "masterclass" in Netherlands 7-0 Greece

By Ben Knapton | 14 Nov 2026 10:22

Arsenal's Jurrien Timber was the star of the show as the Netherlands demolished Greece 7-0 in Friday's UEFA Nations League affair, and the Dutch media did not hold back in their praise of the defender.

The 25-year-old has experienced a mildly frustrating start to the 2026-27 season overall, starting just three Premier League games due to his long-term groin injury and the strong form of Ben White.

Timber played the full 90 in both of Arsenal's last two top-flight wins against Liverpool and Hull City before the international break, though, and he started at left-back when the Netherlands hosted Greece, with Denzel Dumfries operating on the right.

Timber earned his shot thanks to Virgil van Dijk's withdrawal, which saw Micky van de Ven shifted into a central role, but the former Ajax man repaid Xavi's faith in him with his first two goals for his country.

Timber had failed to score in any of his first 25 Netherlands appearances, but the defender tapped home his maiden senior international goal in the 40th minute from close range, before netting his second and his country's sixth at the far stick from Dumfries's ball across.

The Arsenal man put in a "flawless" display, according to Soccernews, who awarded him a perfect 10/10 rating and also praised his two pre-assists and the "ability to play anywhere".

Mee met Oranje held off on giving Timber full marks, but the 25-year-old was nevertheless handed a 9/10 as the "most striking" player on the field, delivering an "exceptional" performance that left Greece unable to get a hold on him.

Voetbal Primeur highlighted Xavi calling Timber the "perfect joker" in the lead-up to the game and claimed that the defender fulfilled that role to perfection, while operating more like a "half number 10" when attacking.

The same outlet also handed Timber a nine out of 10 for a Nations League "masterclass", as the Netherlands moved three points clear at the top of the League A Group 2 standings.

Timber is no stranger to playing as a left-back for Arsenal, featuring there 14 times in his Gunners career, but Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie are currently battling for minutes on that side.

Calafiori in particular has embraced a free bird role at left-back, often popping up in central attacking areas, while Timber has been more widely lauded for his 1v1 defensive prowess.

However, the Dutchman has now demonstrated a Calafiori-esque strength to his play, offering Arteta an intriguing and highly useful alternative from a tactical and fitness sense.

Timber at left-back allows the Arsenal boss to rotate Gabriel Magalhaes with Calafiori and/or Hincapie, so long as White also steers clear of injury and maintains his standout form.

Timber and the Netherlands' next assignment comes away to Germany on Monday, and Xavi's side need just a point to be sure of a place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

#1851. Mauricio Pochettino sends message to Sir Alex Ferguson ahead of Man Utd mission

Mauricio Pochettino would welcome the chance to speak with Sir Alex Ferguson as he prepares for the task of resurrecting Manchester United.

Michael Carrick’s successor’s penultimate match in charge of United States ended in an emphatic 6-0 thrashing of Haiti as he moved a step closer to beginning his United tenure.

The former Tottenham boss will start life at the Red Devils on Wednesday after two Nations League matches with Haiti, but USA all but assured their place in the semi-finals of the competition with a comprehensive first-leg showing.

Austin Trusty’s smart finish from a 10th-minute set-piece ensured Pochettino’s team were ahead at half-time before they ran riot after the break with Christian Pulisic able to net a brace either side of goals from Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun ahead of Tuesday’s second leg.

Pochettino paid tribute to his staff and players in an emotional press conference on Friday and duly watched USA romp to a 6-0 victory.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We played for him,’ Trusty said in a post-match interview with TNT Sports after opening the scoring in the 10th minute.

‘Obviously, he’s our gaffer. Obviously it’s sad that he’s moving on. It’s a great opportunity that he’s moving on to. But we played for him. It’s his team. It’s his identity, and the mindset is to win every single game, every single match.’

The second leg of the Nations League quarterfinals will take place Tuesday in Cincinnati.

‘Pochettino is an amazing manager and he added a lot to us with the national team,’ Folarin Balogun told TNT Sports. ‘It’s always sad to see a top coach leave but it’s a part of the sport.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The 54-year-old will have little time to reflect on his accomplishments in his soon-to-be former role as he will immediately begin plotting for his first game in charge of United at Anfield next Sunday.

Pochettino inherits a side that is currently in the bottom three in the Premier League table, short on confidence and a dressing room split following the recent actions of senior players, including the likes of Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez.

Given the current state of play and his pre-existing relationship with Ferguson, it is perhaps no surprise that Pochettino is seeking the advice of the club’s greatest ever manager as he prepares to embark on arguably the toughest assignment of his managerial career to date.

‘Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,’ Pochettino told Telegraph Sport when asked if he had been in contact with Ferguson.

‘I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

‘For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense.

‘But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.’

#1850. Wigan Athletic 2 Barnsley 1: Keeping the faith is tough as Reds hit new low

Barnsley were the ones left dishevelled and on the floor by the end.

A single-digit points haul by the second half of November, their season is currently in pieces. Fifty points seems a long way off.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

These lot will give you a chance is the sentence that every opposing League One manager must surely utter when talk turns to Barnsley.

A well-meaning, nice group of boys who say - and hope to do - the right things, Barnsley don’t last the course, unfortunately.

You don't have to play particularly well to beat them and that is a considerable worry.

They have been in most games this season, but eventually err.

Concentration, physicality and sensing danger are all areas where this group are deficient. A disturbing cocktail. They don’t handle pressure, quite simply and their game management is lamentable.

Barnsley have lost their last five away league matches. Their concession of 17 goals in the second half of games is the joint-worst record in the third tier.

The 23rd-placed Reds, only kept off the bottom by goal difference, are winless in nine league matches since September 2. Autumn, certainly on the league front, has been appalling.

Ahead of kick-off, the Monkees "I’m a Believer" got an airing on the Wigan jukebox. Bob Marley’s classic “Three Little Birds” - a song beloved of Barnsley - did the rounds at the final whistle as Wigan escaped the relegation zone after showing the savvy.

Barnsley should be worried about a number of things, for sure.

As is their manager. Keep the Faith is the motto of the Northern Soul movement - another thing associated with Wigan.

Daniel Stendel was clearly struggling on that count in the immediate aftermath of events on Saturday.

He spoke about holding discussions with Reds majority shareholder/chairman Neerav Parekh. Not necessarily about his own position - not yet, anyway - but endeavouring to find ways to support a playing squad who plainly need help.

It was all a bit unclear. It wasn't to do with bringing in more free agents either.

Then what was it? Discussing what Barnsley need to do in the January transfer window should be top of the agenda. Even if it feels some way in the distance.

Make no mistake, if the Oakwell outfit get the winter window wrong, then there is a pretty high chance that they will be playing fourth-tier football next season for the first time since 1978-79 unfortunately.

‘Probably as good a place as we’ve been’, was Gary Caldwell’s pre-match take on Wigan’s mood ahead of this one.

In fairness, his Barnsley counterpart - in his second spell at the club much like the Scot - could have said the same on the back of two healthy cup wins. The league is a different matter, alas.

It was the former whose side would build momentum.

A relatively even first half had one key moment.

Fraser Murray had delivered a warning with his sweet curler producing a full-stretch parry from Ceiran Slicker.

A few minutes later, the Reds custodian had no chance when Murray again showed delicious technique to bend an unstoppable low shot into the far corner, for his first goal of the campaign. An important one.

How the ball arrived at his feet, with Wigan afforded an ocean of space in the middle of the pitch was poor from a Reds perspective. Latics also fancied it out wide against both Ziyad Larkeche and Jubril Okedina.

On the resumption, Barnsley found a much-needed lifeline in front of their admirable band of stoic supporters. Luca Connell found Reyes Cleary - who worried Wigan for most of the afternoon.

He expertly manufactured space before fizzing over a superb low cross which was buried by Cam McGeehan, backing up in the box.

It was classic wing-play from Cleary to present an opportunity on a plate for McGeehan, who struck his ninth goal of the campaign.

Barnsley had their tails up, but - all the while - there was a nagging feeling about what might happen at the other end. The fears were borne out in appalling fashion.

Morgan Fox hung up a cross which was attacked by Jensen Weir. Larkeche, having a poor game, challenged meekly and Weir couldn’t believe his luck.

His header caught Slicker by surprise at the near post as he could only pat the effort into the net, horribly. And that was that. A scruffy concession in a bedraggled season. Sheffield Wednesday next.

Wigan Athletic: Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett (Trevitt 68), Weir, Power, Mellish; Burrowes (Miller 87), Murray; Saydee (Hogan 67). Substitutes unused: J Walsh, Chilokoa-Mullen, A Harris, Higgins.

Barnsley: Slicker; Okedina, Gale, Kay, Larkeche (Reid 87); Connell, Johnson (Richards 56); Yoganathan, McGeehan (Noslin 82), Cleary; Kirk (Brownlie 56). Substitutes unused: Ravenhill, Smith, Alker.

Slovakia square off against Kazakhstan on Monday having already secured top spot in Group C3 of the UEFA Nations League.

In sharp contrast to the visitors earning promotion with a game to spare, Kazakhstan must win this fixture to have any chance of avoiding finishing bottom of the group.

Ranked highest in the FIFA World Rankings, Slovakia were the clear favourites to win this group, and Vladimir Weiss's side have delivered.

Despite failing to win either match against Faroe Islands, scoring eight goals across victories in the other games has given them a four-point lead with one fixture left.

On a negative note, Slovakia have only kept clean sheets versus Moldova, something which will serve as added motivation for his contest.

Although they came from behind to earn a 2-2 draw at home to Faroe Islands on Friday, Slovakia extended their unbeaten record in all competitions to eight games.

Meanwhile, Slovakia have scored at least two goals in all but one of those encounters.

As for Kazakhstan, they have now gone seven matches without recording a win, their last success coming against Comoros on March 31.

Like their next opponents, failing to emerge victorious from either fixture versus Faroe Islands was a major disappointment, but they have not helped themselves with red cards in the last two games.

John van 't Schip's team went down 2-1 in Moldova on Friday, ending their hopes of finishing in the top two.

However, victory on Monday would keep them in the hunt of finishing third, with Faroe Islands also needing to lose to Moldova to keep their chances alive.

Kazakhstan have scored and conceded in each of their last seven games.

Having lost out to a 77th-minute goal on Friday, Van 't Schip may be against making many changes to his Kazakhstan XI.

However, Sergey Maliy has served a one-match ban and could replace Temirlan Erlanov in the middle of the back three.

Yan Vorogovskiy may get the nod over Nauryzbek Zhagorov at left wing-back, a result of replacing him at half time versus Moldova.

Slovakia will make a change at right-back with Martin Valjent serving a one-match ban for an accumulation of yellow cards.

Tobias Paliscak is in line to come into the team, while Weiss will consider making further alterations with top spot secured.

Centre-back Ivan Mesik, centre-midfielder Matus Bero and forward Robert Bosenik could all b handed opportunities.

#1845. Di'Shon Bernard goal points to Sheffield Wednesday tweak that can up entertainment levels

Despite the 3-0 scoreline over Plymouth Argyle, Challinor's first league game as Owls manager only really delivered on the first front.

But it would be unreasonable to expect an instant transformation, especially with injuries forcing players into unfamiliar positions.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

After six games without a win and cup defeats in Challinor's first two matches, Wednesday just needed to get over the line.

But on an afternoon where the football never rivalled Plymouth's orange away kit for brightness, one moment really stood out.

It was born of a mistake, Di'Shon Bernard failing to find Keillor-Dunn after winning the ball deep in Wednesday territory.

But when Malachi Boateng's interception turned into a one-two and the centre-back drove into shooting range and scored in off a post.

The game already won by Keillor-Dunn's finish two minutes earlier, it was no more than the cherry on the cake, six games into Bernard’s return from a 19-month knee injury.

But the story of Henrik Pedersen's tenure was clear – excited by the potential of David Storch’s ownership, Owls fans are greedy. They do not just want the cake, they want the cherries too. After the thin gruel of last season, who can blame them?

"I want people to be brave," said Challinor. "If the shot goes into the Kop, so be it. I'll always encourage people to make positive decisions.

"They're going to make mistakes. We're going to ask them to do things that are different.

"Of course we'll get frustrated, but that's acceptable. That's on us and that will always be the case."

Wednesday's shape flitted between a 4-2-3-1 and a 3-2-4-1 when Sil Swinkels tucked from left-back into a more familiar position.

Back threes need a player willing to break out, especially on days – not Saturday, in fairness – when the visitors come to S6 to frustrate.

"We should, if we do things right, come up against more blocks and teams getting men behind the ball,” argued Challinor.

"That's when people need to step in, be positive and make the most of opportunities. That comes from backing yourself, and quality."

Bernard, a team-mate of Marcus Rashford in the Manchester United youth ranks, has that.

"He wants to put his body on the line," commented Challinor. "He got injured at Notts County by blocking a shot and opening his knee up.

"There's loads of work we can do with him, he can get so much better.

"We'll ask him to be better and more positive in possession as well as being able to do the other things."

When pressed into giving the ball up in the 37th minute he got back to kill the move when it came into the penalty area. When Xavier Amaechi threatened to force his way through, Bernard refused to be shaken off and made an excellent recovery tackle.

He believes working with Challinor and his assistant Clint Hill – more no-nonsense centre-backs in their day – can elevate his game.

"Playing the right of a three he's trusting me to do more on the ball," he says. "Before I got injured, that was probably one of my strengths.

"Now I need to really just build up the confidence to do more of it because you can see in glimpses I am capable of it.

"He's pushing me to be that player and I'm grateful him and his staff have shown that's what I need to do."

For the 80 minutes before those two goals in two minutes there was not a great deal to write home about.

The fizzing atmosphere Challinor was looking forward to after only tasting Hillsborough-lite in the EFL Trophy was flat for an hour because Wednesday's football was.

Although they were fortunate Roman Curtis' chest high tackle on Jamal Lowe only got a yellow card, Plymouth should have gone in at half-time multiple goals up.

Instead, when Bernard's goalbound header was nodded over at the end of the first half, Billy Mitchell’s deflected shot from the corner brought his first goal since 2021.

The second half was more even but Hillsborough helped its team over the line.

Having missed an easy chance from a quick throw-in, Keillor-Dunn poked home the loose ball at a badly-defended free-kick and at 2-0 the contest was over.

But the mouth-watering bit was still to come.

Sheffield Wednesday: Lumley; Valery, Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels; Mitchell, Heskey; Slattery, Bannan (Barry 72), J Lowe (Palmer 85); Keillor-Dunn (Gray 85).

Unused substitutes: Santos, Trueman, Weaver, Thornton.

Plymouth Argyle: Cooper; Harding, MacKenzie (Irow 63), Hartridge; Curtis, Boateng, White (Oseni 77), Ross; Amaechi, Ibrahim (Watts 63); Evans.

Unused substitutes: Storer, Campbell, Mwaro, Maund.

​The misses: Plymouth spurned some great chances, Xavier Amaechi horribly failing to make contact with a ball in from Bradley Ibrahim, then heading a great second-half chance from a Alex Hartridge cross wide. Earlier, Will Evans cushioned a volley into the side netting when Joe Lumley’s flapping at a corner left the goal gaping.

Star performers: Di’Shon Bernard was excellent but so too was midfielder Billy Mitchell, the stand-out Owls player in a first half where they were well below par.

Run over: This was the first time in eight league games Hillsborough’s attendance had officially fallen below 30,000 – though only by 772. The football did not lift them in the first half but they took it upon themselves to inspire the players around the hour.

#1844. Mauricio Pochettino faces grim Man United relegation statistic

By Naim Beneddra | 14 Nov 2026 11:33

Mauricio Pochettino will inherit a Manchester United side facing a worrying historical relegation precedent, with 41.5% of Premier League teams who collected eight points from their opening 10 matches ultimately going down.

The Argentine was confirmed as United's new head coach on Friday, replacing Michael Carrick after a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign left the Red Devils 18th in the Premier League.

United have managed just one victory in their opening 10 league fixtures, collecting eight points despite finishing third last season and returning to the Champions League.

According to an analysis published by Opta Analyst on November 10, 41 teams have recorded exactly eight points after 10 Premier League games since the competition's creation in 1992.

Of those, 17 were relegated at the end of the season, representing a rate of 41.5%.

The figures underline the scale of Pochettino's challenge, although the historical percentage should not be confused with United's actual probability of relegation this season.

1 - Manchester United's eight points after 10 games are their fewest in a league season at this stage since 1986-87 (also eight), the season Alex Ferguson arrived as manager in November. Poch? https://t.co/hvyVWQ2vja

Opta's research offers a sobering comparison for a club that has not played outside the English top flight since the 1974-75 season.

Of the 10 most recent teams to collect exactly eight points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, four were subsequently relegated.

Southampton suffered that fate in 2022-23, finishing bottom with 25 points, while Swansea City went down in 2017-18 after collecting 33 points.

Norwich City in 2013-14 and Wolverhampton Wanderers in 2011-12 also failed to recover from similarly poor starts.

There is some encouragement for United, with the other 24 clubs in the wider historical sample ultimately retaining their Premier League status.

Nevertheless, the latest Opta supercomputer projections before Carrick's dismissal suggested that United's risk of relegation had risen substantially.

The model gave the Red Devils a 20.9% chance of going down, compared with just 3.6% before the season began.

That represents almost a sixfold increase, although the simulations were conducted before Pochettino's appointment and do not account for any potential improvement under the new manager.

United's underlying results offer little reassurance.

They have scored 14 league goals but conceded 19, leaving them with a goal difference of minus five. Their dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last weekend, rescued by two stoppage-time goals, was another illustration of their defensive difficulties.

The club's current position also carries historical significance.

Before this month, United had not ended a day in the relegation zone beyond August since October 1986, shortly before Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson.

They spent 28 consecutive days in the bottom three during that campaign, eventually finishing 11th in Ferguson's first season.

With the international break keeping United out of action until November 22, their current spell in the relegation zone is guaranteed to last at least 15 days, their longest such run since 1986.

Pochettino's appointment has offered United a potential turning point, but the 54-year-old faces an exceptionally demanding introduction.

The former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager will officially take charge on November 18 after completing his remaining commitments with the United States national team.

His first match will be against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, November 22, leaving him little time to work with his new squad.

United could even begin that fixture at the bottom of the Premier League, depending on results involving Sunderland and Crystal Palace earlier in the weekend.

More significantly, remaining in the relegation zone after the 11th round of fixtures would represent another unwanted milestone.

According to Opta, United have not occupied a relegation position this late into a top-flight season since November 1986, when Ferguson was beginning his legendary managerial tenure.

Pochettino will therefore have an immediate opportunity to change the direction of United's campaign, although his appointment has already raised questions about the scale of the rebuilding task.

The Argentine arrives with a reputation for developing young players and building aggressive, high-intensity teams, qualities United highlighted when announcing his appointment.

However, the immediate priority will be restoring defensive stability and converting the team's attacking output into victories.

United have another 28 Premier League matches remaining, giving their new manager sufficient time to move the club away from danger.

The historical numbers provide a reminder of how damaging their opening 10 games have been, but the more immediate challenge is clear: Pochettino must deliver an improvement quickly enough to prevent a difficult start from becoming a genuine relegation battle.

#1843. How Harrogate Town banished ghosts of Carlisle United with 4-0 rout of Altrincham - analysis

When Altrincham defender Reuben Lopata-White lunged in on Harrogate Town winger Ellis Taylor, there will have been two shivers down the spines of the home supporters.

The first one being the natural one, brought on by the reckless nature of the loaned-out Leeds United prospect’s foul. The second will have been prompted by the dawning realisation of what comes next.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Harrogate have not had the best of times against 10-man sides and lost 3-0 to a Carlisle United side who saw two men sent off less than three weeks ago.

Halloween has been and gone, but the ghosts of Carlisle threatened to haunt when the red card was brandished on the 13-minute mark.

“I think everyone in the stadium thought that [it was going to be a struggle],” said Harrogate boss Simon Weaver. “[Altrincham] probably, ultimately, were buoyed by the fact that it didn't go our way the last time.

“It's not a case of sulking and berating everyone when it just didn't work on that occasion, but are we capable of next time, especially against a really good team like Altrincham, carrying out our roles a bit better?”

To say Harrogate carried out their roles a bit better would be an understatement. The strong Sulphurite grip on the game rarely loosened as they cruised to an emphatic 4-0 win.

It took until the second half but once the hosts started firing on all cylinders in the final third, the afternoon raced away from the Robins.

Will McGowan drew first blood shortly after the restart and Morgan Williams pounced merely 10 minutes later.

Pressure continued to be applied and the advantage was built upon by Michael Craig and Rohan Vaughan, who both hammered home thunderous strikes.

Ellis Taylor may not have etched his name on the scoresheet but the Marcy Fitness Stadium became his playground, one in which he toyed with defenders with relative ease.

“We still had to be very patient,” said Weaver. “[We had] to really break through and put the game to bed.

“We did in the end and that's what mattered and a growing maturity I thought the lads showed today.

“You’ve got to kill off the hope, kill off the energy and psychologically I think the best way of doing it is to keep the ball and keep probing and not get flustered ourselves.”

Boreham Wood have steamed away at the top of the National League table but it remains early days. Harrogate reduced the gap between the sides to 10 points and will be keen to keep chipping away.

As for the ghosts of Carlisle - consider them banished.

“I think we've got a really good, honest group,” said Weaver. “There’s blips on the journey of every team but 18 new players and people are handling disappointments well, people aren't getting over the top or egotistical when we bang a few goals in.

“They want to play and they want to play in the right way but not play boring football. We’ve got a proud record at home.”

#1839. Faroe Islands vs Moldova - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 11:45

Faroe Islands play host to Moldova on Monday night looking for the win that would see them finish in second place in Group C3 of the UEFA Nations League.

However, the visitors only require a draw to ensure that they qualify for the promotion playoffs.

Having been promoted from League D in 2024-25, Moldova would have been targeting consolidation at this level for 2026-27.

However, Lilian Popescu's side are on the brink of sealing second place behind Slovakia.

Two 2-1 victories over Kazakhstan, the second of which was recorded on Friday, has ultimately proven to be the difference thus far.

Despite conceding six goals without reply versus Slovakia, a draw will be enough to earn a spot in the promotion playoffs.

Moldova head into this fixture having failed to keep a clean sheet in 20 matches, their last shutout coming in Andorra two years to the day of this game.

Meanwhile, Faroe Islands possess the unusual record of posting five successive draws in this group.

Three 1-1 scorelines in a row have been followed by back-to-back 2-2 draws versus Kazakhstan and Slovakia.

Eydun Klakstein's side now have the opportunity to secure a place in the promotion playoffs with a win on Monday.

Since a 3-1 defeat in Croatia 12 months ago, Faroe Islands have only suffered one defeat in nine games, that coming by a 1-0 scoreline in Estonia.

Meanwhile, Croatia are the only nation to beat Faroe Islands in Torshavn in more than three years.

Faroe Islands will make a change at right wing-back, a consequence of Joannes Danielsen serving a one-match ban.

Jann Benjaminsen is in line to deputise in that role, while the likes of Poul Kallsberg, Joannes Bjartalid and Adrian Justinussen are alternatives having been introduced as substitutes in Slovakia.

Meanwhile, Moldova centre-back Iurie Iovu is suspended for this contest, which should lead to Mihail Stefan starting in the back three.

However, captain Vladyslav Baboglo will be assessed after being withdrawn during the latter stages versus Kazakhstan.

Petru Popescu scored both goals against Kazakhstan, taking him to four goals in nine games for the national team.

#1838. California votes to give record $8.4 billion to medical research

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Students, researchers and others at the University of California, Los Angeles, have protested over cuts to science funding made by the administration of US President Donald Trump during the past two years.Credit: Robyn Beck/AFP via Getty

Voters in California have approved US$8.4 billion in funding for immunology research — the largest ever infusion of cash for science authorized by a public vote in US history.

The funding proposal, known as Proposition 38, appeared on the ballot for voters in California in last week’s US mid-term elections, but it has taken nearly a week for officials to count enough ballots to declare it a success. The state government will pay for the research — which aims to find treatments that harness or re-engineer the body’s immune system to fight illnesses such as cancer and Alzheimer’s disease — by selling state government bonds. (This is unusual for science funding. Bonds are typically reserved to pay for infrastructure projects such as road construction and require the state to pay back its debt with interest.)

‘Historic change’: what the 2026 US mid-term election results mean for science

‘Historic change’: what the 2026 US mid-term election results mean for science

Supporters of the proposal say that the funding will provide stability for researchers in California, who have been affected by political turmoil. The administration of US President Donald Trump has pushed for massive cuts to science funding; put political appointees in charge of grant decisions at federal science agencies such as the US National Institutes of Health; and forced policy change at US universities that receive federal funding, including those in California.

The $8.4 billion “is an advantage to California that is unprecedented”, says Antoni Ribas, a cancer researcher and physician at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), who supported Proposition 38. It will make the state “even more of a global hub for immunology research”.

But the proposal has sparked debate. That’s because it calls for about half of the funding to be given directly to research institutes — and the only institute that matches the criteria called for in the proposal is one co-founded by Gary Michelson, a billionaire medical-device inventor. He wrote the proposition and donated about $45 million of his own funds to get it placed on the ballot and to campaign for its passage.

“I feel like the voters have been taken advantage of,” says Sarah Hill, a political scientist at California State University in Fullerton, who tracks the state’s ballot measures. Michelson did not respond to Nature’s request for comment before this story was published, but has said elsewhere that he will not personally profit from the bond revenue.

In California, citizens can place proposed laws directly on the election ballot by collecting hundreds of thousands of voter signatures.

The state has funded scientific research through this process before. In 2004, after then president George W. Bush restricted federal funding for human embryonic stem-cell research, voters in California approved a $3-billion bond to establish the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine, which they then voted to replenish with another $5.5 billion in 2020.

A campaign mailer encouraging California voters to support Proposition 38.Credit: Smith Collection/Gado/Getty

“The model works,” Ribas says. Immunologists have been making great strides with medicines such as personalized treatments called CAR-T therapies, which are revolutionizing care, he says. There has also been a flurry of research into developing vaccines, including the mRNA shots that have been the target of funding cuts by the Trump administration. Proposition 38 will ensure that such research can continue regardless of the political headwinds, Ribas adds.

Around $4 billion from Proposition 38 will fund grants for researchers at select public universities and non-profit institutes in California through a competitive review process. According to the proposal, any commercialized therapies developed through funded research must be sold at a 20% discount to people in California, with 10% of drug royalties returning to the state’s general fund.

#1837. Ian Wright praises ‘magnificent’ Arsenal star after England beat Spain

Ian Wright praised ‘magnificent’ Arsenal defender Ben White after England’s thrilling Nations League win over World Cup holders Spain.

England ended Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday evening.

The Three Lions were bright from the start and took the lead on the stroke of half-time through a penalty from England record goalscorer and Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

Ezri Konsa headed in Declan Rice’s corner shortly after the interval and England were in dreamland when White added a third on the hour mark, arriving at the back-post and firing past Unai Simon.

Spain were being outplayed but had renewed hope when Elliot Anderson was sent off for bringing down Lamine Yamal as he raced through on goal and Mikel Oyarzabal converted the subsequent penalty.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

England fans were having flashbacks of last summer’s World Cup semi-final collapse against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second to set up a tense final 20 minutes.

The hosts pressed for an equaliser but were denied by some valiant England defending and an impressive display from goalkeeper James Trafford.

The hard-fought win means England, already through to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, finish top of their group ahead of World Cup holders Spain.

Wright felt England ‘deserved’ the win despite the late pressure from Spain and singled out Arsenal star White for special praise.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

White was part of England’s World Cup group in Qatar four years ago but left Gareth Southgate’s squad for personal reasons.

He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Southgate’s reign, a decision that has led to him being booed by some England fans in recent games.

‘Can I just say, I’m really pleased for Ben White and the way things have turned around for him,’ Wright said on ITV.

‘It’s just brilliant for him to get back in and he was magnificent tonight. Not just with the goal but he was making tackles, niggling the Spain players. I’m so pleased it’s ended that way for him.

"This England team are RUNNING RIOT in Spain" 🤩👀 They lead the World Cup winners by 3-0 in Madrid!! WOW. pic.twitter.com/2GuDnscRb4

‘There was a lot to be excited about for England. They were 3-0 up and cruising against the world champions before the red kind of changed the game.’

Meanwhile, Arsenal midfielder Rice said the England squad ‘knew’ they were going to end Spain’s two-year unbeaten run.

‘We knew we were going to beat them tonight,’ he said on ITV. ‘The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive.

‘The first 10 minutes was the best we’ve played. Overall 10 men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against a team unbeaten in 43 is massive.

‘Argentina that day [at the World Cup] wasn’t meant to be. That’s football. When they [Spain] got a second maybe it could have gone another way. It’s a massive win.’

Blown away in Braga on Sunday as they slumped to that shock 4-1 drumming against Denmark, Portugal will be searching for an immediate Nations League response here. Nevertheless, already cruising their way to a knockout stage ticket, Jesus’ superstar squad have their sights set on defending their Nations League crown. Opening proceedings with a 1-0 victory against the Dragons back on September 24th, Portugal will be looking to exploit a Wales squad who have already accepted they will finish rock-bottom of the League A standings.

#1835. Nottingham Forest transfer news: Igor Jesus 'takes stance' over future amid winter exit talk

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 12:29

Igor Jesus reportedly has no plans to leave Nottingham Forest in order to return to Brazil.

In the summer of 2025, Forest paid a fee allegedly in the region of £10m to sign the attacker from Botafogo.

A total of 17 goals and five assists have been contributed across 59 appearances in all competitions, the Brazil international having already justified his transfer fee.

However, he remains with just seven goals and four assists in 43 Premier League outings, while just one strike has come in six such games in 2026-27.

With Liam Delap seemingly viewed as Oliver Glasner's first-choice forward, it has raised questions over Jesus's future at the City Ground.

According to Sport Witness, the 25-year-old has no intention of returning to Brazil anytime soon.

Jesus is said to be prioritising remaining in the Premier League, even if he is seemingly not in line for guaranteed starts with Forest.

Former club Botafogo and Flamengo are said to be monitoring the situation, albeit aware that Jesus has a contract with the East Midlands outfit until 2029.

The player's representatives are also of the opinion that he should stay in the Premier League for the foreseeable future.

As per ESPN Brazil, Forest would demand in excess of £33m if any teams expressed serious interest in Jesus.

A calf injury has prevented Jesus from featuring in four of Forest's last five games, his solitary outing since September 19 coming from the substitutes' bench against Manchester City before the November international break.

He has not played more than 31 minutes in a single game since August 29, emphasising that he has dropped down the pecking order.

However, he has only had the chance to play two games since scoring the winner against Aston Villa on September 12.

Providing that he stays fit, Jesus should earn regular minutes after the November international, but Delap's double versus Man City means that he can only expect to appear from the substitutes' bench in the short term.

#1834. Switzerland vs Scotland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 14 Nov 2026 12:30, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 16:17

Switzerland welcome Scotland to Berit Sitterstadion on Monday night for a matchday six clash in UEFA Nations League League B Group 1.

The hosts have already secured top spot heading into the final game, while the visitors are still battling to finish second and in the promotion playoff place.

Switzerland have bounced back from the heartbreak of their 2026 World Cup quarter-final elimination in superb style during the 2026-27 Nations League campaign.

Murat Yakin's side have won four and drawn one of their five Group 1 matches so far, leaving them comfortably at the top of the table with 13 points - five ahead of second-placed Slovenia.

Switzerland, as a result of their five-point lead with one game remaining, have already secured top spot and their promotion to League A for the next edition of the UEFA Nations League.

Regardless of their success, Yakin will want to see his side remain unbeaten across the entire group stage and secure another three points against Scotland on Monday.

The hosts have already proven their dominance over Scotland in the reverse fixture, winning 3-0 at Hampden Park on matchday two - marking one of four clean sheets they have recorded in the group stage.

Switzerland have also been particularly dangerous going forward, scoring 11 goals in their five matches, although they did fail to find the net for the first time in a 0-0 draw with Slovenia earlier in the November international break.

Scotland, meanwhile, head into Monday's encounter with plenty more at stake, as Sebastien Pocognoli's side remain in the race to secure a second-placed finish and the chance to earn promotion to League A.

Pocognoli, who took charge after long-serving boss Steve Clarke stood down following the disappointment of Scotland's World Cup, has recorded two wins, one draw and two defeats in his first five matches at the helm.

Scotland, consequently, place third in the league and trail second-placed Slovenia by one point going into the final matchday, meaning Pocognoli's side must win and Slovenia draw or lose against North Macedonia if Scotland are to secure second in the group.

Although Scotland lost 3-0 to Switzerland in the reverse fixture, Pocognoli's side have shown significant signs of improvement since that defeat, scoring all of their five goals in the following three matches.

Scotland have also remained undefeated on the road in League B Group 1 so far, recording one win and one draw, keeping back-to-back clean sheets.

Scotland also boast a better record in this fixture than Switzerland, winning eight and losing six of their 18 encounters, although they have failed to win any of their last three clashes.

Switzerland are without Johan Manzambi after the midfielder left the squad due to a calf issue, meaning Fabian Rieder is likely to start in attacking midfield once again.

After failing to score against Slovenia, Yakin could make changes elsewhere in attack, meaning Dan Ndoye and Breel Embolo could be joined by Zeki Amdouni.

Further back, Denis Zakaria and Remo Freuler should remain at the base of midfield, with Manuel Akanji and Nico Elvedi in central defence.

As for Scotland, after securing an important 2-1 win against North Macedonia, Pocognoli could name an unchanged starting 11 against Switzerland.

John McGinn scored a brace in that game, and the attacking midfielder could continue alongside Scott McTominay and behind Che Adams in the front three.

Kobel; Athekame, Elvedi, Akanji, Britschgi; Freuler, Zakaria; Ndoye, Rieder, Amdouni; Embolo

Gunn; Porteous, Graham, Tierney; Doak, Ferguson, Gilmour, Robertson; McGinn, McTominay; Adams

Scotland may have more at stake but Switzerland have been the dominant force in League B Group 1, and we expect their unbeaten run to continue with another win here.
