#1833. The Brugge issue and a familiar backstory: Why the Tresoldi deal is becoming off-putting

Recently, it’s felt like AC Milan have been set on signing Nicolo Tresoldi in the winter. It may be the easy option, but is it the right one?

At a time when Milan are doing the PR side of things almost perfectly, Tresoldi feels like another easy win. It seems increasingly likely that Francesco Camarda departs in the winter mercato, so why not replace him with another Milanista?

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Replace the boy who was destined to become king with another who seems further down the career line. He’s already scored a senior goal – or three – at San Siro and he’s got attention from all of Europe’s best clubs. However, if the Rossoneri came knocking, would he be able to say no to his boyhood club?

Well, here is the alternative view: maybe they shouldn’t knock at all.

Now, it’s unpopular to suggest that Tresoldi isn’t the right man, but stick with us here, especially after reports today. If you’ve not seen, Club Brugge have made a statement in the Belgian outlet Het Laatste Nieuws that they won’t be selling him in January.

It’s a ‘club policy’ and even for €60-70 million, he won’t be leaving Belgium. We’ve seen these kinds of statements become pointless in the past and this could become one of them. However, that’s not really the important thing here.

Instead, it’s that Tresoldi has now entered a new bracket. €50m in January is steep, but it’s workable. Ultimately, we’re not in record-breaking territory. Taking that €10-20m step upwards, though, that’s where we enter that territory. There’s also a possibility that more would be needed, too.

It’s a figure that Gerry Cardinale may not be afraid to spend. In fact, reports would have you believe that he really loves Tresoldi and sees him as a perfect addition to a strong frontline roster. However, that’s a lot of money on two strikers in one season.

Then, you’ve also got negotiations with Brugge to deal with. Historically, the Diavolo have found it difficult to close deals with them and with Tresoldi, it’ll be harder than ever, especially after the Ardon Jashari situation.

With the figures being discussed too, you can only imagine how small the margins will be.

Then, you have maybe the most difficult factor. Tresoldi, taking romanticism out of it, has only performed in, with respect, sub-tier leagues. Now, that’s not to take away from his records; scoring-wise, he’s been phenomenal and he’s matched it in the Champions League.

However – and it’s a big however – we’ve already seen that it doesn’t always translate. For example, look at Charles De Ketelaere, but that’s not the real parallel here.

Here, we head to the parallel. In the summer just gone, Milan hired a new Portuguese coach, who initially faced a few questions. After an up-and-down first half of the season, they find themselves in need of a statement January window and stumble upon a boyhood fan of the Rossoneri.

Said fan is banging goals in for fun in a league outside of Europe’s top five, but there’s no need to panic as he’s performing in the Champions League, even against the biggest teams. So, the Rossoneri make the plunge.

Six months later, they try to sell him and a year after that, he’s on loan at Porto, with an €18m buy clause sitting in his deal, unlikely to be touched. Of course, that’s Santiago Gimenez.

There are differences between them, of course, but the formula has already been tried and the results speak for themselves. Trying it again, whilst enticing for the same romantic reasons as Gimenez’s arrival, may not be the answer.

Yes, Gimenez had issues with selection and injuries and eventually, both together. Nevertheless, even without these problems, it was a rushed deal and the Diavolo are going to be the ones paying for that rush next season.

The point here isn’t to discredit the Mexican, but rather suggest that rushing to sign a romantic connection isn’t always the best way to spend big money. It’s about balance, which is why another striker signing like Nicolas Füllkrug wouldn’t be ideal.

Denying that Tresoldi could become a great would be naive, but it would also be as bad to ignore the reasons why the deal is becoming more of a gamble. At €50m, it makes sense, but we’re entering an echelon of deals that requires serious consideration.

In January, Milan would probably have to spend upwards of €70m and that wouldn’t guarantee them Champions League football. Nothing really will offer complete assurances in football; few things – if anything – are guaranteed. Yet, for that fee, it would be expected and you’re still not really addressing the issues within the squad completely.

To do that, Cardinale would have to spend at least another €30-40m to satisfy the fanbase and that’s unreasonable halfway through a season.

So, diversifying the money across the team and then reassessing in the summer may be the best route forward. After all, with this increased price demand, you’re hardly going to be paying more in the summer – and if their demands reach that amount, you’re voicing new questions.

With Markus Krösche also coming in, the January mercato will be one where everything has to be considered carefully and judgements will be made before February 1 rolls around. Spending so heavily on one target may also be an early and unnecessary strike on his record, if it doesn’t work.

For many, Tresoldi made sense in January because he’d be an investment at an investment price. Now, you’re looking at a major budget depletion for a striker who has yet to become a senior international and/or a regular goalscorer in one of Europe’s top five leagues.

The romantic side of it is great; it’s difficult not to fall for that. Financially, though, signing Tresoldi is becoming a tougher sell and that’s where we might have to start listening to the brain rather than the heart.

#1831. North Macedonia vs Slovenia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 14 Nov 2026 12:58

North Macedonia will welcome Slovenia to Tose Proeski Arena on Monday night for a matchday six clash in UEFA Nations League B Group 1.

The hosts' relegation to League C has already been confirmed, while the visitors are fighting to secure second place and a chance at promotion to League A.

North Macedonia have endured a catastrophic 2026-27 UEFA Nations League, losing all of their five matches and having their relegation to League C already confirmed before the final matchday.

North Macedonia's miserable run extends far before the Nations League campaign got underway, having failed to win any of their last 13 matches across all competitions - with their last victory coming against Liechtenstein (5-0) in September 2025.

Goce Sedloski's side did, at least, manage to end their eight-game goalless run as Elmin Rastoder scored in the 57th-minute against Scotland last time out, although it ultimately mattered little as North Macedonia were defeated 2-1.

Two more goals conceded in that match brings their total goals allowed to 12 across the five group fixtures, six goals more than any other team in the group has conceded.

While those results have already confirmed North Macedonia's relegation to League C for the 2027-28 edition, the hosts will be desperate to end their dismal winless run by treating the home crowd to a win against Slovenia.

Slovenia, however, head into Monday's match as the considerable favourites to pick up all three points, while the visitors also have much more at stake going into the final matchday.

Bostjan Cesar's side are second in the League B Group 1 table with eight points going into Monday's match, leaving them narrowly one point ahead of Scotland.

Slovenia must, therefore, match or better Scotland's result against Switzerland to ensure a second-placed finish and earn themselves the chance to compete for a promotion to League A via the playoff.

Slovenia will look back to a comfortable 2-0 triumph over North Macedonia in the reverse fixture, with goals from Sandi Lovric and Aljosa Matko securing the victory.

Cesar's team have, however, struggled at times on the road, conceding all of their three goals when away from home and suffering their only defeat on their travels.

Rastoder ended North Macedonia's lengthy wait for a goal when he found the back of the net against Scotland, and the striker should lead the line once again on Monday.

The striker should be supported by captain Enis Bardhi in attack, with Eljif Elmas and Matej Gastarov partnering at the base of the midfield.

Meanwhile, Cesar could name a similar lineup to the one that secured a 0-0 draw with group leaders Switzerland earlier in the November international break.

Vanja Drrkusic, Jaka Bijol and Zan Zaletel should, therefore, remain in the back three, while Aljosa Matko, Danijel Sturm and Zan Vipotnik are likely to provide the attacking threat.

North Macedonia possible starting lineup:

Dimitrievski; Ilievski, Mladenovski, Musliu, Alioski; Gastarov, Elmas; Churlinov, Bardhi, Doriev; Rastoder

Oblak; Kuzmic, Drkusic, Bijol, Zaletel, Karnicnik; Matko, Zabukovnik, Cerin, Sturm; Vipotnik

Slovenia are undoubtedly the favourites to win this match, as demonstrated in their comfortable victory in the reverse fixture, and the visitors should secure all three points.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jorge Jesus rubbished suggestions Portugal missed Cristiano Ronaldo as they were humbled 4-1 by Denmark in the Nations League.

All-time great Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football after a public falling out with Portugal head coach Jesus during the September and October Nations League games.

"Missing Cristiano how? If he's no longer in the national team? Only if it's to keep me company. He doesn't play anymore, he's not here, he's already decided his situation."

#1829. England injury news: Arsenal receive Ezri Konsa update as Thomas Tuchel gets double fitness boost ahead of Spain clash

By Ben Sully | 14 Nov 2026 13:45, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 15:20

Arsenal's Ezri Konsa and Inter Milan's Djed Spence have taken part in training ahead of England's UEFA Nations League clash against Spain.

The Three Lions officially secured their place in the quarter-finals with a 2-1 victory over Croatia at Wembley on Thursday.

Guaranteed at least second place, England could still snatch first place away from Spain, who are currently three points clear after winning all five of their Nations League games.

The Three Lions have been handed a timely double fitness boost ahead of their daunting trip to the Metropolitano, with the news that Konsa and Spence took part in full training on Saturday after missing the win over Croatia.

Konsa was not fit to play a role at Wembley, leading to the late call-up of Bournemouth defender James Hill.

Spence, meanwhile, has not played for England since playing a pivotal role in the 2026 World Cup campaign.

The 26-year-old missed the last international window through injury, and while he has recently returned to action for Inter, England decided against risking him in Thursday's victory.

As per Sky Sports News, there is a 'chance' that Konsa and Spence could feature against Spain if they prove they are fully match fit.

In Konsa's absence, Tuchel went into Thursday's games with Jarrel Quansah and Dan Burn as his central defensive pairing, the latter of whom was called up as a replacement for the injured Marc Guehi.

Quansah made a mistake for Petar Sucic's equaliser and is likely to make way if Konsa comes into the starting lineup.

Meanwhile, Tuchel is likely to stick with Lewis Hall at left-back, but there is some doubt as to whether he will keep faith with Trent Alexander-Arnold on the right side of the back four.

If Tuchel opts to favour a defensively strong full-back, the door may open for Spence or Ben White to start at the Metropolitano.

Nevertheless, his arrival would be compared to Luka Modric in defence, an elite player whose reputation is among the best of his peers. He could be the core part of a new defence for the Diavolo.

#1827. Why your physics project needs an anthropologist

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Jaco de Swart is a historian and anthropologist of science at the University of Cambridge, UK.

The TAMBO team assesses suitable observatory sites in the Andes Mountains of Peru.Credit: Jaco de Swart

It is uncommon for a social scientist to have a seat at a meeting about an astronomical observatory, let alone for them to jointly lead one. For one-quarter of attendees to be social-science scholars is almost unprecedented. But that’s exactly what happens at meetings about the Tau Air-shower Mountain-based Observatory (TAMBO), a proposed detector to be built in the Peruvian Andes to look for cosmic particles called tau neutrinos.

Space diplomacy: bridging the operating gaps between myriad missions

Space diplomacy: bridging the operating gaps between myriad missions

Tau neutrinos are elusive fundamental particles that are transmitted through space from black holes and other distant sources. When these particles interact with rocks on Earth, they can produce a shower of other, short-lived particles. The idea behind TAMBO is that if such a shower were emitted from one side of a deep canyon, it could be picked up by an array of 5,000 detectors on the other side (TAMBO collaboration. Nature Astron. 10, 947–951; 2026). The Andes Mountains of Peru contain many promising sites.

For those who live in the area, however, the case for TAMBO is less clear. The Andes are a sensitive ecological environment and home to Indigenous farming communities that consider the mountains sentient beings that are integral to their society. The area is also affected by legal and illegal mining, large-scale infrastructure projects and legacies of colonialism. This all leads to scepticism towards large projects that are developed by people from outside the area.

I am the co-principal investigator of the TAMBO collaboration, alongside Peruvian neutrino physicist Carlos Argüelles at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. I lead the social-science and ‘responsible siting’ side of the project. Having received funding to build a proof-of-principle experiment called TAMBITO, we are searching for a potential location for the observatory.

Developing astronomers in Africa: ‘We wanted to create a discipline’

Developing astronomers in Africa: ‘We wanted to create a discipline’

Since 2024, the TAMBO collaboration has built partnerships with 11 Peruvian institutions, which are involved in the design and development of the telescope. Scientific links are an important starting point, but they are not enough. No matter what their discovery potential is, big scientific experiments are not beneficial to everyone. For example, construction of the Thirty Meter Telescope has been stalled since 2015 because of protests triggered by objections to its planned site on Maunakea in Hawaii — a mountain that is sacred in Native Hawaiian culture.

To integrate environmental care into the project and build good relationships with the communities that might host the telescope, TAMBO brought in experts on the Andean region. In 2024, the collaboration held a workshop at Harvard’s Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study, at which scholars and policymakers discussed what equitable astrophysics in Peru would look like. This led to the formation of a responsible-siting team that includes geographers, sociologists and anthropologists who have worked in the Andes.

IceCube just won a Nobel prize. Protect astroparticle physics projects with the same potential

#1826. Liverpool transfer news: Reds 'send scouts' to watch Barcelona-linked Bundesliga defender

By Ben Sully | 14 Nov 2026 14:28, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 14:30

Liverpool have reportedly scouted Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, who has emerged as a potential target for a number of top clubs across Europe.

Jeltsch has made 63 competitive appearances since joining Stuttgart from Nuremberg in the summer of 2025.

The 20-year-old has emerged as one of the Bundesliga's brightest young defenders during his time with Sebastian Hoeness's side, and his performances have earned him a call-up to Jurgen Klopp's senior squad.

While he is still waiting to make his debut for the national side, Jeltsch is already attracting significant attention from around Europe.

Liverpool and Barcelona have already been linked with the central defender who is also capable of covering at right back.

According to journalist Christian Falk, Liverpool are continuing to keep tabs on Jeltsch's situation as they weigh up a potential move.

The update claims the Reds recently sent scouts to watch Jeltsch in action for Stuttgart, although it is unclear what games were watched by Liverpool personnel.

Falk is of the belief that a move to the Premier League will not be the next step in Jeltsch's career, suggesting the defender may look to continue his development elsewhere before making the leap to the English top flight.

Bayern Munich are keeping tabs and could offer Jeltsch the opportunity to continue his career in the Bundesliga.

Virgil van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet, Joe Gomez and Ronald Araujo are the centre-back options currently available to Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola.

Giovanni Leoni is also part of the squad, but he is still waiting to make his return from a serious knee injury.

As a result, Liverpool could look to loan out the 19-year-old in January so he can build up his minutes and continue his development elsewhere.

Meanwhile, there is also uncertainty surrounding Virgil van Dijk's future, with his contract set to expire at the end of the season.

Liverpool's recruitment will surely be drawing up contingency plans for the event of Van Dijk's potential exit.

#1825. Arsenal: Declan Rice hits back at Graeme Souness after ‘cheating’ rant in new response

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Declan Rice has hit back at Graeme Souness over previous criticism of his playing style and defended Arsenal team-mate Ben White following more boos by England fans.

Former player, manager and pundit Souness has made headlines on more than one occasion in recent months for his controversial comments on England midfield star Rice, saying in the summer on Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored that he might be better suited to playing at centre-back because of his limited passing abilities.

Souness then doubled down on that criticism via the same platform in September, reiterating his belief that Rice might be a central defender and “isn’t the complete midfield player” who perhaps would not get into the team at any of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich or Manchester City.

He ramped up the rhetoric by saying that Rice was “cheating” in his midfield role with the way he dropped into defence as he called it “old man’s football”.

Rice has now answered those comments when asked in a press conference held ahead of England’s crunch final Nations League group game against Spain in Madrid on Sunday night.

“My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. For a centre-back, I think that’s not bad numbers!” Rice said with a laugh.

“I think I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals and to be a top-class centre-back getting those numbers I’m delighted with that!

“No, but look, if you speak about, like you said, the positioning, the old man’s football. Look at Harry Kane, for instance.

“We played him the other week [in the Champions League], he dropped next to the centre-backs 20-30 times in the game to pick up the ball. The game’s different now.

“It’s what the game demands, to get away from your man, to get away from who’s marking you, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch.

“Football’s way different. It’s changed a lot, and you’re always trying to look for tactical advantages.

“In terms of me as a midfielder, I’m constantly watching clips with Mikel [Arteta, Arsenal manager]. He’s constantly coaching me on the pitch.

“How I can progress the ball from deep, how I can drop next to the goalkeeper, how I can go next to full-back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

“So, I feel like we’re now seeing something totally different to what he would see. But in his time football was different, so I totally understand that and, of course, he played in midfield.

“He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There’s no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, as his career, you have to respect what he’s done.

“I didn’t get to see him play but obviously his accolades were top, and I’ve never got to meet him in person.

“If I met him, there wouldn’t be no, like I said, no disrespect. I would speak to him like I would speak to anyone so, yeah, it is what it is.”

Rice also provided an impassioned defence of Arsenal team-mate White, who was once again booed by some England fans after coming off the bench against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday.

It also happened in the friendlies against Uruguay and Japan back in March as the versatile defender made his first appearances for his country since leaving Gareth Southgate’s squad at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

“Ben has moved on from what's happened in the past, he's totally focused on playing for England,” Rice said. “When he's been fit and available he's constantly put himself forward to play for England.

“He loves being here, it's not like he doesn't like being here, he loves playing for England, loves being around the lads.

“If people knew and understood Ben White as a character he's not fazed by anything, he goes with the flow and he just wants to play football and for England.

“Fans are entitled to their opinion, it is what it is but he doesn't feel that way with England. He wants to come out and play his best football and enjoy himself.

“I think that's credit to him, coming on and playing for England and being booed is not easy but the way his character is it really helps him.

“It's not been a conversation for the team. It's so long ago now, it's nearly five years and it doesn't need to keep getting brought up. We need to look forward to the future and what Ben White is going to do in an England shirt, that's the most important thing.

“It's a pointless conversation, Ben has moved on, no one talks about it around the dinner table, no one speaks about it in the pool, we just play football and do what we need to do.”

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Erling Haaland says he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City and is solely focusing on performances on the pitch instead of potential sanctions off it.

City were found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between 2009-10 and 2017-18 in September, and they have since appealed the ruling.

With the appeal ongoing, the potential punishments should the verdict be upheld have not been revealed.

Haaland, who joined City back in 2022 and signed a further long-term contract in 2024, was asked about the case following Norway's 3-1 Nations League win over Wales, though he insisted his only aim was to get results on the pitch.

"This is a question I struggle to answer, because it's a legal battle between the Premier League and Manchester City," Haaland told Norwegian broadcaster TV2.

"Am I supposed to answer that? I don't really know. It's a difficult question to answer when I don't know that much about it.

"To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022, and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024.

"I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there."

— Manchester City (@ManCity) November 14, 2026

Haaland scored a penalty against Wales, netting his 66th goal in his 60th appearance for his country.

He has also made a strong start to 2026-27 for City, having scored 14 goals in 14 games in all competitions – no Premier League player has netted more.

However, City suffered three successive losses in the league before the international break, with Haaland failing to score in the latter two defeats.

But he is keen to get back firing as soon as possible, something he reiterated when asked if the case affects his future at the Etihad.

"I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024," Haaland added.

"I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

"I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

"I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1. Things aren't going so well in the Premier League, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham [on Saturday]."

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Declan Rice insists that he is relishing the competition from Alex Scott with England, as Arsenal are linked with a potential big-money transfer swoop for the Bournemouth star.

Scott continues to go from strength to strength for both club and country, earning his first senior caps for the Three Lions during the previous international break in recognition for his fine form in the Premier League.

The 23-year-old made his England debut off the bench in September’s 2-0 away win over the Czech Republic in the Nations League, with Rice having pulled out of the squad, before then being handed his maiden start by Thomas Tuchel in the 7-0 demolition of Croatia last month.

Scott picked up a thigh injury during that camp that it was feared could keep him out for up to two months, though the issue was not as serious as first feared and he was back on the Bournemouth bench in their last game against Ipswich.

While Scott has been unable to press his claims for further England involvement during the current international window, Rice knows that he will be quickly back challenging for a regular starting role in Tuchel’s engine room.

“To be honest, Alex Scott playing was incredible,” Rice said of Scott ahead of Sunday night’s crunch clash with world champions Spain in Madrid, per The Mirror. “The way he's been playing for Bournemouth the last two or three seasons has been remarkable.

“The way he's being spoken about is totally right because of the levels he's set for himself and I totally understand playing for England comes with competition.

“When we [Arsenal] signed Bruno Guimaraes, when we signed [Martin] Zubimendi, when we had Myles [Lewis-Skelly], [Mikel] Merino, [Martin] Odegaard, you're competing with six midfielders at your club every day so for me there's nothing different.

“Throughout my whole career there's been competition. It's normal.”

#1822. Martin Odegaard reveals Arsenal contract "hope" as Gunners captain delivers update on future

By Ben Sully | 14 Nov 2026 14:53, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 14:53

Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard has revealed he is yet to hold discussions over a new contract.

Odegaard has established himself as one of the key figures in Mikel Arteta's squad, as demonstrated by the fact that he has been the club captain since the summer of 2022.

The Norwegian became the first Arsenal captain to lift the Premier League trophy last term, although his campaign was disrupted by injury.

Odegaard has enjoyed a consistent run of games this season, allowing him to start all 12 of Arsenal's matches across the Premier League and Champions League, contributing four goals and an assist.

But while he remains an integral player in Arteta's squad, there is some doubt about his long-term future with the Gunners due to his uncertain contract situation.

Odegaard's current deal expires at the end of the 2027-28 season, meaning he will enter the final year of his contract next summer.

The Norway international has now offered an update on his future, revealing he has yet to hold discussions over a new deal despite being keen to extend his stay at the Emirates Stadium.

“I’m happy and hope I can stay there for a long time to come, but we haven’t started on that yet,” Odegaard said while on international duty.

While Odegaard is keen to sign a new deal, Arsenal would have to consider selling him if they are unable to reach an agreement by next summer.

That is because it would represent their last chance to command a considerable fee, with their main goal being to avoid losing him on a free transfer in 2028.

Bayern Munich are believed to be among Odegaard's suitors and will surely be keeping a close eye on any contract developments over the coming months.

In the short term, Odegaard will be focusing on Norway's two Nations League games against Wales and Denmark, before he returns to Arsenal ahead of a Premier League away clash against Newcastle United.

#1820. Arsenal star sets new goal record after clear transfer message sent

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres set a new Nations League record as his incredible goalscoring run for Sweden continued.

The Gunners forward netted a first-half brace for Graham Potter’s side in Stockholm on Saturday night as they held off a fightback from Bosnia and Herzegovina to win 3-2 in Group B4 and seal promotion back to League A with a game to spare.

Both of Gyokeres’ goals came via penalties, the first he earned himself following a foul by Stjepan Radeljic to put Sweden 2-0 up after only 11 minutes after Daniel Svensson’s early effort.

He slammed in from 12 yards again during first-half stoppage time after Svensson was fouled by ex-Arsenal full-back Sead Kolasinac, who scored himself in the second half after Armin Gigovic’s header to set up a lively finish at Strawberry Arena.

Gyokeres became the first player ever to score in eight consecutive Nations League matches, having notched 12 times during that span - including a memorable four-goal haul against Azerbaijan in November 2024, while he was still at former club Sporting.

He also scored in the away draw with Bosnia and Herzegovina last month, as well as hitting the back of the net home and away against both Romania and Poland, plus in meetings with Slovakia and Estonia.

In total, Gyokeres has 18 goal contributions in his last 11 appearances for Sweden - 14 goals and four assists. His overall record for his country stands at 27 goals in 42 games, good for ninth place on an all-time list led by Zlatan Ibrahimovic that also includes the likes of Henrik Larsson.

He will hope to add further to that tally on Tuesday night, when Potter’s team travel to meet Poland in Wroclaw.

Sweden’s thrilling win over Bosnia and Herzegovina was also notable for the return of Tottenham’s Dejan Kulusevski, who made his first international appearance in almost two years on Saturday following a long-term kneecap injury.

Arsenal will be hoping to benefit from Gyokeres’ strong performances in the Nations League as they seek to maintain or increase their five-point lead at the Premier League summit when they return to action away at struggling Newcastle next weekend.

Only two of his eight goals so far this term have been for his club, in October’s shock Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood and in the 2-1 victory at Slavia Prague in the Champions League earlier this month, when he was excellent.

The 28-year-old - who has received plenty of criticism from fans and pundits for his performances at Arsenal this season - has yet to register at all in the Premier League, where he has made only one start with Kai Havertz remaining manager Mikel Arteta’s preferred option up front.

#1816. Erling Haaland issues major transfer update as Man City ‘learn date’ for Premier League appeal decision

Erling Haaland has said he is happy at Manchester City, after commenting on the club’s financial scandal.

During the autumn international break, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2018/19.

While City deny any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal, serious sanctions - such as points deductions, fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League - are likely if that fails.

According to reports, a hearing is to take place in December and a decision on the appeal expected in early 2027.

Should Man City relegated or be issued a huge points deduction, many have speculated that a number of the club’s stars will likely depart, including Haaland.

However, the Norway international - who is valued at £183million on transfermarkt and would have a host of clubs queuing up for his signature were he to leave the Etihad Stadium - has set the record straight on his future with a transfer update.

“I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,” Haaland told TV2 after scoring in Norway’s 3-1 Nations League win over Wales on Saturday.

“I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

“I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we’re top of our group in Europe.

“Things aren’t going so well for City in the league, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can’t focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.”

Haaland also said that he has not done much research into the investigation as it covers a period when he was not at Man City.

"The investigation covered 2009 to 2018," he added. "In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2012, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don’t need the whole list…2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team.

"Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne’s first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

"So this is a question I struggle to answer because it’s a legal battle…It’s a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with.

"Am I supposed to answer that? I’m not really sure."

#1815. Trinidad and Tobago vs Antigua and Barbuda - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 14 Nov 2026 14:55, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 16:09

Trinidad and Tobago will host Antigua and Barbuda at the Hasely Crawford Stadium on Tuesday for the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League tie, with a place in the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup Prelims at stake.

The home side head into the encounter with a slender advantage after claiming a 3-2 victory in the first leg of the Play-In tie, and will need another strong performance to secure their place in the next stage of Gold Cup qualification.

It has been a dismal campaign so far for Trinidad and Tobago, who are yet to register a victory in the CONCACAF Nations League, League A.

The Soca Warriors sit fifth in the relegation zone with just one point from four matches, although they have managed to avoid defeat in their last two outings.

After suffering three consecutive losses, Derek King's side secured a 1-1 draw against Curacao before claiming victory over Antigua and Barbuda in their most recent match.

Their defensive record remains a major concern, having failed to keep a clean sheet in their last 14 matches, but the latest win over Antigua marked their 13th victory in 16 meetings between the two nations.

Antigua and Barbuda made a dream start in the first leg, taking an early lead through an own goal from Ryan Telfer.

However, the visitors fought their way back into the contest and scored three quick goals to establish a 3-1 advantage at half time, before Brandon Satchell's stoppage-time strike gave Jacques Passy's side renewed hope ahead of the return fixture.

The Benna Boys have enjoyed an impressive League C campaign, finishing top of Group B with nine points from four matches.

They have also scored 13 goals in their last four outings and, despite their first-leg defeat, can take confidence from their attacking form as they look to find the net again and make life difficult for Trinidad and Tobago on Tuesday.

Trinidad and Tobago CONCACAF Nations League form:

Antigua and Barbuda CONCACAF Nations League form:

Molik Khan was outstanding for Trinidad and Tobago in the first leg and is likely to retain his place in the starting lineup, although Nathaniel James could provide an alternative.

Tyrese Spicer and Dante Sealy remain unavailable through injury, but Daniel David and Kaihim Thomas could be handed more playing time.

Kylano Issac and Leroy Graham struggled to make an impact in the previous game for Antigua and Barbuda, but both are still expected to retain their places in a 4-3-3 formation.

Satchell made a significant impact after coming off the bench, and Passy could be tempted to hand him a starting role in place of Dion Pereira, while Vaughn Jackson is another candidate to feature from the outset.

Trinidad and Tobago possible starting lineup:

Smith; Telfer, Garcia, Joseph, Payne; Khan, Rampersad, Frederick; Gilbert, Gill, Phillip

Antigua and Barbuda possible starting lineup:

Dorsett; Daley, Griffith, Graham, Issac; Pereira, Bramble, Tomlinson; Garro, Bishop, George

While their defensive frailties remain a major concern, King will be encouraged by the way his side responded after falling behind in the first leg. With so much at stake and a draw enough to secure qualification, the Soca Warriors should have just enough to edge past their rivals.

Dominik Szoboszlai has provided Liverpool with a big injury boost, despite playing for Hungary with heavy strapping on his right knee.

Szoboszlai’s fitness for Hungary’s Nations League double-header was up in the air at the beginning of the week after Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola admitted the midfielder was not at 100 percent.

This was after suffering a knee sprain in the 3-1 win over Crystal Palace, with Szoboszlai then linking up with his national team for further tests.

Fortunately for Liverpool - who host Manchester United in their first Premier League game after the international break - the feedback on the 26-year-old has been largely positive.

Amid worrying post-match comments and footage of Szoboszlai’s right knee being heavily strapped, he was able to complete 90 minutes of Hungary’s 2-0 win over Georgia and claimed an assist for Barnabas Varga.

"During the warm-up I was close to saying that I wouldn't be able to play after all,” Szoboszlai told reporters after the game. “I felt the injury during one of my shots.

“But I thought to myself that, having come this far, I wasn't going to let the team down. So I tried to give everything I had, as best as I could.

"My leg felt good, but now the treatment process starts all over again, and I need to be ready for Tuesday."

Hungary are next in action on Tuesday night as they host Northern Ireland in decisive final game from Nations League B, Group 2.

Szoboszlai’s side currently sit second in the table, a point behind Northern Ireland, and know they must win to gain promotion to League A.

The midfielder is likely to start in Budapest and Iraola will be hopeful the Liverpool No8 comes through the game unscathed ahead of the Man United showdown at Anfield five days later.

#1811. Gibraltar vs Malta - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 14 Nov 2026 15:17, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 16:14

Gibraltar will be looking to finish their UEFA Nations League campaign on a positive note when they welcome Malta to Europa Point Stadium on Monday evening.

The visitors have already secured top spot in their League D group, while the hosts will be keen to pick up their first win.

Gibraltar have picked up just two Nations League points so far, with two draws and one defeat from three games.

Scott Wiseman's side began their campaign with a goalless draw against Andorra, but they earned a respectable 1-1 stalemate away to Malta four days later, with James Scanlon scoring the equaliser.

However, Friday's 2-0 defeat away to Andorra was a disappointing result, with Guillaume Lopez and Albert Rosas Ubach on target for the hosts.

Although a victory over Malta on Monday would see Gibraltar leapfrog Andorra into second, there is a real lack of jeopardy surrounding the fixture.

Due to a restructuring of the Nations League, every side in League D will be promoted to League C for the 2028-29 edition.

Malta, meanwhile, have enjoyed an impressive Nations League campaign and would have been promoted to League C anyway under the original rules.

Emilio De Leo's side are unbeaten and have collected seven points from their three group games so far.

Malta have picked up two victories over Andorra, beating them 2-1 and 1-0, and also drawing 1-1 with Malta.

In their most recent game, Malta were held to a 1-1 stalemate in a friendly against Eswatini, who were down to 10 men for much of the game after Gift Gamedze was sent off.

Malta will be keen to get back to winning ways on Monday and De Leo is expected to name a much stronger side, having rotated on Thursday.

Gibraltar will need at least one change after Friday's loss to Andorra, with Tjay De Barr suspended after picking up another booking.

Ethan Jolley is also a doubt after he was forced off with an injury in the 33rd minute against Andorra, with Louie Annesley expected to replace him.

Malta, meanwhile, will be without Alexander Satariano, who is suspended for the final group fixture after receiving a one-match ban.

The likes of Teddy Teuma, Ilyas Chouaref and Brandon Paiber could all come into the side, while Basil Tuma is set to be rewarded with a start after scoring off the bench against Eswatini.

Hankins; Annesley, Bent, Lopes, Valarino; Pozo, Ronan; Richards, Scanlon, Mason; Borge

Bonello; Lonardelli, Muscat, Shaw, Beerman; Guillaumier, Paiber; Mbong, Teuma, Chouaref; Tuma

Gibraltar should provide a tough test for Malta, but the visitors are unbeaten in the Nations League for a reason and should have enough quality to pick up the win.

#1810. Luis de la Fuente and Spain star agree on England ranking ahead of Nations League decider

Luis de la Fuente has labelled the Spain vs England match as a meeting between “two of world football's powerhouses”.

The Metropolitano Stadium, home of La Liga giants Atletico Madrid, will stage a decisive Nations League showdown on Sunday evening as top spot in Group A3 is up for grabs.

As Spain won the reverse fixture at Wembley Stadium back in September, they just require a point to qualify for the quarter-finals as group winners.

However, due to having a superior goal difference and taking UEFA’s tiebreaker rules into account, victory in Madrid for England would see them leapfrog the reigning world and European champions.

Speaking ahead of the game, De La Fuente spoke highly of the Three Lions by saying: “These are two of world football's powerhouses. It's one of the best matches you can watch.

“Of the different styles of football, I prefer ours because our players are suited to it.

"We'll see if anyone breaks these records in the future, but for now we're on the longest-ever unbeaten run. And we're not stopping here; we want to break more records and stretch them even further."

Alex Baena, a scorer in Spain’s 3-2 win over England earlier in the season, then echoed the words of his national team manager.

He said: "I think England and us are the two best teams in the world on form. They're a great team, with a great coach, absolutely fantastic players and, on top of that, the Ballon d'Or winner."

As per FIFA’s current world rankings, Sunday’s showdown pits the team ranked top (Spain) against the team ranked fourth (England), though the next official update is expected early next week.

#1809. Guimaraes learning a lot from ‘machine’ Rice at Arsenal

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Declan Rice is "a machine", according to Bruno Guimaraes, who says he is learning a lot from his Arsenal team-mate.

Guimaraes joined Arsenal for a reported £75m from Newcastle United in August, and has shown promising signs that he is creating a strong midfield partnership with Rice.

The Brazilian has made 14 appearances in all competitions since joining Arsenal, and has made and won more tackles than any of his team-mates (15/24).

Rice, however, tops the charts for touches (1,229), assists (five), successful passes (931/1,026), and possessions won (61).

And Guimaraes was full of high praise for the England defender, who hinted he will be signing a new Arsenal deal soon.

"Look, I think that ever since he announced I was coming here, everything was practically set," Guimaraes told ESPN Brazil.

"He sent me a message right away saying: 'We've had a lot of fights in the past, but now we're friends – we're going to play together. I'm really happy you're coming here. You're going to really raise the level of our team'.

"So, he was a guy who had already won me over even before I arrived. We know – I'd say he's a complete player; he's a machine on the field.

"He can run, I don't know, 22 kilometres in a game without stopping for a second. I was really happy.

"I'm learning from him – learning a lot from him – since he's a very technical player.

"So, I think we have one of the best midfields in Europe here. Yes – given the number of players we have – and anyway, I think Declan is a guy who's been helping me a lot; I felt right at home."

Our midfield marvel Declan Rice's impactful October earns him the Player of the Month award

Arsenal sit top of the Premier League table for the international break, with their 1-0 win over Hull City before the hiatus seeing them leapfrog Manchester City to the summit.

Despite being knocked out of the EFL Cup by League Two side Fleetwood Town, Arsenal are still looking strong this season, as they also remain unbeaten at the halfway stage of the league phase in the Champions League.

"I'm happy here; I'm starting my journey here as well," Guimaraes added.

"I think I'm increasingly understanding Arteta's approach – which is completely different from what I was used to doing at Newcastle – and I'm adapting more and more, getting to know the new players better.

"It's not easy to switch clubs after nearly five years, when you were already completely used to the routine, to everything. But I think this is a huge challenge, and I'm ready for it."

#1807. Next USA manager: Gareth Southgate one of four 'candidates' to replace Mauricio Pochettino

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 16:06

The United States Soccer Federation may reportedly approach Gareth Southgate to become their next manager.

Earlier this week, it was confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino will become the new Manchester United boss after the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti.

With Pochettino taking charge of the next two games, it gives US soccer chiefs time to find a permanent successor for their next meaningful fixtures in March.

A report has suggested that former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has been identified as a potential candidate.

According to TEAMtalk, there are three other names that have been highlighted behind the scenes, including Southgate's.

The report emphasises that trying to tempt Guardiola to take the job is the priority of US soccer chiefs.

Nevertheless, Southgate, ex-Portugal boss Roberto Martinez and former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe are also viewed as possible successors.

In the case of Southgate, he has not been in the dugout since guiding England to the Euro 2024 final, where they lost to Spain.

Southgate has previously hinted that he may not manage another team, and the report suggests that there is currently little chance that he would consider becoming the new USA boss.

Furthermore, it is suggested that the 56-year-old is more likely to take a role at the Football Association than take another managerial job.

In December, a USA squad that will largely include MLS-based players will face Jamaica in a friendly, but the presence of that game on the schedule will not speed up the process to appoint a new manager.

Instead, discussions with suitable candidates are likely to take a number of weeks, with the onus on Pochettino's replacement being prepared for games scheduled for March.

The only way that the process will speed up is through Guardiola accepting any approach for his services.

#1804. Manchester United: Sir Alex Ferguson has already approved of Mauricio Pochettino as talks planned

Mauricio Pochettino says he will have the opportunity to speak to Sir Alex Ferguson as his Manchester United tenure gets underway.

Pochettino was announced as the new Man United head coach on Friday, succeeding Michael Carrick who had been sacked the day before, with the club languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.

However, the Argentine has not yet officially started work at Old Trafford.

As communicated in Man Utd’s official statement, Pochettino has been allowed to finish up his commitments with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) and their double-header against Haiti.

The first of which took place on Saturday evening with USA recording a 6-0 win to put one foot in the CONCACAF Nations League finals.

Following Pochettino’s penultimate game in charge of USA, he spoke to the Telegraph and was asked if he can spoken to Ferguson since accepting the Man United job.

“Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,” the 54-year-old said.

“I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

“For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense. But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.”

Pochettino and Ferguson have remained in close contact since first dining with each other in 2016.

They first crossed paths in the dugout during the 2012-13 season when Man United beat Southampton at Old Trafford, though Pochettino left a lasting impression on Ferguson despite the defeat.

"For the first 30 minutes we were fantastic," Ferguson told BBC Sport in January 2013. "But in the second half Southampton have been the best team to play here this season. We were fortunate to win."

Then in 2016, David Lammy, MP for Tottenham, shared details of a meeting with Ferguson at a charity function.

"I’m going to let you in to a secret," Lammy told The Spurs Show podcast. "About six weeks ago I sat next to Alex Ferguson at a dinner in support of grassroots football abroad.

"He said to me, 'I think you guys have the best manager in the Premier League.' Alex Ferguson said that."

With five goals and as many assists already this season, he’s thriving for Ruben Amorim, who is keen to keep him as an essential player in his team.

In this morning’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews), the leading line is that Rabiot remains key, and that the Rossoneri aim to tie down his future by the end of the season. That much is not new information, but it’s a reminder that he’s not been forgotten.

With Christian Pulisic’s renewal finalised, the Frenchman is next in line, with his importance not unknown to the Diavolo. Indeed, they are ready to offer him what could be his final ‘big’ contract, which would see him extend his stay at San Siro until 2030.

Alongside this, a pay rise from €3.5 million to €5m per season is expected, another reminder of his importance.

The step here, though, is that the offer has now officially been made and is laying on the table. Rabiot played at San Siro last night, and he’ll now take some time to evaluate the offer from the club, which he now calls home.

#1802. Arsenal: Why Kepa Arrizabalaga was allowed to make second international debut amid surprise twist

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga has been in action during the international break, though not for the Spain national team.

The 32-year-old, who joined the Gunners from London rivals Chelsea in July 2025 for £5million, has 13 senior caps for La Roja, but has not made an appearance since a 2-0 loss to Scotland in March 2023.

Overlooked once again by Luis de la Fuente for Spain’s Nations League double-header against the Czech Republic and England in favour of Unai Simon, Joan Garcia and Arsenal team-mate David Raya, it was set to be a quiet international window for Kepa.

In a surprise turn of events, Kepa was called up to the Basque Country squad for their friendly against Venezuela and made his debut on Saturday, playing 45 minutes of the 1-0 win at San Mames.

While Athletic Club star Mikel Jauregizar scored the only goal of the game, some Arsenal fans may have been left wondering why their back-up goalkeeper was able to play for another national team.

Of course, it is well known that FIFA rules state that players cannot switch national teams after they've played three competitive fixtures.

However, despite Kepa winning 13 senior caps for Spain, he was cleared to play for the Basque Country because they are currently not recognised by FIFA.

As such, the win over Venezuela was not an official match, in the eyes of football's governing body.

Nevertheless, Kepa was able to get valuable minutes in his legs, having made just one appearance for Arsenal so far this season - the 4-2 win over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup third round.

Future Kepa appearances for the Basque Country could be in doubt as they have started the process to secure official international status for the national team.

Part of a statement reads: “The Basque Football Federation (EFF-FVF) has revived the process to obtain international official status for the Basque National Team, both men's and women's.

“With this aim, it has approached the Supreme Sports Council and has communicated information about the initiative to the Spanish Football Federation.”

#1801. Prediction: Hungary vs Northern Ireland

Everything is on the line in Budapest on Tuesday evening as Hungary and Northern Ireland meet in the decisive match of their UEFA Nations League campaign.

The visitors lead the group by a single point heading into the final round of fixtures, meaning a draw would secure promotion for Northern Ireland, while Hungary must win to leapfrog their rivals and clinch top spot.

Hungary head into the final round of Nations League group matches knowing that only a victory will be enough to secure automatic promotion to League A.

Marco Rossi’s side currently sit second in the group with 10 points, one behind leaders Northern Ireland, meaning the equation is straightforward at the Puskas Arena. A win would send the Magyars into first place and guarantee promotion, while any other result would leave them depending on a promotion playoff.

Hungary boosted their chances with a 2-0 victory over Georgia on Saturday, although they were made to work hard for the breakthrough and relied on an own goal from Lasha Dvali to open the scoring.

That success was their third consecutive Nations League win and continued a strong run of form that has seen them lose only once in their last nine matches in all competitions. During their recent three-game winning streak, Hungary have scored five goals and kept two clean sheets.

Home form has also been encouraging. The Magyars have won four of their last six matches when playing on home soil and will believe they have a genuine opportunity to overturn the one-point deficit separating them from Northern Ireland.

Dominik Szoboszlai revealed he almost suffered an injury before the victory over Georgia, but the Liverpool midfielder is expected to feature and could operate in an advanced role.

Hungary are without Milan Vitalis through suspension, while captain Willi Orban is also banned, potentially forcing Attila Szalai into the starting lineup.

Barnabas Varga is expected to lead the attack and will be aiming to score his 17th international goal.

Northern Ireland arrive in Budapest sitting at the top of the group and knowing that a draw will be enough to secure promotion to League A for the first time.

Michael O’Neill’s side strengthened their position with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Ukraine on Saturday, courtesy of a long-range strike from Terry Devlin. That result moved them onto 11 points and left them in control of their own destiny heading into the final matchday.

The Green and White Army have become extremely difficult to beat. Their only defeat in their last eight matches came against France in June, with four wins and three draws recorded during that period.

While Northern Ireland have not always been prolific, they have consistently found ways to collect results. They have scored exactly one goal in five of their last eight games and have developed a reputation for staying competitive in tight contests.

Their record against Hungary is reasonably encouraging too. Northern Ireland have only lost one of the last four meetings between the nations and held Hungary to a goalless draw earlier in the group stage.

The visitors have also won both of their away fixtures in this Nations League campaign, although their broader away record remains mixed.

Jamie Donley will miss the game after picking up a yellow card against Ukraine.

His absence could see Josh Magennis lead the attack, with Ethan Galbraith and Isaac Price expected to provide support from wide areas.

Shea Charles should once again be tasked with controlling the midfield.

This is effectively a winner-takes-all contest for automatic promotion, although Northern Ireland hold the advantage of knowing that a draw will achieve their objective.

Hungary’s recent form and strong home record make them slight favourites to claim victory, but Northern Ireland have built their campaign on defensive resilience and consistency. The visitors have proved extremely difficult to break down throughout the group and already held Hungary scoreless earlier in the campaign.

With the stakes so high and neither side likely to take unnecessary risks, a closely contested encounter seems to be on the cards, and the visitors are likely to leave with what they come for: a point.

Prediction: Austria vs Republic of Ireland

#1799. How Nico Paz compares to Bruno Fernandes as Man United consider Como star amid captain's contract uncertainty

By Ellis Stevens | 14 Nov 2026 17:04, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 17:14

The mood surrounding Manchester United is already one of misery given their disastrous start to the 2026-27 Premier League season, with the Red Devils sitting inside the relegation zone with just eight points after 10 matches.

Cautious optimism may have started to return following the announcement of Mauricio Pochettino as the new Manchester United manager, but the Red Devils have already been dealt another potential blow in the early days of the new boss' tenure.

Reports have emerged that captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected a second offer of a new deal at Old Trafford, leaving his long-term future uncertain as his current contract approaches its expiry in June 2027 - although the Red Devils do have the option to extend his stay by a further 12 months.

As the Portugal international is yet to commit his future to the club, subsequent reports have suggested that Man Utd are monitoring Nico Paz as a potential replacement in the summer transfer window.

Securing Paz's signature would certainly not be straightforward, with Real Madrid retaining a buy-back clause and several of Europe's elite sides likely to join the race, but replacing Fernandes and becoming Man Utd's new talisman under fellow Argentine Pochettino could prove tempting.

With speculation continuing to circulate around Fernandes' future and Manchester United's reported interest in Paz, Sports Mole takes a closer look at how the two players compare.

Although both Fernandes and Paz operate in the traditional number 10 position, the two players bring a very different style and ability in possession.

In 2026-27, and throughout his more recent years at Old Trafford, Fernandes has thrived as Manchester United's primary creative operator, with almost every attack flowing through the Portugal international.

As demonstrated by his Premier League record-breaking 21 assists last season, as well as creating 0.44 big chances per 90 in the league this term, Fernandes' greatest strength is his ability to pick out dangerous passes.

In comparison, Paz, while capable of picking out a threaded pass - as shown with 0.22 through balls per 90 in Serie A this season - is at his best when carrying the ball.

Paz attempts a considerable 3.50 dribbles per 90 in Serie A, completing 1.97 of them, whereas Fernandes averages just 0.89 attempted dribbles and 0.22 successful dribbles per 90 minutes.

While Paz is able to then create an opportunity for a teammate, with 0.22 big chances created per 90, the Argentine often prefers to manoeuvre himself into goalscoring positions.

Paz has taken 5.03 shots per 90 minutes in the Serie A, scoring 0.33 goals per 90, while Fernandes has taken 3.44 shots per 90. Although the Portugal international has scored at a greater frequency, with 0.44 goals per 90, two of his four goals have come from the penalty spot, while Paz's strikes have all come from open play.

Paz's ability to play in a possession-oriented side must also be taken into consideration, with the Argentine playing a key role in Cesc Fabregas's Como, who boast the highest average possession in Serie A this season (61.6%).

Fernandes, while one of the best in European football at consistently creating chances, has a track record for seemingly preferring to attempt ambitious passes rather than recycling the ball.

While that is undoubtedly what makes Fernandes such a phenomenal chance creator, forcing the midfielder into a system that operates around keeping the ball more often may subtract from arguably his greatest quality.

As a result of his tendency to look for the most dangerous pass, Fernandes' successful pass percentage stands at 80.9% this season, compared to Paz's considerably higher 87.94% pass completion.

Given Pochettino's recent tendency to create teams with a possession-based identity, demonstrated by his Chelsea side boasting around 59% average possession - which would place them in the top four of Premier League teams this term - Paz may better suit the new Manchester United's identity.

However, it must be noted that Paz, due to his more adventurous dribbling approach, is dispossessed 0.87 times per 90 this season, compared to Fernandes' figure of 0.78.

While both certainly bring their respective strengths in possession, shown by their attacking numbers, their defensive and off-ball contributions are equally as important.

Paz's numbers show that the 22-year-old could offer a greater physical presence in midfield, particularly when competing for possession and challenging opponents in individual duels.

The Como midfielder averages 11.7 duels per 90 minutes, almost double Fernandes' figure of 6.00, while Paz also wins considerably more of those contests, recording 6.89 successful duels compared to the Portugal international's 2.11.

Paz's physical advantage is also evident in aerial situations, with the Argentina international's 6'1" frame helping him to win 0.87 aerial duels per 90 minutes, while Fernandes, standing at 5'10", wins just 0.11 of his aerial contests.

Fernandes does cover more ground, covering 101.3km in nine league matches to Paz's 88.4km covered in 10 league games.

However, Fernandes is often used as Manchester United's trigger for the press, although the Red Devils captain can also be seen charging forward without support on numerous occasions throughout matches.

Paz's ability both in and out of possession were witnessed first-hand by Manchester United in their 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League earlier this season.

The Argentine dispossessed Carlos Baleba before driving nearly 25 metres up the pitch and converting pass Senne Lammens to make it 3-1 - marking his second goal of the game after also netting a stunning strike from just inside the box in the second minute.

Paz also registered the assist for Anastasios Douvikas's goal in that victory, and that impressive performance is surely one of several reasons why the Red Devils hold an interest in the attacking midfielder.

#1796. Canada vs Guatemala - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 14 Nov 2026 17:19

Needing only to avoid defeat to advance into the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals, Canada will host Guatemala in leg two of that tie on Monday at BMO Field in Toronto.

The opening match between the two saw Canada hold on to a 3-2 victory, putting them in pole position to advance.

They lost their inspirational leader early in their last match, but the Canadians did not lose their spirit, putting together a strong opening half against the Guatemalans with three goals.

The win for Jesse Marsch’s men came at a cost, as their captain Alphonso Davies was taken off less than 10 minutes into the match with a suspected lower body issue, having missed his share of action of late for the team through injury.

Their three goals in the opening leg were as many as this team had managed in their three internationals combined before that, while they conceded one more goal on Friday than they had in those last three games.

While they go into this game with a narrow one-goal advantage, Canada will fancy their chances of advancing, as they are without a defeat at BMO Field in nearly three years.

Les Rouges will hope to go beyond this stage for a second successive occasion, having beaten Suriname 4-0 on aggregate in this phase last season.

Canada have not lost to a Central American side in 90 minutes since Honduras beat them 2-1 in the group stage of this competition in 2022.

It took them nearly 50 minutes to settle into the match, and by then it felt like it was already too late for Guatemala to mount a comeback on Friday.

Luis Fernando Tena’s team gave up as many goals in 45 minutes in leg one of this tie as they had in the entire group phase of this competition (three).

To avoid elimination on Monday, the Guatemalans must do something they have yet to do in 2026, win a match away from home.

Los Chapines have lost five of their six internationals played this year as the visiting team, failing to score on four of those occasions.

Guatemala have also lost two of their last three Nations League affairs away from home, conceding three goals in two of those instances.

Monday will mark the first time they play the Canucks in Canada since 2004, with Los Mayas pulling out a 2-0 win in Vancouver on that occasion.

After his early injury on Friday, Alphonso Davies is out for Canada in leg two, leaving Ralph Priso as his likely replacement, while Kevin Khan is the only one in the squad seeking his first senior cap.

Tani Oluwaseyi netted his third on the international stage in leg one, with Liam Millar scoring for the second time and record goalscorer Jonathan David now up to 44 with the national team.

On the Guatemala side, Jonathan Franco and Carlos Estrada will serve the second of a three-match ban on Monday, while Jorge Aparicio is dealing with an ankle injury.

Oscar Santis put his team on the board in the second half Friday, while an own goal by Luc de Fougerolles in stoppage time has them within striking distance of turning this tie around.

The margin between these two is thin heading into this match, but the Guatemalans have rarely been able to create much away from home all year, and they have never beaten a North American side in this competition.

#1793. Low: Germany moving in positive direction under Klopp

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Joachim Low believes Jurgen Klopp is moving Germany in a "positive direction", though he warned that there will be setbacks for the team.

Klopp replaced Julian Nagelsmann as Germany's head coach following their shock World Cup last-32 exit at the hands of Paraguay on penalties.

He has overseen five games so far in the Nations League, with the team still in with a chance of reaching the quarter-finals, though their fate is going down to a final-day clash with the Netherlands in Group A2.

Klopp has won two of his games so far (D2 L1), and Germany are unbeaten in their last three outings following a 3-1 win over nine-man Serbia last time out.

Low, who led Germany to World Cup glory in 2014, has so far been impressed by what he has seen from Klopp's start.

"He is doing a very, very good job," Low told Bild TV.

"He gives the players a lot of confidence and is trying to develop a sustainable playing philosophy.

"You get the feeling that things are heading in a positive direction."

Klopp has already faced bumps along the way, failing to win either of his first two matches, including a shock 1-0 loss to Greece.

But in recent years, Germany have struggled to go toe-to-toe with the best; at World Cups, they have fallen at the group stage twice since their 2014 triumph, while this year's exit came at the first hurdle of the knockout stages.

And Low urged caution against raising expectations too high this early into Klopp's reign.

"His name alone does not always guarantee success. There will still be a few setbacks before we get back to that level," Low added.

"The results are not all that important at this stage. We are in the Nations League now, and qualifying begins next year, which we will get through.

"The important thing will be for the team to spend six months playing together and building an understanding.

"You cannot expect any coach to get everything working within a few weeks. You have to look at whether there is progress."

Germany face the Netherlands in their final Nations League game on Monday, knowing a win will take them into the last eight of the tournament.

#1789. Xavi: Netherlands players out to enjoy themselves in huge Germany test

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Netherlands coach Xavi wants his team to go out and enjoy themselves when they take on Germany, though he knows Jurgen Klopp's team will pose a huge challenge.

The Oranje turned in their best display under Xavi yet last time out, as they hammered Greece 7-0.

That victory sent the Netherlands to the top of Nations League Group A2 on 11 points, three better off than third-place Germany, who beat Serbia 3-1. Greece sit second, also on eight points.

With Germany and the Netherlands having drawn on MD1, it means the winner of Monday's game will go through to the quarter-finals, though a point for the Oranje would be enough.

If Germany win, then the Netherlands will still go through if Serbia avoid defeat against Greece.

And Xavi has asked his players to go out with the same level of enjoyment that they had during their rout of Greece on Friday.

A Donyell Malen special! https://t.co/hnzMJGY7mZ

— OnsOranje (@OnsOranje) November 15, 2026

"The players enjoyed themselves against Greece and they want to do that again against Germany," Xavi told reporters.

"I am so proud of them. I am convinced that they can be good again. We know how it should be done. We need to bring in even more continuity.

"Now that I am [the] coach, I feel the rivalry [with Germany]. That is why it is so important for us. It is a fantastic test."

Germany's win over Serbia was just their second victory under Jurgen Klopp, who is out to avoid an underwhelming start to his tenure.

"It is difficult to surprise other coaches, and certainly Jurgen Klopp. He is one of the best coaches of recent years," Xavi said.

"It will be a big challenge. They have to win. It is a big test."

The Netherlands have not won any of their last five meetings against Germany, with their last victory coming in a Euro 2020 qualifier in September 2019 (4-2).

#1786. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

#1783. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.
